## Summary

Cursor Cloud Agents keep their transcripts only in Cursor's backend, so no local provider could see them and users got no histories. This adds `cursorcloud`, the first provider whose native store is a remote HTTP API. It reads the Cloud Agents API with the user's key, mirrors each agent under `.specstory/cursorcloud/` (ignored by its own `.gitignore`, because the mirror is unredacted), and renders one history per agent with one exchange per run. `watch` and `run` poll the API and follow live run streams over SSE; `run` opens cursor.com/agents and then watches.

Research behind the design: `specstory-cli/docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md`. Format and lifecycle: `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md`.

## Built and tested against

- Cloud Agents API `1.0.0` (v1 public beta plus legacy v0), live on 2026-10-13.
- Manually exercised on macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0) against real cloud agents in a throwaway repository. Linux and Windows were cross-compiled and vetted (`GOOS=windows` build and vet pass) but not exercised manually.

## Manual test table rows run

- `check cursorcloud`: location reported, no version line (the API exposes none); `-c` with a bad path fails naming it; missing or rejected key gives guidance.
- `sync`, `sync cursorcloud`, `sync -s <id>`, `sync -s <id> --print`: one file per agent; a second sync changes no bytes and rewrites no mirror files.
- `sync --debug-raw --log --debug`: `agent.json`, `conversation.json`, `usage.json` and one file per run under `.specstory/debug/<id>/`.
- `watch cursorcloud`: existing agents left alone at startup; live runs followed and saved as they stream.
- `run cursorcloud`: opens the dashboard and behaves as `watch` (hosted-agent substitution).
- `resume cursorcloud` of its own session: opens the agent's page and watches. Resume of another agent's session into `cursorcloud` refuses with a clear message.
- `resume claude --session bc-…`: the cloud session reconstructs into Claude Code with its history, from a directory with no git origin.
- `list`, `search`, `reindex`: cloud sessions attributed to the right project by origin URL with full searchable bodies.

## Enumeration artifacts and audit

Under `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/`: `testdata/tools.txt` (recorded and model-facing names with the mapping), `examples/versions.txt`, `examples/TOOL-AUDIT.md` (every rendered block graded, failures included), and the synced histories under `examples/history/`. Fixtures in `testdata/` are real captures, scrubbed of account identifiers.

## SPI and shared-code changes

- `GlobalSessionRef.OriginRepoURL`: a hosted agent records a repository, never a directory. Reindex resolves the project from it with the same `git_id` normalization, parses bodies through `spi.PathSessionReader`, and resume reads such sessions by path. Without this, cloud sessions were indexed metadata-only under `unknown`.
- Git-origin helpers moved from `pkg/utils` to `pkg/spi` (`GitOriginURL`, `NormalizeGitRemoteURL`, `FindGitRoot`) with `pkg/utils` delegating, so providers use the exact normalization the CLI hashes.
- `pkg/cmd/session_uri.go` accepts `bc-`-prefixed session ids.
- Config: `cursor_api_key` and `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` settings reach the provider through `cmd.ApplyProviderSettings`; the config wiring test gained an allowlist for non-command settings.
- `NEW-PROVIDER-GUIDE.md` now covers hosted agents: remote stores, polling watchers with the acceptance-case mapping, credential-based `Check`, provider settings, remote checkout paths, provider-owned stores under `.specstory/`, and the rules this provider surfaced. Every guide gap found during the build was reviewed one by one and folded in.

## Known limitations

- Full transcripts are retained by Cursor for 24 hours after a run; after that only the v0 conversation text remains, so histories of older runs are text only. Sync daily or keep `watch` running.
- `Model` is empty and per-message `Usage` is nil because the API exposes neither; both stay in `RawData`.
- Resume into `cursorcloud` from another agent is unsupported: creating a cloud conversation launches a paid run.
- The default mirror is per project, so `reindex` sees the current project's mirror plus any configured shared `cursorcloud_mirror_dir`.
- SpecStory Cloud needs an exact agent-name entry for `cursorcloud` on the sync side (`specstory-sync`), handled separately.

## Review

The code was reviewed file by file against the provider guide during the build. Copilot's first pass (eight findings) and the CodeQL alerts are addressed in 657a76e, its second pass (three findings) in f74478b, and its third (one thread plus five untreaded notes) in c4353b0; each thread carries its resolution, and the untreaded notes are answered in a PR comment. Two Copilot findings are closed without change: `ssh://git@host` remote normalization (#358), because the helper's output is hashed into the persisted `git_id`, and multi-repository agent attribution (#359), which needs an index-level change.

Two changes from that round reach beyond the provider:

- Config files the CLI creates are now mode `0600` instead of `0644`, because `cursor_api_key` can live in them. An existing user config (`~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`) is tightened to owner-only on load, so upgraded installs are covered too. Project configs are never chmodded, and Windows is untouched.
- `watch` and `run` now end with an error when the agent listing is refused permanently (rejected key, Privacy Mode) instead of polling forever; `sync` and `list` detect already-mirrored agents without a key.
- A new repo-root `.gitattributes` marks provider `testdata/` fixtures `-text`, so Git for Windows stops converting them to CRLF at checkout. The cursorcloud golden and SSE tests compare bytes and failed on the Windows runner for that reason.

    40	// cloud-resumable blob for this session" and the server leaves session_data_size NULL.
    41	func (s *AgentChatSession) SessionDataJSON() string {
    42		if s == nil || s.SessionData == nil {
    43			return ""
    44		}
    45		data, err := json.Marshal(s.SessionData)
    46		if err != nil {
    47			slog.Warn("Failed to marshal SessionData for cloud sync", "sessionId", s.SessionID, "error", err)
    48			return ""
    49		}
    50		return string(data)
    51	}

    53	// SessionMetadata contains lightweight metadata about a session without full content
    54	// Used by ListAgentChatSessions for efficient session listing
    55	type SessionMetadata struct {
    56		SessionID string `json:"session_id" csv:"session_id"` // Stable and unique identifier for the session
    57		CreatedAt string `json:"created_at" csv:"created_at"` // Stable ISO 8601 timestamp when session was created
    58		Slug      string `json:"slug" csv:"slug"`             // Stable human-readable session name/slug
    59		Name      string `json:"name" csv:"name"`             // Human-readable description of the session (may be empty if not available)
    60	}

    62	// GlobalSessionRef is a lightweight, project-discovering reference to a single
    63	// native session, returned by Provider.ListAllAgentChatSessions.
    64	//
    65	// Unlike the project-scoped ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is NOT
    66	// an input here: each ref carries the originating working directory (read from inside
    67	// the session) so the caller — the `specstory reindex` command — can resolve project
    68	// identity with utils.ComputeProjectID. The project is discovered, not supplied.
    69	//
    70	// It is intentionally metadata-only (no full SessionData parse); reindex re-fetches
    71	// full data per ref via GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID) when it needs the
    72	// conversation body. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
    73	type GlobalSessionRef struct {
    74		SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
    75		CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
    76		Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
    77		Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
    78		NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
    79		OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
    80	
    81		// OriginRepoURL is the git remote URL of the repository the session worked on,
    82		// for a hosted agent that records a repository but never a local directory.
    83		// When OriginCwd is empty, reindex derives the project from this URL with the
    84		// same normalization and hash as a project's git_id, and parses the session's
    85		// body through spi.PathSessionReader. Leave it empty when OriginCwd is known.
    86		OriginRepoURL string
    87	
    88		// Fingerprint is the provider's own freshness token for the session, for a
    89		// store where NativePath is shared by every session (one SQLite database):
    90		// that file's size and mtime move whenever any session changes, so a
    91		// fingerprint taken from it would re-read every session on each reindex.
    92		// Nil means reindex fingerprints NativePath itself.
    93		Fingerprint *SessionFingerprint
    94	}
    95	
    96	// SessionFingerprint is a pair of values that change whenever a session's
    97	// content does. Reindex compares them to the pair it stored when it last
    98	// indexed the session; their meaning is the provider's (a row count and the
    99	// newest write time, say), not a file's size and mtime.
   100	type SessionFingerprint struct {
   101		Size  int64
   102		Mtime int64
   103	}

   105	// ScanReporter accumulates a provider's enumeration progress (sessions found) so the CLI can
   106	// render a live "scanning" display. It is safe for concurrent use and safe to call on a nil
   107	// receiver (a no-op), so providers can report unconditionally.

   111	
   112	// Add records that n more sessions have been found. Files that yield no session (warmup-only or
   113	// sidechain-only transcripts) are deliberately not counted, so the running total reflects real
   114	// sessions rather than raw files.

1	     1	# New Provider Guide
2	     2	
3	     3	This guide is for anyone, human or agent, adding support for a new coding agent to the SpecStory CLI. It tells you what a complete provider contains, the standards a submission is held to, and how it will be exercised before release, so your pull request lands with as few needed changes as possible.
4	     4	
5	     5	The service provider interface (SPI) is documented in [pkg/spi/provider.go](pkg/spi/provider.go). Read the doc comments on `spi.Provider` and the optional capabilities below it first. A provider must implement `spi.Provider`; it may also implement either or both optional interfaces.
6	     6	
7	     7	The unified session data format is [pkg/spi/schema/types.go](pkg/spi/schema/types.go), explained in [docs/SPI-SESSION-DATA-SCHEMA.md](docs/SPI-SESSION-DATA-SCHEMA.md).
8	     8	
9	     9	Once you've followed this guide and developed a provider, you can submit it for inclusion in the SpecStory CLI. Contributions of providers are welcomed! This guide defines the submission requirements. [docs/NEW-PROVIDER-REVIEW.md](docs/NEW-PROVIDER-REVIEW.md) supplements it with guidance for reviewers on evaluating evidence, prioritizing findings, and reporting readiness.
10	    10	
11	    11	## Before you write any provider code
12	    12	
13	    13	### Understand a provider's responsibilities and how a provider works
14	    14	
15	    15	A provider is the part of the SpecStory CLI that knows how to work with one specific coding agent. Each agent stores conversations (sessions) in its own location and format. The provider finds those sessions and translates them into SpecStory's shared session format, preserving the conversation, tool calls and results, and available metadata.
16	    16	
17	    17	A provider has four main responsibilities:
18	    18	
19	    19	- **Find the agent and its sessions.** Check the installation, discover sessions, and identify which project each session belongs to.
20	    20	- **Read and translate sessions.** Parse the agent's stored data, retain the raw transcript, and format its tool activity for readable output.
21	    21	- **Follow an active session.** Launch the agent for `run`, or observe it for `watch`, and report new or updated sessions as the agent writes them. Finish delivering updates before shutting down.
22	    22	- **Support resuming conversations.** Launch the agent with a selected local session and, where supported, convert SpecStory's shared format back into a native session the agent can resume.
23	    23	
24	    24	The provider hands session data back to the CLI through the provider SPI. The CLI, not the providers, handles writing Markdown history, redaction, indexing, and SpecStory Cloud sync. For example, during `specstory run`, the specific coding agent writes its session, the provider detects and reads the session change, and the CLI renders and saves the updated markdown file.
25	    25	
26	    26	### Use exemplar providers as a starting point
27	    27	
28	    28	Every provider is judged by behavioral parity with the established siblings. Choose the closest one as a starting point for file organization and method shapes, adapting the layout to your agent's needs. No single provider is reference-grade for everything, so take each concern from the provider named for it:
29	    29	
30	    30	|                                                Concern                                                |                                              Copy from                                               |
31	    31	| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
32	    32	| Parsing a JSONL session store, per-record debug output, a watcher that reconciles on a bounded window | `pkg/providers/claudecode`                                                                           |
33	    33	| Tool rendering keyed to the agent's real inventory, `Check` with shared analytics, lifecycle logging  | `pkg/providers/musecode`, `pkg/providers/antigravitycli`                                             |
34	    34	| Watch-only startup with adoption of late-arriving directories                                         | `pkg/providers/musecode`                                                                             |
35	    35	| Reporting the agent's exit status without losing the last save                                        | `pkg/spi/exit.go` (its doc comment states the contract)                                              |
36	    36	| Bounded line reading                                                                                  | `pkg/spi/jsonl.go` (`spi.ReadRecordLine`); capped `bufio.Scanner` for sidecars: `pkg/providers/musecode` |
37	    37	| An IDE-backed (likely VSC) agent: workspace discovery, minting, launching                             | `pkg/providers/cursoride`, `pkg/providers/copilotide`, and the shared `pkg/providers/vscode` package |
38	    38	| Dealing with a SQLite session store                                                                   | `pkg/spi/sqlite.go` and `pkg/providers/cursoride`                                                    |
39	    39	| A remote or API-backed store: credential resolution, rate limiting, SSE streaming, a local mirror, and a polling watcher | `pkg/providers/cursorcloud`                                                                          |
40	    40	| The SpecStory CLI Software Factory's maintenance scripts                                              | `pkg/providers/claudecode/factory`, `pkg/providers/antigravitycli/factory`                           |
41	    41	
42	    42	### Learn the agent's native session store
43	    43	
44	    44	Install the agent, run it, and read what it writes as its sessions to disk, to a database, or exposes through its API; the stored sessions are the contract. Capture what you learn in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md` (the agent's short name in capitals, for example `MUSE-CODE-FORMAT.md`), placed **inside your provider package** next to the code it documents, in the style of [MUSE-CODE-FORMAT.md](pkg/providers/musecode/MUSE-CODE-FORMAT.md) and [ANTIGRAVITY-FORMAT.md](pkg/providers/antigravitycli/ANTIGRAVITY-FORMAT.md):
45	    45	
46	    46	- Store layout, record envelope, and the shape of every tool call and result you observed.
47	    47	- The write lifecycle: which file is the durable record, which files are transient (checkpoints, rolling "latest" files, locks), when each is written and deleted, and whether a transient file is shared across concurrent sessions. A session that is still in flight is expected to be invisible until the agent commits it.
48	    48	- For a hosted agent whose sessions live only in a vendor backend, the store is its API. Document the endpoints and response shapes, retention windows, rate limits, and the signal that a session changed, exactly as you would files and timestamps, and mirror what you read locally so that sync, reindex and debug output still work from local data.
49	    49	- How the agent records its version and the working directory.
50	    50	- How native resume works and which file the agent actually reads on resume.
51	    51	- The baseline agent version the provider targets, stated as the exact string the binary prints for `--version`.
52	    52	
53	    53	Leave out any notes about versions below your baseline; a brand new provider has no backwards compatibility requirement.
54	    54	
55	    55	### Enumerate the agent's real tools yourself
56	    56	
57	    57	Build `tools.txt` from the harness's own tool declaration where available, such as startup output, a stream init event, or an extension hook. Prefer that inventory over asking the model or inferring the list from tools used in a session. Record the agent version, operating system, relevant configuration, and enabled extensions alongside the inventory so its scope is clear.
58	    58	
59	    59	If no declaration is available, run the agent directly (not through `specstory run`) in a scratch directory and ask it:
60	    60	
61	    61	```text
62	    62	Hello <agent>, tell me all the tools you have access to. Write all the tool names to the file ./tools.txt.
63	    63	```
64	    64	
65	    65	Then run the agent directly in the scratch directory and prompt it to exercise the tools available in that environment:
66	    66	
67	    67	```text
68	    68	Please use each of the tools in ./tools.txt that is available in this environment, one-by-one, to show me how they work. Identify any tools you cannot exercise and explain why.
69	    69	```
70	    70	
71	    71	Some agents discover and load additional tools after startup. Include those in the inventory where the harness exposes them; when using the model fallback, also ask it to include tools it can discover or load through tool search.
72	    72	
73	    73	Keep `tools.txt` and a `versions.txt` containing the agent's version banner and the SpecStory CLI version in a scratch directory. After the session ends, save a copy of its native session files for that session there too, leaving the originals in the agent's store so `specstory sync` can read them. These artifacts document what the agent actually did: use them to build test fixtures, verify tool rendering, and prepare the audit and PR attachments described in [How your provider will be tested](#how-your-provider-will-be-tested).
74	    74	
75	    75	Three rules about the tool list:
76	    76	
77	    77	- Model answers and observed sessions may omit tools. Check them against the harness declaration where available, and add any observed tools missing from the inventory.
78	    78	- Strip any namespace prefix the model adds (`functions.`, `<agent>.`); session data records bare names, and those are what your provider matches.
79	    79	- If the harness records tool names that differ from the names the model sees, the recorded names are the inventory, since those are what your provider matches. Keep the model's inventory alongside with the mapping between the two, so the audit can show which model-facing tool each rendered block came from.
80	    80	
81	    81	The tool names in that file are the only tool renderings your provider should special-case. Renderers, classifier cases, argument-key aliases, and fallback branches must each trace to an observed tool record. A renderer for a tool that never fires is untestable code that reads as though it were verified behavior, and it may be deleted in review.
82	    82	
83	    83	Exercise every tool reasonably available in the tested environment. Platform-specific tools, disabled optional extensions, and tools requiring unavailable external accounts may remain unexercised with a documented reason. Keep them in the inventory and distinguish declared, enabled, and exercised tools in the audit. Do not invent bespoke renderers for unobserved payloads; retain generic rendering. Where an attempted call produces an error, capture it and verify failure rendering, without claiming that this verifies the success path.
84	    84	
85	    85	### Find out what the agent needs to resume a session
86	    86	
87	    87	Cross-agent resume works by flattening the conversation into ordered user/agent text turns, then writing those turns in the target agent's native session format. Everything the agent said, thought, or did becomes agent text, including rendered tool activity. This shared representation avoids having to translate one agent's tool protocol or thinking blocks into another's. See [the reconstruction model](docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md#reconstruction-model).
88	    88	
89	    89	Before writing the conversion code, find out which files and native structure the target needs to load and continue that flattened conversation. The goal is a valid native session carrying the shared text transcript, not recreation of every original native field.
90	    90	
91	    91	Use a disposable session in your scratch project:
92	    92	
93	    93	1. Tell the agent "the magic passphrase is PURPLE-ELEPHANT-42", then exit the agent.
94	    94	2. Reopen that session using the agent's own resume command and ask "What is the magic passphrase?" Check that it recalls the fact without you supplying it again.
95	    95	3. Back up the session's stored files. With the agent stopped, temporarily move one file aside, then repeat the resume test. Restore the backup before testing the next file. This helps identify which files are needed to recover the conversation.
96	    96	4. Build a minimal native session containing plain user/agent text turns in the required structure, then repeat the recall test and continue the conversation. Verify that the agent loads it cleanly and appends to that session. Record required fields, lifecycle markers, and any necessary compatibility defaults in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`.
97	    97	
98	    98	Your conversion code must produce the native structure needed to resume the flattened conversation. Missing source tool structures, thinking signatures, or historical model/usage metadata are expected consequences of flattening, not reasons to declare reconstruction unsupported. If you cannot produce a native session the target can resume using this approach, return `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported` from `ReconstructSession` and `false` from `SupportsReconstruction`, and document that resuming other agents' conversations in this agent is unsupported.
99	    99	
100	   100	## What a complete provider contains
101	   101	
102	   102	### Package and files
103	   103	
104	   104	The architecture is one-directional: 
105	   105	
106	   106	- `pkg/spi` defines the interfaces, the schema, and the shared helpers and imports no provider
107	   107	- every provider imports `pkg/spi`
108	   108	- `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go` imports every provider and is the only place that knows them all. 
109	   109	- Nothing else in the CLI imports a provider package directly.
110	   110	
111	   111	The package is `pkg/providers/<agent>`: the product's own name, lowercased, with the spaces removed. That is the whole rule for ten of the twelve, including `cursoride`, because Code, CLI, TUI and IDE are part of what those products call themselves. The IDE-backed providers end in `ide`, which Cursor IDE's own name already supplies and VS Code Copilot does not, so it becomes `copilotide`. Pi is `piagent`, the one place a bare product name was too slight to stand on its own. The following file layout is recommended, not mandatory; add, combine, or split files where that makes the provider easier to understand:
112	   112	
113	   113	|                                      File                                      |                                          Purpose                                           |
114	   114	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
115	   115	| `provider.go`                                                                  | The `Provider` struct, `NewProvider()`, `Check`, `DetectAgent`, session listing and lookup |
116	   116	| `agent_session.go`                                                             | Conversion from the native format to `schema.SessionData`                                  |
117	   117	| `jsonl_parser.go` (or `json_parser.go`, `transcript_parser.go`, `database.go`) | Native format decoding                                                                     |
118	   118	| `markdown_tools.go`                                                            | Per-tool `Summary` and `FormattedMarkdown` rendering                                       |
119	   119	| `watcher.go`                                                                   | fsnotify or polling watcher used by `run` and `watch`                                      |
120	   120	| `<agent>_exec.go`                                                              | Command line parsing, resume arguments, process launch, exit handling                      |
121	   121	| `path_utils.go`                                                                | Native store discovery and working directory encoding                                      |
122	   122	| `reconstruct.go`                                                               | `ReconstructSession`, `NativeSessionPath`, `SupportsReconstruction`                        |
123	   123	| `*_test.go`                                                                    | Tests alongside each source file                                                          |
124	   124	| `testdata/`                                                                    | Inputs consumed by automated tests and expected outputs those tests actually compare      |
125	   125	| `examples/`                                                                    | Captured examples, rendered histories, QA results and other human-review evidence          |
126	   126	| `factory/`                                                                     | Software factory scripts (see below)                                                       |
127	   127	
128	   128	Keep related logic together and avoid unnecessary file sprawl. Small helpers usually belong in the file whose concern they serve; a separate file is reasonable when it groups a distinct concern, such as debug output. File organization may differ from this example while still meeting the provider's behavioral and architectural requirements.
129	   129	
130	   130	Add `var _ spi.Provider = (*Provider)(nil)` so the compiler enforces the interface, and the same assertion for any optional interface you implement.
131	   131	
132	   132	### Separate test fixtures from examples
133	   133	
134	   134	Reserve `testdata/` for files that automated tests actually consume as inputs or compare as expected outputs. For each fixture or fixture set, identify the consuming test and the behavior it asserts. A file does not become test data merely because a test helper copies the directory containing it.
135	   135	
136	   136	Put captured examples, manual QA results, version banners, tool audits, and generated JSON or Markdown that no test compares in `examples/`, following [Pi's examples](pkg/providers/piagent/examples/). Keep native captures in `testdata/` when parser or rendering tests consume them; link from the examples to those fixtures rather than duplicating them. A generated `session-data.json` or rendered history belongs in `testdata/` only if an automated test actually compares it as a golden file. Do not add a superficial test just to justify keeping a review artifact there. This includes `tools.txt`: when the tool inventory sweep test reads it, it lives in `testdata/`; otherwise it is a review artifact in `examples/`.
137	   137	
138	   138	This distinction is required even when choosing a different source-file layout. Before submitting, audit every file under `testdata/` for an actual test consumer and move unused review artifacts to `examples/`. Update documentation and audit links after moving them.

140	   140	### Every SPI method, including the ones that are easy to miss
141	   141	
142	   142	Implement every method on `spi.Provider` in `pkg/spi/provider.go` (count them against the most recent version of the file). Beyond the obvious ones, review these carefully:
143	   143	
144	   144	- `ListAgentChatSessions` returns lightweight metadata without a full parse.
145	   145	- `ListAllAgentChatSessions` enumerates every session in the native store across all projects, reading the originating working directory from inside each session or, for a hosted agent that records a repository rather than a directory, its remote URL. This powers `specstory reindex`, `search`, and `resume`. A provider whose store is per project can enumerate only the stores it can locate from the current directory and its configuration, and says so in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`.
146	   146	- `ReconstructSession`, `NativeSessionPath`, and `SupportsReconstruction` implement cross-agent resume into your agent. `SupportsReconstruction` is a pure constant answer and must agree with the other two. `NativeSessionPath` only resolves the path; the CLI creates the directory and writes the file.
147	   147	- The `progress` callback on `GetAgentChatSessions` is invoked once per session file, including skipped and failed ones, so the progress bar reaches its total.
148	   148	- The optional capabilities are also defined in [pkg/spi/provider.go](pkg/spi/provider.go). `spi.PathSessionReader` (`GetAgentChatSessionByPath`) lets reindex open a session by its known path instead of searching by id. `spi.ProgressEnumerator` (`ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress`) adds live scan counts. Implement either, both, or neither; reindex falls back to the required methods when they are absent. Both are recommended for JSONL stores, and `spi.PathSessionReader` is required when sessions carry no working directory. JSONL stores can use `spi.ScanSessionsInParallel` for enumeration (it walks `*.jsonl` files only; other store kinds implement enumeration themselves).
149	   149	
150	   150	### Wiring outside the package
151	   151	
152	   152	- `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`: register under a short lowercase id (`muse`, `antigravity`, `droid`).
153	   153	- `pkg/config/config.go`: a `<id>_cmd` entry in the default config template, a `ProvidersConfig` field, a `GetProviderCmd` case with its doc comment updated, and rows in the config tests. `specstory run <id>` must honor it; `specstory check <id> -c` honors the flag only. **All three parts are required and none of them fails loudly on its own** — TOML accepts a key with no struct field, and `GetProviderCmd` returns `""` for an unknown id — so a partial wiring ships a config key that silently does nothing. Two tests enforce it: `config.TestProvidersConfigIsFullyWired` checks each `ProvidersConfig` field reaches both the template and a `GetProviderCmd` case, and `cmd.TestEveryRegisteredProviderHasACommandOverride` checks every registered provider id resolves to one.
154	   154	- A provider setting that is not a launch command (a credential, a store location) is a `ProvidersConfig` field with a commented example in the template, an entry in `nonCommandProviderSettings` in the config test so the wiring test knows it is deliberate, and a line in `cmd.ApplyProviderSettings` that hands it to a package-level setter in your provider (the pattern `cursoride.SetUserDataDirOverride` uses). An environment variable, where one exists, overrides the config file. A credential never appears in generated artifacts, debug output, logs, or analytics.
155	   155	- `pkg/cmd/session_tui_browser.go`: add an accent color in `colorForAgent` as a hex code (`#RRGGBB`), based on a color associated with the agent's own brand. Check it on both dark and light terminal backgrounds and adjust the shade if needed for legibility. The maintainer may replace it.
156	   156	- `pkg/skills/agents.go`: a row when the agent supports agent skills (it has a project or global skills directory). Its `Name` is the public `npx skills` canonical id, not the provider id.
157	   157	- `README.md` in this directory: the intro sentence, the Agent Support table row, the `[providers]` example block, the Configuration Options row, and the Debug Raw Mode provider list. Write a prose paragraph only if the provider behaves differently from wrapping a terminal process.
158	   158	- `../README.md` at the monorepo root: the ASCII diagram line, the Installation table row (leave the Min Version to the maintainer), the lead-in sentence, and a `specstory run <id>` example.
159	   159	- `changelog.md`: an entry under a placeholder heading such as `## Unreleased`. Use the fixed announcement sentence from the previous provider's entry, listing every previously released provider, followed by a sentence on resume in each direction. State a version floor as the version you tested; the maintainer replaces it with the release-day version and moves your entry under the release heading. Do not also add it under an existing version, and do not add an "Improvements" section for a provider that has never shipped.
160	   160	- Providers whose `run` does not hand the terminal to an agent (IDEs, hosted agents): the per-save line during `run` is printed by the CLI and keyed to the registry id in `main.go`, so add yours there. IDE providers only: the restart note after `resume` is keyed the same way in `pkg/cmd/resume.go`.

162	   162	### Naming layers
163	   163	
164	   164	Five identifiers exist and they are not the same string:
165	   165	
166	   166	|                                         Identifier                                         |                                                    Convention                                                     |     Example      |
167	   167	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
168	   168	| Package name                                                                               | `<agent>`                                                                                                         | `antigravitycli` |
169	   169	| Registry id (CLI argument, `<id>_cmd`, statistics, index, check-event `provider` property) | short lowercase agent name                                                                                        | `deepseek`       |
170	   170	| `ProviderInfo.ID` in session data                                                          | the registry id, for every provider from Muse Code onward                                                         | `muse`           |
171	   171	| `Name()` and `ProviderInfo.Name`                                                           | the product's own name and casing; also the `agent_provider` analytics property and the telemetry agent attribute | `DeepSeek TUI`   |
172	   172	| Skills registry `Name` in `pkg/skills/agents.go`                                           | the public `npx skills` canonical id                                                                              | `claude-code`    |

174	   174	Go identifiers follow the brand's casing (`DeepSeekCmd`, not `DeepseekCmd`).
175	   175
