178	   178	## Rules that will otherwise get your submission changed
179	   179	
180	   180	These are the changes reviewers make most often. Each one is a real review finding from a past provider.
181	   181	
182	   182	### Reuse the shared helpers in pkg/spi
183	   183	
184	   184	Every helper below replaced copies that had drifted apart across providers. Do not reimplement them.
185	   185	
186	   186	- Use `schema.CurrentSchemaVersion` and the shared `schema.ContentTypeText` / `schema.ContentTypeThinking` constants when constructing `SessionData`, rather than repeating their string values. Native record fields and code-fence language labels follow their own formats.
187	   187	- `spi.CodeFence` for every fenced block, sized past any backtick run in the content. Never write a literal triple backtick, and never backslash-escape backticks.
188	   188	- `spi.ReadRecordLine` with `spi.MaxRecordLineSize` for every JSONL session file. It is the only correct way to cap a record: a cap applied after `bufio.Reader.ReadString` returns has already allocated the oversized record it exists to prevent. A capped `bufio.Scanner` is still right for sidecar and index files, where losing the remainder of the file is acceptable.
189	   189	- `spi.CapRunes` for truncation. Never slice a string by bytes.
190	   190	- Compare a sentinel error with `errors.Is` and match an error type with `errors.As`. Never `err == io.EOF` or `err.(*exec.ExitError)`: a wrapped error fails both, and wrapping gets added later by someone who has no reason to look for a bare comparison.
191	   191	- `spi.LanguageFromPath`, `spi.RenderGenericJSON`, `spi.TodoSymbol`, `spi.FormatDiffBlock`, `spi.StringValue`, `spi.NormalizeToolName` for tool rendering.
192	   192	- `spi.LookPathForCheck` for binary lookup, `spi.ClassifyCheckError` for lookup/storage errors, and `spi.ClassifyCheckExecutionError` for probe failures after the binary was found. Populate `CheckResult.ErrorType` with the same `spi.CheckError*` value sent to analytics; leave it empty on success. Empty `--version` output on a successful run is a success reported as `"unknown"`, not a failure (`spi.CheckErrorNoOutput` is a legacy shape).
193	   193	- `analytics.CheckAttempt` populated once per `Check`, with the event emitted by `analytics.TrackCheckSuccess` or `analytics.TrackCheckFailure`. No inline `analytics.TrackEvent` calls in a provider.
194	   194	- `spi.SplitCommandLine` for custom commands; `spi.EnsureResumeArgs` when the agent resumes via a subcommand, or `spi.EnsureResumeFlagArgs` when it uses a flag.
195	   195	- `spi.AgentExitError` to report a non-zero agent exit. Never call `os.Exit` inside a provider; it skips the final session save (the reason is in `pkg/spi/exit.go`).
196	   196	- `spi.GetDebugDir` for debug output paths. See [Native debug output](#native-debug-output) for the provider's export responsibilities; the CLI writes `session-data.json` itself.
197	   197	- `spi.NormalizePath` and `spi.ExtractShellPathHints` for path hints; `spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean` for local path comparison; `spi.FileURIToPath` for any `file://` URI.
198	   198	- `spi.GitOriginURL`, `spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL` and `spi.FindGitRoot` when a session is matched to a project by repository rather than by directory. They are the normalization the CLI hashes into `git_id`, so a provider that normalized URLs its own way would attribute sessions to a different project than the rest of the CLI.
199	   199	- `spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage`, `spi.GenerateReadableName`, and `spi.ReadableTitleFromSessionData` for slugs, names, and titles. If the agent records its own title or summary for a session, prefer it for `Name` and fall back to the shared generator.
200	   200	- `spi.PrepareTurns`, `spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot`, `spi.ReconstructRole`, `spi.RFC3339Millis`, `spi.ResumedSessionTitle` in `ReconstructSession`.
201	   201	- `spi.NewFSWatcher` to create every fsnotify watcher, in production code and tests alike. Never call `fsnotify.NewWatcher` or `fsnotify.NewBufferedWatcher` directly; see [The watcher](#the-watcher) for why.
202	   202	- `spi.WatchWindowDays`, `spi.WatchWindowCutoff`, `spi.DateDirWithinWatchWindow` when watched paths can grow without limit and the store layout supports a rolling date window. A fixed set of directory watches does not need a rolling window merely because the number of session files grows.
203	   203	- `spi.DeliverSession` for synchronous callback delivery with panic recovery. If using `spi.DispatchSession` for asynchronous delivery, track and join every callback before shutdown.
204	   204	- SQLite stores: open every read handle as `file:<path>?mode=ro&` plus `spi.BusyTimeoutPragma`. The `file:` scheme is required; the driver ignores `mode=` on a bare path and opens read-write-create. Call `spi.EnsureWALMode` once at watcher startup, never on a read path.
205	   205	
206	   206	Providers must never import `pkg/utils`, `pkg/session`, or `pkg/cloud` (the import graph cycles through the registry), nor `pkg/telemetry` (layering).
207	   207	
208	   208	### Honest data over convenient data
209	   209	
210	   210	- `CheckResult.Version` is the version string the probe printed. It is empty when no version probe is possible (an IDE store, a hosted agent), and the CLI then omits the version line; it is the literal `"unknown"` when the binary ran but printed nothing. Never any other label.
211	   211	- `ProviderInfo.Version` is the agent's version when the native data records it, otherwise the literal `"unknown"`. The model name is not a substitute; it belongs on each agent message's `Model` field, and it is the real model, never a placeholder such as an automatic-mode label.
212	   212	- `SessionData.WorkspaceRoot` is never empty: the workspace the agent stated, then the caller's project path, then the process working directory as a documented last resort. These fallbacks support path normalization and rendering; they are not evidence that the session belongs to the caller's project.
213	   213	- `GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd` records the session's originating working directory. Leave it empty when the origin cannot be determined; do not fill it from a rendering fallback. Global enumeration still returns the session, and the CLI assigns the `"unknown"` project ID. The literal `"unknown"` belongs in neither `OriginCwd` nor `WorkspaceRoot`. A session that records a repository but no directory leaves `OriginCwd` empty and sets `OriginRepoURL`; reindex attributes it to the project with that origin by the same `git_id` normalization. A provider whose sessions carry no cwd must implement `spi.PathSessionReader`, because reindex and resume read such sessions by path.
214	   214	- Never infer project membership from the paths that tools touched; one read of `~/.gitconfig` would attach the session to every project under the home directory. Session-to-project matching uses containment of stated paths, never a rendering fallback or a guessed common ancestor.
215	   215	- `GetAgentChatSession` returns `nil, nil` for not found. Errors are for real failures.
216	   216	- A by-id lookup on a global store must still check that the session belongs to the requested project, or one project's conversation will be written into another's history.
217	   217	- On an IDE store the same session can appear under several matching workspace entries, and an empty copy can come first; mark an id as seen only after the content check, and keep an empty copy only as a fallback.
218	   218	- `AgentChatSession.RawData` carries the native transcript on every session you return, whether or not debug output is enabled; SpecStory Cloud stores it. Build it from the records you already parsed, never by reading the file a second time: a session being written grows between the two reads, so the raw transcript would describe turns the converted session never saw, and during `run` that happens on nearly every save. `RawData` contains the accepted native records from the same parsing snapshot; malformed or oversized records skipped during parsing are excluded.
219	   219	- `Usage` carries only the token fields the native data distinguishes; a session total is not an input count, so leave it nil with a why-comment rather than guess. A token kind not already in `schema.Usage` is a shared change to ask for.
220	   220	- Timestamps come from the record, never from `time.Now()` in a parse or render path, are consistent across every code path, and are RFC 3339 parseable.
221	   221	
222	   222	### Comments explain why, and stay true
223	   223	
224	   224	- Every non-obvious line carries a "why" comment. Restating the code is noise.
225	   225	- Comments are self-contained. Do not reference other providers ("Claude Code uses X here"), plan documents, decision numbers, or the history of how the code came to be.
226	   226	- Magic values carry their provenance ("as observed in sessions written by version 3.12").
227	   227	- A comment that contradicts its code will be treated as a bug.
228	   228	- Every exported identifier, in particular each SPI method, carries a Go doc comment consistent with the siblings.
229	   229	
230	   230	### Parsing
231	   231	
232	   232	- For JSONL session files, read each record with `spi.ReadRecordLine(reader, spi.MaxRecordLineSize)`. It bounds allocation as the record is read and reports an oversized record instead of returning it, so one bad record degrades to one bad record rather than an aborted file. Log the skip at Warn with the file and line and carry on. Sidecar and index files may use a `bufio.Scanner` capped at `spi.MaxRecordLineSize`, mapping `ErrTooLong` to a clear error.
233	   233	- When a record holds `json.RawMessage`, unmarshal from a copy of the line (`scanner.Text()`, never `scanner.Bytes()`); the scanner reuses its buffer.
234	   234	- A record that fails to parse is skipped, never silently: log at Warn with the file and line ("Skipping corrupted JSONL line" is the established message shape).
235	   235	- Preserve the agent's native ordering and branch-selection semantics. Use sequence numbers where provided, parent links for tree formats, and file order where the native format defines it. Test supported out-of-order cases and branch selection where applicable.
236	   236	- Identify tool-result records using the native format's result markers or envelope; an unfamiliar record is not automatically a tool result. A recognized tool result with an unfamiliar payload type degrades to a generic result instead of vanishing. Pair results to calls using the native correlation fields, preferring an explicit call id; use tool type or first-in-first-out only where the native format makes that pairing unambiguous. When a call is re-serialized on every state update, merge the records field by field and take its result only from a record the native format marks as final, since an in-progress record may carry a provisional result that the final one replaces. Test a call that was interrupted before its final record.
237	   237	- The parser's kind switch enumerates every record kind observed in real data, rendering it or naming it as known-nothing-to-render with the reason, so the default "unknown kind" log fires only for genuinely new kinds.
238	   238	- Preserve unsupported native content in `RawData` when its record is accepted, and document what is omitted from normalized data and Markdown in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`. Preserve meaningful conversation text where the shared schema can represent it faithfully. Reserve "known-nothing-to-render" for records with no conversational content to display; an unfamiliar role or missing tool-call pairing is not sufficient reason to discard meaningful content.
239	   239	- Scan and watch only the durable session file; never read a scratch file the agent rewrites in place.
240	   240	
241	   241	### Native debug output
242	   242	
243	   243	`--debug-raw` helps provider authors, reviewers, and future maintainers inspect what the agent actually stored, compare it with SpecStory's interpretation, and diagnose missing content or format changes. The provider saves readable native input alongside the normalized `session-data.json` written by the CLI. Populating `AgentChatSession.RawData` does not create these native debug files; exporting them is a separate provider responsibility.
244	   244	
245	   245	- Honor `debugRaw` in single-session and bulk reads, live `run`/`watch` updates, and optional by-path reads. Write under `spi.GetDebugDir(sessionID)`, which defaults to `.specstory/debug/<session-id>/` and respects `--debug-dir`. When the flag is false, this export creates no files.
246	   246	- For JSONL, write one pretty-printed file per accepted native record, numbered from `1.json`, `2.json`, etc. in sequenced source order. For JSON or database stores, write pretty-printed session objects or individual records with native identifiers. Preserve native fields and envelopes, including unfamiliar fields, relevant headers, and sidecar data used during conversion. Keep source identity and ordering clear enough to trace an output back to its input.
247	   247	- Generate the export from the same input snapshot used for conversion. Do not reread a changing transcript or substitute a reduced typed structure that drops unknown fields or records omitted from Markdown. Those details may be exactly what a maintainer needs to understand a format change. Malformed or oversized records may be skipped under the parsing rules above, with the required diagnostic.
248	   248	- Refresh the export when the session changes, removing obsolete provider-owned files so earlier records cannot masquerade as current data. Preserve CLI-owned files such as `session-data.json`. Log export failures with the session and path, without aborting session processing.
249	   249	- Test that a field the provider does not recognize still appears in the saved native JSON, and that `--debug-dir` puts the files in the requested directory. For numbered files, export a session with three records, then export the same session with only two: the old `3.json` must be removed. Check that live updates produce current debug files, and that not using the debug flag creates none. Keep test output isolated with `spi.SetDebugBaseDir(t.TempDir())` and reset the override during cleanup.
250	   250	
251	   251	### The watcher
252	   252	
253	   253	- For a file-based store, filesystem events through fsnotify are the primary change signal. Supplement them with bounded periodic reconciliation to recover missed events, including writes to files that were not yet watched. Keep reconciliation scoped to the relevant session paths and prune idle watches where applicable. For a remote store, a bounded poll of the agent's session list is the primary signal, and the same acceptance cases apply with "file written" read as "session updated".
254	   254	- File-based stores: create the watcher with `spi.NewFSWatcher`, never `fsnotify.NewWatcher`. On Windows, fsnotify has a single I/O goroutine that both delivers `Events`/`Errors` and services `Add`/`Remove`. `Add` and `Remove` wait for that goroutine to reply, and the goroutine waits for someone to receive the event or error it is sending. Nearly every watcher calls `Add` or `Remove` from the same loop that drains those channels (adopting a new session directory, re-scoping to an ancestor, pruning idle watches). With a plain fsnotify watcher, that loop deadlocks as soon as another event or error is ready. The watcher then hangs silently and no more sessions are saved. `spi.NewFSWatcher` returns an ordinary `*fsnotify.Watcher` whose channels are relayed through a lossless, ordered queue, so the I/O goroutine is never blocked. Keep `select` on `watcher.Events` and `watcher.Errors` exactly as with fsnotify. The same applies to tests that construct a watcher and call `Add`/`Remove` without draining its channels. macOS and Linux never show this failure, so only the Windows CI job will catch it, and only intermittently.
255	   255	- Establish a startup baseline without emitting existing, unchanged sessions merely because the watcher started. New or changed sessions after startup count as activity, including changes made while the initial watches and baseline are being established. Each watcher architecture must establish this boundary reliably so initialization neither republishes history nor absorbs new activity into the baseline.
256	   256	- If a session directory appears after startup, walk it once and adopt the files that arrived inside it, even when they carry old preserved modification times. Arrival is new activity. A pre-existing directory discovered later during the initial scan is part of the baseline, not a late arrival.
257	   257	- Never let the watcher silently disable itself. File-based stores: if the agent's directory does not exist yet, watch the nearest existing ancestor and wait.
258	   258	- File-based stores: when the store is keyed by project, watch only this project's subtree, never every project's directory. Walks and watches stop at the session directory; a session's own subdirectories (tool outputs, subagent logs) are neither watched nor walked.
259	   259	- File-based stores: watch every path the agent writes session content to, including asynchronous sidecar files. Change detection uses an on-disk signature (size and modification time) of every file the session spans, not a parsed field that a title-only rename would not touch.
260	   260	- A debounced burst is re-processed once after the burst ends; the burst's last write is often the completed response.
261	   261	- Deliver callbacks in order (one worker) or synchronously; contain panics in the consumer callback; close the race between `Stop` and in-flight work under one lock. Track goroutines with `wg.Go`, never `wg.Add(1)` paired with `defer wg.Done()`.
262	   262	- Make the watcher restartable: create the context per start, not in `init()`.
263	   263	- File-based stores: file descriptor usage stays bounded over a months-long watch. When watched paths can grow without limit, bound them with a strategy appropriate to the store layout: for date-organized stores, use `spi.WatchWindow*`, prune watches at rollover, and re-watch a dormant file when its modification time moves. A single-directory watch or another fixed set of watches already satisfies the descriptor bound and does not need a rolling date window.
264	   264	- The command layer fingerprints every delivered session and suppresses unchanged parses; add no content-equality guard of your own.
265	   265	
266	   266	The startup boundary and shutdown behavior must satisfy these acceptance cases:
267	   267	
268	   268	| Scenario                                                                                             | Expected behavior                                                |
269	   269	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
270	   270	| A session file is written just before startup and remains unchanged                                  | No emission merely because the watcher starts                    |
271	   271	| A session file changes while the initial watches and baseline are being established                  | The update is eventually emitted, not absorbed into the baseline |
272	   272	| A directory appears after startup containing session files with old preserved modification times     | The arriving sessions are adopted and emitted                    |
273	   273	| A pre-existing directory is discovered later during the initial scan, with no activity since startup | No emission merely because discovery happened later              |
274	   274	| Shutdown occurs with no new or pending session activity                                              | No emission merely because the watcher stops                     |
275	   275	
276	   276	Shutdown must still drain pending updates before returning. These cases define which activity counts, without prescribing a particular snapshot, watch-registration, or timestamp strategy.
277	   277	
278	   278	For a remote store the cases map as follows:
279	   279	
280	   280	| Guide case                                                            | Remote-store equivalent                                                                                                                      |
281	   281	| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
282	   282	| A session file is written just before startup and remains unchanged   | The session is listed at the baseline poll and its change marker (such as `updatedAt`) is unchanged afterwards                               |
283	   283	| A session file changes while the baseline is being established        | The baseline records the marker it listed, not what the session became, so a change during the baseline's own fetches is seen by the next poll |
284	   284	| A directory appears after startup with old preserved modification times | A session first listed after the baseline counts as new activity whatever its creation time                                                 |
285	   285	| A pre-existing directory is discovered later during the initial scan  | A session on a later page of the baseline listing is part of the baseline                                                                   |
286	   286	| Shutdown with no new or pending activity                              | Stop joins every poll and stream goroutine; an undelivered burst is drained and nothing else is emitted                                      |
287	   287	
288	   288	Two further rules apply only to a remote store:
289	   289	
290	   290	- Stay inside the vendor's documented rate limit with a client-side limiter shared by every caller in the process, honor `429` and `Retry-After`, and retry transport errors with bounded backoff. The poll interval is a trade-off between freshness and quota; state the chosen interval and why in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`.
291	   291	- A live stream that disconnects is resumed from the last event received, never restarted from a blank state. Events replayed on attach or resume are not new activity: count only events stamped after the watcher started, and deduplicate repeats when the vendor's event ids are not unique.
292	   292	
293	   293	### Run and exec
294	   294	
295	   295	- Honor the custom command from `-c` and `<id>_cmd`; parse it with `spi.SplitCommandLine`.
296	   296	- When a resume id is requested it wins over any id pinned in the configured command. Use `spi.EnsureResumeFlagArgs` for flag-style resume (`--resume <id>`), passing the agent's supported flag names. It replaces pinned ids, fills bare or empty flags, and preserves the caller's slice.
297	   297	- Stop the watcher and join in-flight saves before returning the agent's exit status.
298	   298	- For an IDE provider, `run` opens the project directory with the IDE's own CLI, canonicalizing the path first, prints install guidance if that CLI is missing, waits for the IDE to create the workspace, and then watches until Ctrl-C. No silent fallback to opening the app on its home screen.
299	   299	- For a hosted agent, `run` opens the agent's web surface with the configured `<id>_cmd` (default: the operating system's URL opener), prints one line saying so, and then behaves as `watch` until Ctrl-C. Say so in the README row and in the config template comment for `<id>_cmd`.
300	   300	
301	   301	### Resume into your agent
302	   302	
303	   303	- Call `spi.PrepareTurns` to obtain the shared ordered user/agent text turns, then serialize them into your agent's native session format. The flattening policy lives in `pkg/spi/reconstruct.go`; providers must not implement their own conversion policy.
304	   304	- User text remains user text. Agent speech and thinking become ordinary agent text, and tool activity becomes agent text through `Tool.Summary` and `Tool.FormattedMarkdown`. Do not reconstruct native tool calls, tool-result relationships, or signed thinking blocks. Preserve the prepared text and its order, adapting message grouping only where the target format requires it.
305	   305	- Produce the native envelope, fresh identifiers, ordering links, and lifecycle markers the target needs to load and continue the flattened conversation cleanly. Include required end-of-run or end-of-session records so the agent shows no crash or unclean-stop warning. Verify that subsequent turns extend the reconstructed session.
306	   306	- Source model, usage, and path-hint metadata are intentionally dropped by the shared flattening step. Source system and environment scaffolding must not be replayed; the target supplies its own runtime context. Document any additional provider-specific preservation limits in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`.
307	   307	- Do not invent model, usage, or version metadata to make reconstructed sessions resemble native ones. Omit unavailable fields where supported; otherwise use accepted empty or neutral values. A realistic compatibility placeholder is permitted only when testing establishes that the target cannot load or continue the session without it and rejects omission or neutral values. Document the requirement and test evidence in `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`; an existing provider's placeholder is not evidence that yours needs one. For example, if a native message requires a model field that is absent from `spi.Turn`, write `"model": ""` if the loader accepts it, rather than attributing imported turns to the model configured for future turns.
308	   308	- Carry a provenance back-link (`specstorySourceSessionId`) in the native metadata.
309	   309	- Keep user-identifying data (account labels, auth metadata) out of reconstructed files.
310	   310	- Your parser must exclude your agent's own slash-command and system scaffolding from user turns; the shared resume filter strips only Claude Code's markers.
311	   311	- If the agent cannot resume from reconstructed data, return `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`, return `false` from `SupportsReconstruction`, and say so in the changelog. Such a provider is offered as a resume target only for its own local sessions.
312	   312	
313	   313	### Rendering
314	   314	
315	   315	- Tool inputs render as labeled lines (`Path:`, `Command:`), not JSON blocks. JSON is the last-resort generic fallback only, pretty-printed in a `json` fence. Maps and slices are JSON-marshaled, never formatted with `%v`.
316	   316	- Edits render as `diff` fences. Files render in a fence tagged by extension. Shell output renders in a `text` fence with control bytes sanitized. Web search results render as a linked list.
317	   317	- A JSON tool result (an answer envelope, a diff array, a subagent record) is parsed into the idiomatic markdown for its kind and folded into the call block; the result renderer then returns empty so the raw JSON does not also appear.
318	   318	- A failed call renders the agent's error text; the error branch takes priority over the success formatter for every tool. Agents record failure in more than one shape, and a non-zero shell exit is often a distinct result rather than an error, so capture at least one deliberately failed call per tool family and render every failure shape you observe, showing the exit code with the output.
319	   319	- User-entered shell commands render as user messages clearly labeled "User ran a shell command", with the command and its recorded output/status. They do not need an assistant tool call to pair with. Preserve them as historical activity in flattened resume text, even if the native agent excludes them from its own model context.
320	   320	- Thinking content is captured and rendered once, in place. Narration and tool blocks appear in the order the agent recorded them; an invocation the agent re-serializes on every state update renders once.
321	   321	- Completeness beats brevity: the full system prompt, the full file content. Results are capped with a visible marker; inputs are not.
322	   322	- Never nest `<details>` blocks; the wrapper is owned by `pkg/session`.
323	   323	- Tool type reflects the target: workspace documents are `read`, `write`, `search`; shell is `shell`; todo lists are `task`; agent-state stores (memory, goals, cron, skills, subagents) are `generic`; a URL fetch is `read`. An unenumerated tool must still render, typed `unknown`, never dropped. Every bespoke renderer keeps a generic degradation path so no input is ever lost.
324	   324	- Strip framework boilerplate the agent injects for the model ("Created At:" headers, "proactively run terminal commands" instructions) but never alter real content; scope any whitespace cleanup to the result type where the noise was observed.
325	   325	- A malformed element (a todo item that is not an object) is skipped, never rendered as a placeholder row.
326	   326	- Output is deterministic: never iterate a map into output; sort with one comparator. A second sync with no agent activity must change no bytes.
327	   327	
328	   328	### Check and analytics
329	   329	
330	   330	- `Check` resolves the binary with `spi.LookPathForCheck`, probes `--version` capturing stdout and stderr, reports `"unknown"` when the binary prints nothing, and emits exactly one event per outcome through `analytics.TrackCheckSuccess` or `analytics.TrackCheckFailure`.
331	   331	- Every failed `CheckResult` includes an `ErrorType` and a helpful `ErrorMessage`. Reserve `spi.CheckErrorNotFound` for an absent binary or IDE store: the CLI presents it as informational, except for a missing custom `-c` command. Permission errors, failed probes, and invalid stores remain failures. Use `spi.ClassifyCheckExecutionError` after a successful lookup so a broken interpreter/loader is not mistaken for an uninstalled agent.
332	   332	- The failure message names the command actually run, including a custom one.
333	   333	- Providers emit no other analytics. Hidden flags get none.
334	   334	- IDE providers probe the store, not a binary, preserve filesystem errors for classification, and emit one check event per outcome. Verify the store is readable; merely resolving its path or obtaining a lazy database handle does not prove it is usable.
335	   335	- Hosted agents resolve a credential instead of a binary and probe an identity endpoint. A missing credential is `spi.CheckErrorNotFound` with guidance on where to create it and how to supply it, a rejected credential is `spi.CheckErrorPermissionDenied`, and any other probe failure is `spi.CheckErrorUnknown`. Name the endpoint probed in `CheckAttempt.VersionFlag`, never the credential's value. If the provider also takes `<id>_cmd`, resolve a custom one with `spi.LookPathForCheck` first, so a bad `-c` still fails naming that path.
336	   336	
337	   337	### Logging
338	   338	
339	   339	- Call `log/slog` directly; no package-local logger wrapper or adapter. Use `log.UserMessage` and `log.UserWarn` for the guidance `DetectAgent` prints when nothing is found. The only other permitted terminal output is an IDE provider's "waiting for the IDE to open this project" line. No `fmt.Print` anywhere else in a provider.
340	   340	- `Check`, `ExecAgentAndWatch`, and `WatchAgent` log at Info on start, each transition, and exit. Missing lifecycle logging is a defect, because `--log` is how problems get diagnosed.
341	   341	- Routine, repeating states (file events, waiting for the agent) log at Debug. Warn is for data loss the run survives. Error is for a unit of work that failed, logged once.
342	   342	- Structured keys are camelCase (`error`, `path`, `sessionId`, `projectPath`, `command`, `exitCode`); messages are prefixed with the method name (`Check:`, `WatchAgent:`) for SPI entry points.
343	   343	- Never swallow an error with `_ :=` when the failure would otherwise be silent to the user.
344	   344	
345	   345	### What counts as a security concern
346	   346	
347	   347	The CLI reads files the user's own agents wrote, on the user's own machine, as the user. Data already on the local disk is not a threat to that machine, and anything able to place a file or a symlink inside the agent's store already has the access it would be trying to obtain. So a symlink under the agent's store is read as the user pointing at their own files, a relocated project or sessions shared between checkouts, not as an escape to defend against.
348	   348	
349	   349	The boundary worth defending runs between this machine and everything outside it:
350	   350	
351	   351	- What leaves: SpecStory Cloud stores `RawData` and generated markdown. Redaction is central in `pkg/redact`, applied by `pkg/session` and `pkg/cloud`; providers do not touch it. A secret reaching the cloud is worse than a rare local rendering break.
352	   352	- What arrives: session content is untrusted input. It is parsed defensively, never executed, never interpolated into a shell command, and never followed off the machine, and a malformed or hostile record degrades to a skipped record rather than an aborted file or an unbounded allocation.
353	   353	- User-identifying data (account labels, auth metadata) stays out of generated artifacts and reconstructed files.
354	   354	
355	   355	Local-only symlink and path checks in the providers exist to keep enumeration inside the store it is scanning, so one project's sessions never land in another's history. They are correctness controls, not security controls, and a bot review that rates one as a vulnerability is rating it too high.
356	   356	
357	   357	### Cross-platform
358	   358	
359	   359	The CLI runs on macOS, Linux (including WSL), and native Windows, and CI runs the full test suite on Windows.
360	   360	
361	   361	- Paths from session data are handled by shape (leading `/` or a drive letter), never with `filepath.IsAbs`, `filepath.Join`, `filepath.Abs`, `filepath.Rel`, or `filepath.Clean`, because a session written on one OS is rendered on another. An absolute-path check accepts both shapes; a `/`-only check rejects every native Windows path.
362	   362	- Local paths use `os.UserHomeDir()` and `filepath.Join`. Your cwd-to-store-directory encoder reproduces the agent's own algorithm, including its symlink resolution. Only a path naming a directory on this machine is canonicalized, and only at the boundary where it enters: the process working directory, a `--project-path` override, the local destination handed to `ReconstructSession`. Anything recorded in session data is never canonicalized, absolutized, or case-folded, because it may name a directory on another machine.
363	   363	- A hosted agent works in a remote checkout with a fixed root (such as `/workspace`). Map that root onto the local project path for path hints and render recorded paths relative to it. Never treat a remote path as a local one: it is not canonicalized, checked for existence, or read.
364	   364	- On macOS and Windows the filesystem is case-insensitive but case-preserving, so one directory has a single on-disk spelling and many spellings that work. `cd ~/source` into a directory really named `Source` and every local path in the process carries the wrong case, while the agent records the on-disk one. Canonicalize the local path once, at the boundary, with `spi.GetCanonicalPath`, which walks the path a component at a time and reads each parent directory to recover the real case. Then compare exactly.
365	   365	- `filepath.EvalSymlinks` does **not** correct case. It resolves symlinks, returns the wrong-case path unchanged, and reports `nil` error while doing it, which is what makes it such a convincing wrong answer. `filepath.Abs` and `filepath.Clean` do not correct case either. None of the three is a substitute for `spi.GetCanonicalPath`.
366	   366	- Never repair a case mismatch by comparing case-insensitively, whether with `strings.EqualFold` or by lowering both sides. A recorded path can come from a case-sensitive machine, where two spellings are two different directories, and folding case silently merges them. Fix the local root's spelling instead, so the exact comparison is correct everywhere. The single exception is hashing a path into a stable identity, where there is no directory to read and the hash must not vary with spelling: fold there, gate it on the host filesystem, and expect to invalidate every id already persisted.
367	   367	- IDE-style providers branch on `runtime.GOOS` for `Library/Application Support`, `.config`, and `%APPDATA%`, check `spi.IsWSL()` in the Linux branch and read the Windows side with `spi.FindWindowsAppDataPathFromWSL` first, and honor `--user-data-dir`. Any URI written to an IDE store goes through `vscode.WorkspaceURIMap` or `vscode.PathToFileURI`.
368	   368	- A raw JSONL scan for a path also matches the backslash-escaped form; a Windows cwd inside JSON is written as `C:\\Users`.
369	   369	- No `pgrep`, `sh -c`, `/bin/...`, or `USER`. Username comes from `os/user.Current()`; process detection on Windows uses `tasklist`, checking that the image name echoes back because it exits 0 even when nothing matched.
370	   370	- Before opening the PR run `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` and `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./...` (the prefix goes on both commands).
371	   371	
372	   372	### Tests
373	   373	
374	   374	- Test complicated logic and combinatorial scenarios, not constants. A test that asserts `Name()` returns its own literal will be deleted.
375	   375	- A test must actually create the condition it is named for. One that cannot, and settles for exercising the ordinary path instead, is deleted or made real: it reads as coverage of the hard case while proving nothing about it, which is worse than its absence because it stops anyone else writing the real one. If the condition is too expensive to build, that is a reason to lower the threshold until it is affordable, not to keep the test.
376	   376	- Table-driven with `t.Run(tt.name, ...)` where there is a matrix of cases; a single integration test may stay standalone.
377	   377	- Fixtures are raw shapes captured from real sessions, so the tests encode what the agent actually writes.
378	   378	- Check [fixture placement](#separate-test-fixtures-from-examples): each `testdata/` fixture has an automated consumer and asserted purpose; review-only artifacts belong in `examples/`.
379	   379	- A regression test must fail when the fix is backed out. Prove it before you commit it. When a fix adds a guard, the test also proves the guarded path still works for the legitimate case.
380	   380	- An exhaustive test that walks the agent's real tool inventory and asserts the expected type per name is not tautological; it guards against omission.
381	   381	- Exercise bespoke renderers through the actual dispatch path using captured invocations. Verify that the recorded tool name, after normalization, selects the intended renderer; directly testing the renderer function cannot catch an unreachable dispatch key.
382	   382	- Each acceptance case in [The watcher](#the-watcher) gets its own test, covering the startup boundary, late-directory adoption, and shutdown behavior.
383	   383	- Reconstruction tests verify that the native output preserves the prepared user text, agent text, thinking text, and rendered tool activity in order, with the required native structure and lifecycle markers. Expect plain conversation text rather than native tool or thinking blocks; the shared flattening policy itself is tested in `pkg/spi`.
384	   384	- Tests for a shared helper live in `pkg/spi` next to the helper, not in the provider.
385	   385	- When changing shared parsing, rendering, or identity behavior, verify the affected existing providers. Compare regenerated Markdown from representative captured sessions for rendering changes. State any consequences for saved Markdown, indexes, or persisted identifiers.
386	   386	- Test hygiene: `testutil.SetHome` (never `t.Setenv("HOME", ...)` alone; it does not fake `%APPDATA%`, so IDE-style providers point at a fake install through their user-data-dir override), `testutil.JSONString` when a real path goes into a JSON fixture, `testutil.EqualPaths` after URI round-trips, `t.TempDir()` (a symlink on macOS and an 8.3 name on Windows, so compare canonical to canonical), `t.Chdir`, never a `"file://" + path` splice, deadline polling rather than fixed sleeps for file events, and expected values built with `filepath.Join` or `filepath.FromSlash`. Windows-shaped table rows run Windows behavior on macOS.
387	   387	- A test that creates a fixture and reads it back with the same spelling can never catch a case-sensitivity bug, because both sides carry the same mistake. When the provider matches recorded paths against a local root, add one case that reaches the project through a differently-cased spelling of a real directory and asserts the sessions still resolve. Skip it where the filesystem is case-sensitive rather than asserting the wrong thing there.
388	   388	- Any test that enables debug output first calls `spi.SetDebugBaseDir(t.TempDir())` so nothing is written into the package directory.
389	   389	- Keep test accommodations small: package-level root-path or limit overrides and parameterized internal helpers are acceptable when needed to exercise meaningful behavior affordably. Avoid elaborate interfaces or abstraction layers whose only purpose is testing.
390	   390	
391	   391	### Dependencies and new files
392	   392	
393	   393	- No new dependencies without asking first, with the reason. Prefer the standard library.
394	   394	- Keep provider-specific test helpers in `*_test.go` files alongside the tests. Test helpers shared across packages belong under `internal/`, such as `internal/testutil`.
395	   395	- No planning documents in `docs/`. Keep `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md` as a description of what is, not a plan.
396	   396	- `.specstory/history` is committed in this repository; do not add `.specstory/` to any `.gitignore`, and do not add ignore entries for directories that do not exist. A provider may keep raw native data under `.specstory/<provider>/` only when it writes that directory's own `.gitignore` excluding its contents, because redaction applies to markdown and cloud sync, never to native data.
397	   397	
398	   398	## How your provider will be tested
399	   399	
400	   400	Reviewers exercise every command against the real agent, at the version shipping that week, from a scratch project, invoking the freshly built `./specstory`. Test these yourself before submitting and say in the PR which you ran and on which operating systems.
401	   401	
402	   402	|                                         Command                                         |                                                                                                                                  What must be true                                                                                                                                  |
403	   403	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
404	   404	| `./specstory check <id>`                                                                | Version and location reported; `-c` with a bad path fails with guidance naming that path; the success hint advertises a command that works                                                                                                                                          |
405	   405	| `./specstory sync`, `sync <id>`, `sync -s <session-id>`, `sync -s <session-id> --print` | One markdown file per non-empty session; a second sync with no agent activity reports every session as up to date and changes no bytes; from a directory with no sessions, `sync <id>` prints your provider's own guidance and exits 0                                              |
406	   406	| `./specstory sync --debug-raw --log --debug`                                            | `.specstory/debug/<session-id>/` holds pretty-printed per-record `N.json` files (JSONL agents) or one raw file, plus `session-data.json`; `debug.log` reconstructs every decision and contains no `schema validation:` warnings                                                     |
407	   407	| `./specstory run <id>`                                                                  | The agent takes the terminal with no interleaved output; markdown appears after the first turn and grows; the CLI exits with the agent's status and the last turn is saved even on a non-zero exit; this also works from a project the agent has never seen, and with `--debug-raw` |
408	   408	| `./specstory watch <id>`                                                                | Existing sessions are left alone; the first new update prints and is saved; works when started in a project the agent has never seen                                                                                                                                                |
409	   409	| `./specstory resume <id>` (same agent)                                                  | The agent opens with prior turns visible and answers a question about them; the same native file grows; the same markdown file updates                                                                                                                                              |
410	   410	| `./specstory resume claude` from your agent's session                                   | The reconstructed session opens in Claude Code with the migration note first and every user prompt present; no command or system scaffolding is replayed. Use a source session with plain turns, thinking, at least one tool call, and a slash command                              |
411	   411	| `./specstory resume <id>` from a Claude Code session                                    | Your agent opens the reconstructed session with the prior conversation, answers a question about it, shows no warning about the session file, and appends to that same file rather than starting a fresh session                                                                    |
412	   412	| `./specstory list <id>`, `search`, `reindex`                                            | Every synced session is listed with the same slug as its filename; reindex counts your sessions across all projects and attributes them to the right project                                                                                                                        |
413	   413	
414	   414	Also run `sync`, `list`, and `watch` from the scratch project reached through a symlink and from a path containing a space and an underscore; each must find the same sessions as the canonical path.
415	   415	
416	   416	A hosted agent substitutes three rows: `run <id>` opens the agent's web surface, prints that it did, and then behaves as `watch`; `resume <id>` of its own session opens that session's page and watches; and `resume <id>` from another agent's session refuses with a message saying why reconstruction is unsupported. Record all three in the PR. For a provider that reports no version (IDE or hosted), the `check` row is satisfied when the location is reported and the version line is omitted.
417	   417	
418	   418	Check the integration cases that ordinary provider commands can miss: bare `run` must select the default described by `run --help` and the README; `watch` must return an error if no watcher can start; and `watch <id> --output-dir <dir>` must save to the requested directory while still discovering the current project's sessions. `sync -s <session-id> --print` must print the session without writing history files.
419	   419	
420	   420	For both cross-agent resume directions, use a source session containing user and agent text, thinking, tool activity, and a slash command. Verify that the prepared conversation text survives in order, including thinking and rendered tool activity as ordinary agent text, with the migration note first and no source command or system scaffolding replayed. Ask the target about prior conversation content to establish that it loaded the context, then verify that it continues the same reconstructed session cleanly. Native tool replay and historical model/usage preservation are not part of this contract.
421	   421	
422	   422	Then run the tool enumeration session described above through `./specstory sync --log --debug --debug-raw` and audit the markdown block by block against the raw data. Reconcile native tool invocations with rendered blocks: each invocation appears once, in the native order, with its own results; repeated state snapshots are not additional invocations, and quoted transcripts must not produce phantom tool blocks. Grade every tool-use block as formatted (all important data present and pleasantly presented), partial (formatted but missing important elements), raw (raw JSON or unformatted output), or missing, in a table with the tool name, markdown line, grade, data file, data line, and a comment. Exercised tools should grade as formatted, including failed calls. List unexercised tools separately with the reason for each coverage gap; do not give them a rendering grade. State the tested version, OS, configuration, and extensions, and distinguish declared, enabled, and exercised tools. Attach `tools.txt`, `versions.txt`, the synced history file, and the audit table to the PR.
423	   423	
424	   424	## Software factory affordances
425	   425	
426	   426	The SpecStory provider factory watches each agent's release channel and audits new versions. A provider enrolls by shipping executable bash scripts under `pkg/providers/<agent>/factory/` (the package directory, not the registry id). Model them on `pkg/providers/claudecode/factory/` and `pkg/providers/antigravitycli/factory/`, including the header comment that records the channel decision, what was rejected and why, and the contract paragraph. These scripts run unattended in CI on every merge, so they are read as untrusted code: nothing is piped to a shell except the vendor's own pinned installer, and nothing reads outside the named credential.
427	   427	
428	   428	- `latest-version` (required): prints the current released version to stdout and exits 0. A non-zero exit means sensor failure, never "no change"; an empty extraction becomes a non-zero exit with a diagnosis on stderr. Output is opaque, byte-compared day to day, so it carries no build counters, shas, or dates unless they are part of the string the binary prints for `--version`, and the header states which dist-tag or release train is tracked. Accepted channels are an npm `latest` dist-tag, a GitHub `releases/latest` redirect, the vendor's installer script read as a manifest, or, for a hosted agent, the version field of the vendor's published API specification; never the GitHub API or any tool needing auth. Every curl carries `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 --retry 2 --retry-delay 2`. Runs with no credentials.
429	   429	- `install <version>` (required when the agent has a headless mode): takes the first line of `latest-version`'s output verbatim, installs exactly that version under `$HOME` at `$HOME/.local/bin/<binary>`, disables the agent's self-update where it has one, prints the version read back from the binary as the only stdout line (installer chatter goes to stderr), and exits non-zero on any mismatch.
430	   430	- `list-tools` (required when the agent has a headless mode): runs `$HOME/.local/bin/<binary>` explicitly with self-update disabled and prints the tool inventory one name per line, spelled as the agent records tool names in its session data. Prefer the harness's own declaration (a stream init event, an extension hook) over asking the model; if a model run is unavoidable it must authenticate through one environment variable named in the header, with a fail-fast check when it is unset, and any settings file the agent needs is seeded under `$HOME` inside the script. Passes the agent's isolation flags so user configuration cannot leak in, is bounded by a timeout or the harness's own turn limit, leaves its diagnostics in the working directory, and exits non-zero rather than printing an empty or partial list.
431	   431	
432	   432	Test them the way the factory runs them, under an isolated home directory (`timeout` is GNU coreutils; on macOS install it with Homebrew):
433	   433	
434	   434	```zsh
435	   435	env -i HOME="$(mktemp -d)" PATH="$PATH" timeout 120 bash pkg/providers/<package>/factory/latest-version
436	   436	H=$(mktemp -d); V=$(env -i HOME="$(mktemp -d)" PATH="$PATH" bash pkg/providers/<package>/factory/latest-version | head -1)
437	   437	env -i HOME="$H" PATH="$PATH" bash pkg/providers/<package>/factory/install "$V"
438	   438	for n in 1 2; do ( cd "$(mktemp -d)" && env -i HOME="$H" PATH="$PATH" <VAR>="${<VAR>:-}" bash pkg/providers/<package>/factory/list-tools > "/tmp/reading-$n" ); done
439	   439	diff <(sort -u /tmp/reading-1) <(sort -u /tmp/reading-2) && echo "readings agree"
440	   440	```
441	   441	
442	   442	Also run each script's negative case (an unreachable channel, a bogus version, the credential unset); every one must exit non-zero rather than print an empty reading. IDE providers ship `latest-version` only and say why in its header; so does a hosted agent, whose header also states that nothing installs locally and that the tool inventory comes from a recorded run rather than an unattended one. A terminal agent with no credential-free headless mode may do the same, with the reason recorded.

444	   444	## Submitting the pull request
445	   445	
446	   446	- Open the pull request against `dev`, never `main`. If you are contributing from a fork, enable "Allow edits by maintainers".
447	   447	- Merge `dev` into your branch first and resolve conflicts, so the diff contains only your provider.
448	   448	- In the description state: the agent version you built against and tested on, the operating systems you tested on, which rows of the test table you ran, the attached enumeration artifacts and audit, any SPI or shared-code changes and why, and known limitations (for example, resume into the agent unsupported and why).
449	   449	- Expect the GitHub Copilot reviewer to comment. Its findings are triaged, not obeyed; fix the real ones and comment on and resolve the rest.
450	   450	- Expect the maintainer to review by pushing commits directly onto your branch rather than requesting changes, and to cut the release.

452	   452	## Self-review checklist
453	   453	
454	   454	- [ ] Package named for the product, lowercased and unspaced
455	   455	- [ ] Necessary files only, similar to the recommended files list, no file sprawl
456	   456	- [ ] `var _ spi.Provider` assertion present
457	   457	- [ ] Every SPI method implemented, including `ListAllAgentChatSessions` and the three reconstruction methods
458	   458	- [ ] Tests cover behavioral contracts and capability consistency, including agreement between `SupportsReconstruction` and the reconstruction methods; trivial constant-return methods do not need standalone tests
459	   459	- [ ] Provider registered in `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`
460	   460	- [ ] Config wired: `<id>_cmd` in template, struct, switch, doc comment, and test rows, with both wiring tests passing
461	   461	- [ ] Brand-specific TUI color added
462	   462	- [ ] Both READMEs updated
463	   463	- [ ] Draft changelog.md entry added
464	   464	- [ ] `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`, in the provider package, written from the current release with the write lifecycle and baseline version, no legacy notes
465	   465	- [ ] `tools.txt` from the agent itself, prefixes stripped, declaration preferred over self-report
466	   466	- [ ] Bespoke renderers and classifier cases use names from `tools.txt` and are backed by observed tool records
467	   467	- [ ] Tool audit identifies the tested environment and distinguishes declared, enabled, and exercised tools
468	   468	- [ ] Unexercised tools have documented reasons, and observed failed calls have verified error rendering
469	   469	- [ ] Tool inventory sweep test exists

    51	// Check verifies a key is configured and accepted by probing GET /v1/me.
    52	// There is no binary; customCommand is the dashboard opener used by run, so a
    53	// custom one is checked for existence.
    54	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
    55		attempt := analytics.CheckAttempt{
    56			Provider:      ProviderID,
    57			CustomCommand: customCommand != "",
    58			CommandPath:   customCommand,
    59			VersionFlag:   checkProbe,
    60		}
    61		slog.Info("Check: verifying Cursor Cloud Agent access", "customCommand", customCommand != "")
    62	
    63		fail := func(errorType, detail, message string) spi.CheckResult {
    64			slog.Info("Check: failed", "errorType", errorType, "error", detail)
    65			analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, detail, "")
    66			return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, ErrorType: errorType, ErrorMessage: message}
    67		}
    68	
    69		if customCommand != "" {
    70			opener := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
    71			if len(opener) == 0 {
    72				return fail(spi.CheckErrorNotFound, "empty command", "The custom command is empty.\n")
    73			}
    74			resolved, err := spi.LookPathForCheck(opener[0])
    75			if err != nil {
    76				errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckError(err)
    77				return fail(errorType, err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(
    78					"Could not find the dashboard opener: %s\n\n"+
    79						"• cursorcloud_cmd (or -c) is the command run cursorcloud uses to open https://cursor.com/agents.\n"+
    80						"• Check the path, or remove the setting to use the system URL opener.\n", opener[0]))
    81			}
    82			attempt.ResolvedPath = resolved
    83		}
    84	
    85		key, source := resolveAPIKey()
    86		if key == "" {
    87			return fail(spi.CheckErrorNotFound, "no API key configured", missingKeyMessage())
    88		}
    89	
    90		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), jsonTimeout)
    91		defer cancel()
    92		me, err := newAPIClient(key).me(ctx)
    93		if err != nil {
    94			var ae *apiError
    95			if errors.As(err, &ae) && (ae.Status == http.StatusUnauthorized || ae.Status == http.StatusForbidden) {
    96				return fail(spi.CheckErrorPermissionDenied, err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(
    97					"Cursor rejected the API key from %s (HTTP %d).\n\n"+
    98						"• Create a new key at %s and set %s or cursor_api_key under [providers] in specstory.toml.\n",
    99					source, ae.Status, apiKeyPage, apiKeyEnvVar))
   100			}

   102				"Could not reach the Cursor Cloud Agents API (%s).\n\nError: %v\n\n"+

   105		}

   108		// the version line, as it does for IDE providers.
   109		location := defaultAPIBaseURL
   110		if me.KeyLabel != "" {
   111			location = fmt.Sprintf("%s (key %q)", defaultAPIBaseURL, me.KeyLabel)
   112		}
   113		slog.Info("Check: succeeded", "keySource", source, "location", location)
   114		analytics.TrackCheckSuccess(attempt, "")
   115		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Location: location}
   116	}

   118	func missingKeyMessage() string {
   119		return fmt.Sprintf("No Cursor API key is configured.\n\n"+
   120			"• Create a key at %s\n"+
   121			"• Then set the %s environment variable, or add it to specstory.toml:\n\n"+

   124	
   125	// DetectAgent reports whether this project has cloud agents: the project has
   126	// a git origin, and either the mirror already holds an agent for that
   127	// repository or, when a key is configured, the first page of the agent list
   128	// names one. The mirror is consulted without a key so that histories already
   129	// mirrored can still be synced after the key is unset or rotated.
   130	func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
   131		key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
   132		origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
   133		found := false
   134		if origin != "" {
   135			m, _ := mirrorFor(projectPath)
   136			found = len(m.matchingSnapshots(origin)) > 0
   137			if !found && key != "" {
   138				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), jsonTimeout)
   139				agents, err := newAPIClient(key).listAgents(ctx, 1)
   140				cancel()
   141				if err != nil {
   142					slog.Warn("DetectAgent: listing cloud agents failed", "error", err)
   143				}
   144				for _, record := range agents {
   145					if agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin) {
   146						found = true
   147						break
   148					}
   149				}
   150			}
   151		}
   152	
   153		if helpOutput && !found {
   154			log.UserWarn("\nNo Cursor Cloud Agents were found for this project.\n")
   155			switch {
   156			case key == "":
   157				log.UserMessage("%s\n", missingKeyMessage())
   158			case origin == "":
   159				log.UserMessage("Cloud agents are matched to a project by its git origin URL, and this directory has no origin remote.\n")
   160				log.UserMessage("Run SpecStory from a clone of the repository the cloud agents worked on.\n\n")
   161			default:
   162				log.UserMessage("Cloud agents are matched to a project by repository URL. None of your agents worked on %s.\n", origin)
   163				log.UserMessage("Launch one at https://cursor.com/agents for this repository, then sync again.\n\n")
   164			}
   165		}
   166		return found
   167	}
   168	
   169	// GetAgentChatSessions refreshes the mirror for this project's agents, then
   170	// builds every matching session from the mirror. Without a key or network it
   171	// still returns what the mirror already holds.
   172	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
   173		origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
   174		if origin == "" {
   175			slog.Debug("GetAgentChatSessions: project has no git origin; no cloud agents can match", "projectPath", projectPath)
   176			return []spi.AgentChatSession{}, nil
   177		}
   178		m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
   179		refreshProject(context.Background(), m, projectLocal, origin)
   180	
   181		// Progress is reported once per mirrored agent, including those that fail
   182		// to convert, so the bar reaches its total. An agent whose refresh failed
   183		// is still read from whatever the mirror held before.
   184		snapshots := m.matchingSnapshots(origin)
   185		var sessions []spi.AgentChatSession
   186		for i, snap := range snapshots {
   187			if session := convertSnapshot(snap, projectPath, debugRaw); session != nil {
   188				sessions = append(sessions, *session)
   189			}
   190			if progress != nil {
   191				progress(i+1, len(snapshots))
   192			}
   193		}
   194		return sessions, nil
   195	}
   196	
   197	// refreshProject refreshes every agent for origin. Failures are logged per
   198	// agent; the mirror still serves the rest.
   199	func refreshProject(ctx context.Context, m mirror, projectLocal bool, origin string) {
   200		key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
   201		if key == "" {
   202			slog.Debug("No Cursor API key; reading the mirror only")
   203			return
   204		}
   205		client := newAPIClient(key)
   206		agents, err := client.listAgents(ctx, 0)
   207		if err != nil {
   208			slog.Warn("Failed to list cloud agents; using the mirror only", "error", err)
   209			return
   210		}
   211		for _, record := range agents {
   212			if !agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin) {
   213				continue
   214			}
   215			if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
   216				slog.Error("Failed to create mirror", "path", m.root, "error", err)
   217				return
   218			}
   219			if err := m.refreshAgent(ctx, client, record, refreshOptions{now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
   220				slog.Error("Failed to refresh cloud agent", "agentId", record.agent.ID, "error", err)
   221			}
   222		}
   223	}
   224	
   225	// matchingSnapshots loads every mirrored agent whose repository is origin.
   226	func (m mirror) matchingSnapshots(origin string) []*agentSnapshot {
   227		dirs, err := m.agentDirs()
   228		if err != nil {
   229			slog.Warn("Failed to read mirror", "path", m.root, "error", err)
   230			return nil
   231		}
   232		var snaps []*agentSnapshot
   233		for _, dir := range dirs {
   234			snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(dir)
   235			if err != nil {
   236				slog.Warn("Skipping unreadable mirrored agent", "path", dir, "error", err)
   237				continue
   238			}
   239			if snap != nil && agentMatchesOrigin(snap.agent, origin) {
   240				snaps = append(snaps, snap)
   241			}
   242		}
   243		return snaps
   244	}
   245	
   246	// GetAgentChatSession refreshes and returns one agent when it belongs to this
   247	// project, else nil. Membership is checked because the agent list is global
   248	// to the key: an id alone could name another repository's agent.
   249	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
   250		if !validAgentID(sessionID) {
   251			return nil, nil
   252		}
   253		origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
   254		if origin == "" {
   255			return nil, nil
   256		}
   257		m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
   258	
   259		if key, _ := resolveAPIKey(); key != "" {
   260			ctx := context.Background()
   261			client := newAPIClient(key)
   262			record, err := client.getAgent(ctx, sessionID)
   263			switch {
   264			case isNotFound(err):
   265				return nil, nil
   266			case err != nil:
   267				slog.Warn("GetAgentChatSession: fetch failed; using the mirror", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
   268			case !agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin):
   269				return nil, nil
   270			default:
   271				if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
   272					return nil, err
   273				}
   274				if err := m.refreshAgent(ctx, client, record, refreshOptions{now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
   275					slog.Error("GetAgentChatSession: refresh failed", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
   276				}
   277			}
   278		}
   279	
   280		snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(m.agentDir(sessionID))
   281		if err != nil {
   282			return nil, err
   283		}
   284		if snap == nil || !agentMatchesOrigin(snap.agent, origin) {
   285			return nil, nil
   286		}
   287		return convertSnapshot(snap, projectPath, debugRaw), nil
   288	}

   299	// convertSnapshot builds the session, its RawData and, when asked, the
   300	// native debug export, all from one snapshot.
   301	func convertSnapshot(snap *agentSnapshot, projectPath string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
   302		data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, workspaceRootFor(projectPath))
   303		if data == nil {
   304			slog.Debug("Skipping cloud agent with no recorded prompt yet", "agentId", snap.agent.ID)
   305			return nil
   306		}
   307		raw, err := buildRawData(snap)
   308		if err != nil {
   309			slog.Error("Failed to build raw data", "sessionId", snap.agent.ID, "error", err)
   310			return nil
   311		}
   312		if debugRaw {
   313			if err := writeDebugOutput(snap); err != nil {
   314				slog.Warn("Failed to write debug output", "sessionId", snap.agent.ID, "path", spi.GetDebugDir(snap.agent.ID), "error", err)
   315			}
   316		}
   317		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
   318			SessionID:   snap.agent.ID,
   319			CreatedAt:   snap.agent.CreatedAt,
   320			Slug:        data.Slug,
   321			SessionData: data,
   322			RawData:     raw,
   323		}
   324	}

   403	// stale ones (a run file from a longer earlier export) and leaves the
   404	// CLI-owned session-data.json alone.
   405	func ownsDebugFile(name string) bool {
   406		switch name {

   408			return true
   409		}
   410		return runDebugFileRe.MatchString(name)

   412	
   413	// writeDebugOutput exports the snapshot's native objects pretty-printed:
   414	// agent.json, conversation.json, usage.json and run-<n>-<runId>.json holding
   415	// the run object and its events, numbered in run order.
   416	func writeDebugOutput(snap *agentSnapshot) error {
   417		dir := spi.GetDebugDir(snap.agent.ID)
   418		if err := spi.PrepareDebugDir(dir, ownsDebugFile); err != nil {
   419			return err
   420		}
   421		write := func(name string, raw []byte) error {
   422			var pretty bytes.Buffer
   423			if err := json.Indent(&pretty, raw, "", "  "); err != nil {
   424				return fmt.Errorf("format debug file %s: %w", name, err)
   425			}
   426			path := filepath.Join(dir, name)
   427			if err := os.WriteFile(path, pretty.Bytes(), 0o644); err != nil {
   428				return fmt.Errorf("write debug file %s: %w", path, err)
   429			}
   430			return nil
   431		}
   432		if err := write("agent.json", snap.agentRaw); err != nil {
   433			return err
   434		}
   435		if len(snap.conversationRaw) > 0 {
   436			if err := write("conversation.json", snap.conversationRaw); err != nil {
   437				return err
   438			}
   439		}
   440		if len(snap.usageRaw) > 0 {
   441			if err := write("usage.json", snap.usageRaw); err != nil {
   442				return err
   443			}
   444		}
   445		for i, run := range snap.runs {
   446			events := run.events
   447			if events == nil {
   448				events = []sseEvent{}
   449			}
   450			raw, err := json.Marshal(rawRun{Run: run.runRaw, Events: events})
   451			if err != nil {
   452				return err
   453			}
   454			if err := write(fmt.Sprintf("run-%d-%s.json", i+1, run.run.ID), raw); err != nil {
   455				return err
   456			}
   457		}
   458		return nil
   459	}

   463	func noProjectOriginError(projectPath string) error {
   464		return fmt.Errorf("cursor cloud agents are matched by repository, and %s has no git origin remote", strings.TrimSpace(projectPath))

   174	func (c *apiClient) do(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client, build func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error)) (*http.Response, error) {

   381	// openStream opens a run's SSE stream. lastEventID, when set, resumes after
   382	// that event. The returned body cancels its request once no bytes arrive for
   383	// streamIdleTimeout, so a silently dropped connection surfaces as a read error
   384	// instead of hanging forever. A 410 maps to errStreamExpired.
   385	func (c *apiClient) openStream(ctx context.Context, agentID, runID, lastEventID string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
   386		streamCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
   387		path := "/v1/agents/" + url.PathEscape(agentID) + "/runs/" + url.PathEscape(runID) + "/stream"
   388		resp, err := c.do(streamCtx, c.streamHTTP, func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error) {
   389			req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, c.baseURL+path, nil)
   390			if err == nil {
   391				req.Header.Set("Accept", "text/event-stream")
   392				if lastEventID != "" {
   393					req.Header.Set("Last-Event-ID", lastEventID)
   394				}
   395			}
   396			return req, err
   397		})

   399			cancel()

   403			}

   405		}
   406		return newIdleReader(resp.Body, cancel, streamIdleTimeout), nil

   409	// idleReader cancels its request when no read has returned data for the idle
   410	// period. Cancelling the request context makes the blocked Read return.
   411	type idleReader struct {
   412		body   io.ReadCloser
   413		cancel context.CancelFunc
   414		timer  *time.Timer
   415		idle   time.Duration
   416	}
   417	
   418	func newIdleReader(body io.ReadCloser, cancel context.CancelFunc, idle time.Duration) *idleReader {
   419		return &idleReader{body: body, cancel: cancel, timer: time.AfterFunc(idle, cancel), idle: idle}
   420	}
   421	
   422	func (r *idleReader) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
   423		n, err := r.body.Read(p)
   424		if n > 0 {
   425			r.timer.Reset(r.idle)
   426		}
   427		return n, err
   428	}

   431		r.timer.Stop()
   432		r.cancel()

   434	}

    59		runs            []runSnapshot
