+### Notes on Cursor Cloud Agents
+
+Cursor Cloud Agents run in Cursor's backend, and their conversations are never written to your machine. The `cursorcloud` provider reads them from the [Cloud Agents API](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints) with your Cursor API key (create one at https://cursor.com/dashboard/api, then set `CURSOR_API_KEY` or `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]`). Agents are matched to the current project by repository: an agent belongs to the project when one of its repositories is the project's git `origin`. The provider keeps a local mirror of what it has read in `.specstory/cursorcloud/` (it writes its own `.gitignore` there, because the mirror holds unredacted transcripts); `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` moves it. A finished run's full transcript, including tool calls and output, is available from the API for 24 hours; after that only its text remains, so sync at least daily or keep `specstory watch` running. `specstory run cursorcloud` opens https://cursor.com/agents in your browser and then watches until interrupted with `ctrl-c`. Resuming another agent's session into a cloud agent is not supported, because that would launch a new paid run; cloud sessions can be resumed into local agents.
+
-Supported provider IDs are `cursoride`, `copilotide`, `copilotide-insiders`, `copilotide-vscodium` and `copilotide-vscodium-insiders`. If the override path doesn't exist, SpecStory warns and falls back to the standard location for your OS.
+Supported provider IDs are `cursoride`, `cursorcloud` (where the path is the location of its local API mirror), `copilotide`, `copilotide-insiders`, `copilotide-vscodium` and `copilotide-vscodium-insiders`. If the override path doesn't exist, SpecStory warns and falls back to the standard location for your OS. The exception is `cursorcloud`, whose path is a destination rather than an install: it is created on the first sync.

+# Where raw cloud agent transcripts are mirrored (default: .specstory/cursorcloud in the project)

-Claude Code, Codex CLI, Qwen Code, Factory Droid, Pi, Muse Code, OpenCode, and Grok Build use sequentially numbered JSON files in source order. Codex and Grok preserve native number precision and key order. Grok also exports the sidecars used for conversion and refreshes debug files even when its accepted records contain no rendered conversation. Gemini uses numbered per-message diagnostic objects. ## Most important improvements

1. **Log refresh progress (10, 8).** A first `sync` on a busy repo can sit silent for minutes because of the 3-second rate limit, and `--log` can't diagnose it either. This is the change users would notice most.
2. **Remove `pr_management` (37).** It's a classifier case with no captured record, which the guide says to delete. The generic `unknown` rendering still covers it.
3. **Stop re-parsing the whole mirror every poll (51).** `attachRunning` only needs run status, but it loads every events file each minute for the life of a `watch`.
4. **Resolve two attribution questions (31, 45).** Run-index-to-v0-turn mapping can shift if a run is missing, and repo matching is case-sensitive while GitHub isn't. Both are cases where history lands in the wrong place, which the review doc ranks above style issues. They're labeled ❓ because I couldn't confirm the API's behavior without a key.
5. **Small consistency fixes:** honor `--silent` in the exec lines (46), cap `Retry-After` (21), reconcile the project-config permission comment (70), and add the missing log in `fetchMissingStreams` (28).

## Tests

The suite is strong. Every remote watcher acceptance case has its own named test. Golden tests use real captures, and the debug test covers all four of the guide's requirements. Tool rendering goes through the real dispatch path with captured calls, and the API tests build real conditions (throttling, transport errors, an expired stream, an idle hang). I found nothing tautological or flaky; the watcher tests poll with deadlines rather than sleeping.

Worth adding or changing:
- **v0 fallback with a missing run (31):** a snapshot where run 2 of 3 is absent, asserting run 3's text isn't assigned to run 2. This would fail against today's code and pin whatever fix you choose.
- **Origin case mismatch (45):** if you decide to fold case in the match, add one table row to `TestAgentMatchesOrigin`.
- **Fold the duplicate URL test (58)** into `pkg/spi`.
- **`retryAfter` table test (21):** the seconds, HTTP-date, garbage and over-cap cases are combinatorial enough to justify one.

## Decision

**Ready to merge after small fixes, with nothing blocking.** Contract compliance, concurrency, credential handling and the shared-code changes are solid. Build, lint, tests, race runs and Windows CI are green on 117fa56. I'd fix items 1–3 before merge. Items 31 and 45 need a quick check against the live API, so they could merge as follow-up issues if you prefer. The real-agent rows rest on the PR's own testing on macOS; nobody has run them on Linux or Windows yet.

**Still needed before release, outside this PR:**
- The `cursorcloud` agent-name entry in specstory-sync.
- Replacing the version floor in the changelog on release day.
- Website docs.
- Factory enrollment of `latest-version`.
- Follow-ups #358 and #359, plus a new one for a shared `spi.ExpandHome` (44).

   125	// DetectAgent reports whether this project has cloud agents: the project has

   130	func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
   131		key, _ := resolveAPIKey()

   172	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
   173		origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
   174		if origin == "" {
   175			slog.Debug("GetAgentChatSessions: project has no git origin; no cloud agents can match", "projectPath", projectPath)
   176			return []spi.AgentChatSession{}, nil
   177		}
   178		m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
   179		refreshProject(context.Background(), m, projectLocal, origin)
   180	
   181		// Progress is reported once per mirrored agent, including those that fail
   182		// to convert, so the bar reaches its total. An agent whose refresh failed
   183		// is still read from whatever the mirror held before.
   184		snapshots := m.matchingSnapshots(origin)
   185		var sessions []spi.AgentChatSession
   186		for i, snap := range snapshots {
   187			if session := convertSnapshot(snap, projectPath, debugRaw); session != nil {
   188				sessions = append(sessions, *session)
   189			}
   190			if progress != nil {
   191				progress(i+1, len(snapshots))
   192			}
   193		}
   194		return sessions, nil
   195	}

   197	// refreshProject refreshes every agent for origin. Failures are logged per
   198	// agent; the mirror still serves the rest.
   199	func refreshProject(ctx context.Context, m mirror, projectLocal bool, origin string) {
   200		key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
   201		if key == "" {
   202			slog.Debug("No Cursor API key; reading the mirror only")
   203			return
   204		}
   205		client := newAPIClient(key)
   206		agents, err := client.listAgents(ctx, 0)
   207		if err != nil {
   208			slog.Warn("Failed to list cloud agents; using the mirror only", "error", err)
   209			return
   210		}
   211		for _, record := range agents {
   212			if !agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin) {
   213				continue
   214			}
   215			if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
   216				slog.Error("Failed to create mirror", "path", m.root, "error", err)
   217				return
   218			}
   219			if err := m.refreshAgent(ctx, client, record, refreshOptions{now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
   220				slog.Error("Failed to refresh cloud agent", "agentId", record.agent.ID, "error", err)
   221			}
   222		}
   223	}
   224	
   225	// matchingSnapshots loads every mirrored agent whose repository is origin.
   226	func (m mirror) matchingSnapshots(origin string) []*agentSnapshot {
   227		dirs, err := m.agentDirs()
   228		if err != nil {
   229			slog.Warn("Failed to read mirror", "path", m.root, "error", err)
   230			return nil
   231		}
   232		var snaps []*agentSnapshot
   233		for _, dir := range dirs {
   234			snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(dir)
   235			if err != nil {
   236				slog.Warn("Skipping unreadable mirrored agent", "path", dir, "error", err)
   237				continue
   238			}
   239			if snap != nil && agentMatchesOrigin(snap.agent, origin) {
   240				snaps = append(snaps, snap)
   241			}
   242		}
   243		return snaps
   244	}

   249	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
   250		if !validAgentID(sessionID) {
   251			return nil, nil
   252		}

   255			return nil, nil

   261			client := newAPIClient(key)

   263			switch {
   264			case isNotFound(err):
   265				return nil, nil
   266			case err != nil:
   267				slog.Warn("GetAgentChatSession: fetch failed; using the mirror", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
   268			case !agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin):
   269				return nil, nil
   270			default:
   271				if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
   272					return nil, err
   273				}
   274				if err := m.refreshAgent(ctx, client, record, refreshOptions{now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
   275					slog.Error("GetAgentChatSession: refresh failed", "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
   276				}
   277			}
   278		}

   281		if err != nil {
   282			return nil, err
   283		}

    68	// loadAgentSnapshot reads an agent directory. A directory without agent.json
    69	// is not an agent yet (a refresh writes agent.json last) and yields nil.
    70	func loadAgentSnapshot(dir string) (*agentSnapshot, error) {
    71		agentRaw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "agent.json"))
    72		if err != nil {
    73			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
    74				return nil, nil
    75			}
    76			return nil, err
    77		}
    78		record, err := decodeAgent(agentRaw)
    79		if err != nil {
    80			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", filepath.Join(dir, "agent.json"), err)
    81		}
    82		snap := &agentSnapshot{dir: dir, agentRaw: record.raw, agent: record.agent}
    83	
    84		if raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "conversation.json")); err == nil {
    85			var conv v0Conversation
    86			if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal(raw, &conv); jsonErr != nil {
    87				slog.Warn("Ignoring undecodable conversation", "path", filepath.Join(dir, "conversation.json"), "error", jsonErr)
    88			} else {
    89				snap.conversationRaw = raw
    90				snap.conversation = &conv
    91			}
    92		}
    93		if raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "usage.json")); err == nil && json.Valid(raw) {
    94			snap.usageRaw = raw
    95		}
    96	
    97		runsDir := filepath.Join(dir, "runs")
    98		entries, err := os.ReadDir(runsDir)
    99		if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   100			return nil, err
   101		}
   102		for _, entry := range entries {
   103			name := entry.Name()
   104			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
   105				continue
   106			}
   107			raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(runsDir, name))
   108			if err != nil {
   109				return nil, err
   110			}
   111			record, err := decodeRun(raw)
   112			if err != nil {
   113				slog.Warn("Skipping undecodable run", "path", filepath.Join(runsDir, name), "error", err)
   114				continue
   115			}
   116			events, err := readEventsFile(filepath.Join(runsDir, record.run.ID+".events.jsonl"))
   117			if err != nil {
   118				return nil, err
   119			}
   120			snap.runs = append(snap.runs, runSnapshot{runRaw: record.raw, run: record.run, events: events})
   121		}
   122		// One run is one exchange in creation order. The API lists runs newest
   123		// first; the id breaks ties so the order never depends on directory order.
   124		sort.SliceStable(snap.runs, func(i, j int) bool {
   125			a, b := snap.runs[i].run, snap.runs[j].run
   126			if a.CreatedAt != b.CreatedAt {
   127				return a.CreatedAt < b.CreatedAt
   128			}
   129			return a.ID < b.ID
   130		})
   131		return snap, nil
   132	}

   152	// readStoredAgent returns the mirrored agent object, or nil when absent.

   164	
   165	// ensureRoot creates the mirror root and, for a mirror inside the project,
   166	// the .gitignore that keeps raw transcripts out of commits.
   167	func (m mirror) ensureRoot(projectLocal bool) error {
   168		if err := os.MkdirAll(m.root, 0o755); err != nil {
   169			return err
   170		}
   171		if !projectLocal {
   172			return nil
   173		}
   174		path := filepath.Join(m.root, ".gitignore")
   175		if existing, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil && gitignoreExcludesAll(existing) {
   176			return nil
   177		}
   178		return writeFileAtomic(path, []byte(mirrorGitignore))
   179	}
   180	
   181	// gitignoreExcludesAll reports whether a .gitignore carries the bare "*" rule
   182	// the mirror relies on. A file that exists without it (edited, truncated) would
   183	// let git track raw transcripts, so ensureRoot rewrites it rather than trusting
   184	// its presence.
   185	func gitignoreExcludesAll(content []byte) bool {
   186		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(content), "\n") {
   187			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "*" {
   188				return true
   189			}
   190		}
   191		return false
   192	}
   193	
   194	// writeFileAtomic replaces path with data via a temporary file and a rename, so
   195	// a concurrent reader sees the old file or the new one, never a torn write.
   196	// An unchanged file is left alone, which keeps the directory fingerprint (and
   197	// so reindex) stable across syncs that bring nothing new.
   198	func writeFileAtomic(path string, data []byte) error {
   199		if existing, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil && bytes.Equal(existing, data) {
   200			return nil
   201		}
   202		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
   203			return err
   204		}
   205		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), "."+filepath.Base(path)+".tmp-*")
   206		if err != nil {
   207			return err
   208		}
   209		tmpName := tmp.Name()
   210		if _, err := tmp.Write(data); err != nil {
   211			_ = tmp.Close()
   212			_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
   213			return err
   214		}
   215		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
   216			_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
   217			return err
   218		}
   219		if err := os.Rename(tmpName, path); err != nil {
   220			_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
   221			return err
   222		}
   223		return nil
   224	}

   226	// writeEvents stores a run's events atomically.

   228		data, err := encodeEvents(events)

   235	// refreshOptions tunes a refresh for its caller.
   236	type refreshOptions struct {
   237		// skipStreams names runs whose events another goroutine is writing (a live
   238		// attach); the refresh must not replace their files underneath it.
   239		skipStreams map[string]bool
   240		now         time.Time
   241	}
   242	
   243	// refreshAgent brings one agent's mirror up to date. Runs, conversation and
   244	// usage are re-fetched only when agent.updatedAt differs from what the mirror
   245	// holds. Streams are fetched for finished runs whose capture is missing or
   246	// partial while the API still retains them; a whole capture is never
   247	// re-fetched. Unfinished runs are not streamed here, because reading a live
   248	// stream blocks until the run ends; the watcher attaches to those instead.
   249	// agent.json is written last so an interrupted refresh is retried next time.
   250	func (m mirror) refreshAgent(ctx context.Context, c *apiClient, record agentRecord, opts refreshOptions) error {
   251		agentID := record.agent.ID
   252		stored := m.readStoredAgent(agentID)
   253		changed := stored == nil || stored.UpdatedAt != record.agent.UpdatedAt
   254	
   255		if changed {
   256			runs, err := c.listRuns(ctx, agentID)
   257			if err != nil {
   258				return fmt.Errorf("list runs: %w", err)
   259			}
   260			for _, run := range runs {
   261				if err := writeFileAtomic(m.runFile(agentID, run.run.ID), run.raw); err != nil {
   262					return err
   263				}
   264			}
   265			// A transient failure is returned so agent.json keeps its old updatedAt
   266			// and the next sync retries; a permanent refusal is logged and the agent
   267			// is mirrored without that file, since retrying would never help.
   268			if conv, err := c.conversation(ctx, agentID); err != nil {
   269				if !permanentAPIError(err) {
   270					return fmt.Errorf("fetch conversation: %w", err)
   271				}
   272				slog.Warn("Conversation unavailable for this agent", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
   273			} else if err := writeFileAtomic(filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "conversation.json"), conv); err != nil {
   274				return err
   275			}
   276			if usage, err := c.usage(ctx, agentID); err != nil {
   277				if !permanentAPIError(err) {
   278					return fmt.Errorf("fetch usage: %w", err)
   279				}
   280				slog.Warn("Usage unavailable for this agent", "agentId", agentID, "error", err)
   281			} else if err := writeFileAtomic(filepath.Join(m.agentDir(agentID), "usage.json"), usage); err != nil {
   282				return err
   283			}
   284		}
   285	
   286		if err := m.fetchMissingStreams(ctx, c, agentID, opts); err != nil {
   287			return err
   288		}
   289	
   290		if changed {
   291			return writeFileAtomic(m.agentFile(agentID), record.raw)
   292		}
   293		return nil
   294	}
   295	
   296	// fetchMissingStreams replays the stream of every finished run whose mirrored
   297	// capture is not whole, while the API still retains it.
   298	func (m mirror) fetchMissingStreams(ctx context.Context, c *apiClient, agentID string, opts refreshOptions) error {
   299		entries, err := os.ReadDir(m.runsDir(agentID))
   300		if err != nil {
   301			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   302				return nil
   303			}
   304			return err
   305		}
   306		for _, entry := range entries {
   307			name := entry.Name()
   308			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
   309				continue
   310			}
   311			raw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(m.runsDir(agentID), name))
   312			if err != nil {
   313				return err
   314			}
   315			record, err := decodeRun(raw)
   316			if err != nil {
   317				continue
   318			}
   319			run := record.run
   320			if !run.isTerminal() || opts.skipStreams[run.ID] || !withinRetention(run, opts.now) {
   321				continue
   322			}
   323			events, err := readEventsFile(m.eventsFile(agentID, run.ID))
   324			if err != nil {
   325				return err
   326			}
   327			if eventsAreWhole(events) {
   328				continue
   329			}
   330			replayed, err := replayStream(ctx, c, agentID, run.ID)
   331			if errors.Is(err, errStreamExpired) {
   332				// Expired after all (clock skew or an early purge): the partial
   333				// capture stays and the v0 conversation fills the exchange.
   334				slog.Debug("Run stream expired; keeping partial capture", "agentId", agentID, "runId", run.ID)
   335				continue
   336			}
   337			if err != nil {
   338				return fmt.Errorf("replay stream %s: %w", run.ID, err)
   339			}
   340			if err := m.writeEvents(agentID, run.ID, replayed); err != nil {
   341				return err
   342			}
   343		}
   344		return nil
   345	}
   346	
   347	// withinRetention reports whether a finished run's stream should still be
   348	// replayable. now is wall-clock time; this decides whether to make a network
   349	// call and never reaches rendered output.
   350	func withinRetention(run apiRun, now time.Time) bool {
   351		ended, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, run.UpdatedAt)
   352		if err != nil {
   353			// Without a parseable end time, trying is cheaper than losing the transcript.
   354			return true
   355		}
   356		return now.Sub(ended) < streamRetention
   357	}
   358	
   359	// replayStream reads a finished run's stream from the start to its done event.
   360	func replayStream(ctx context.Context, c *apiClient, agentID, runID string) ([]sseEvent, error) {
   361		body, err := c.openStream(ctx, agentID, runID, "")
   362		if err != nil {
   363			return nil, err
   364		}
   365		defer func() { _ = body.Close() }()
   366		var events []sseEvent
   367		err = readSSE(body, agentID+"/"+runID, func(ev sseEvent) bool {
   368			events = append(events, ev)
   369			return ev.Event != "done"
   370		})
   371		if err != nil {
   372			return nil, err
   373		}
   374		return events, nil
   375	}
   376	
   377	// agentDirFingerprint sums sizes and takes the newest mtime across an agent
   378	// directory: one file (agent.json) does not change when a run's events land.
   379	func agentDirFingerprint(dir string) *spi.SessionFingerprint {
   380		fp := &spi.SessionFingerprint{}
   381		_ = filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
   382			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
   383				return nil
   384			}
   385			info, err := d.Info()
   386			if err != nil {
   387				return nil
   388			}
   389			fp.Size += info.Size()
   390			if mt := info.ModTime().UnixNano(); mt > fp.Mtime {
   391				fp.Mtime = mt
   392			}
   393			return nil
   394		})
   395		return fp
   396	}

    17	// Network constants. The request interval keeps every caller inside the
    18	// documented 20-requests-per-minute limit of the Cloud Agents API; the API
    19	// returns no rate-limit headers to pace against, so the client paces itself.
    20	const (
    21		defaultAPIBaseURL = "https://api.cursor.com"
    22		requestInterval   = 3 * time.Second
    23		jsonTimeout       = 30 * time.Second
    24		maxRetries        = 4
    25		maxBackoff        = 60 * time.Second
    26		// listPageSize is the API's maximum page size for GET /v1/agents.
    27		listPageSize = 100
    28	)
    29	
    30	// initialBackoff is the first retry delay after a 5xx, 429 or transport
    31	// failure, doubling up to maxBackoff. A variable so tests can shorten it.
    32	var initialBackoff = 5 * time.Second
    33	
    34	// apiBaseURL is a variable so tests can point the client at an httptest server.
    35	var apiBaseURL = defaultAPIBaseURL
    36	
    37	// streamIdleTimeout bounds how long a stream read may see no bytes before the
    38	// connection is treated as dead. The live stream sends a heartbeat event while
    39	// the agent is quiet, so 90 seconds of silence means the connection is gone.
    40	// A variable so tests can shorten it.
    41	var streamIdleTimeout = 90 * time.Second
    42	
    43	// errStreamExpired reports a 410 from the run stream endpoint: the stream is
    44	// retained for 24 hours after a run ends and is gone afterwards.
    45	var errStreamExpired = errors.New("run stream expired")
    46	
    47	// apiError is a non-success HTTP response from the Cloud Agents API, carrying
    48	// the error envelope the API returns ({"error":{"code","message"}}).
    49	type apiError struct {
    50		Status  int
    51		Code    string
    52		Message string
    53	}
    54	
    55	// permanentAPIError reports a 4xx other than 429: the API refused the request
    56	// itself, so repeating it with the same inputs cannot succeed. Every other
    57	// failure (5xx, throttling, transport) may pass on a later attempt.
    58	func permanentAPIError(err error) bool {
    59		var ae *apiError
    60		return errors.As(err, &ae) && ae.Status >= 400 && ae.Status < 500 && ae.Status != http.StatusTooManyRequests
    61	}
    62	
    63	func (e *apiError) Error() string {
    64		if e.Message != "" {
    65			return fmt.Sprintf("cursor api: HTTP %d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
    66		}
    67		return fmt.Sprintf("cursor api: HTTP %d", e.Status)
    68	}
    69	
    70	// isNotFound reports whether err is a 404 from the API.
    71	func isNotFound(err error) bool {
    72		var ae *apiError
    73		return errors.As(err, &ae) && ae.Status == http.StatusNotFound
    74	}
    75	
    76	// rateLimiter spaces requests at least interval apart across every caller in
    77	// the process: sync, watch polling and live streams all draw from one budget
    78	// because the API limit is per key, not per connection.
    79	type rateLimiter struct {
    80		mu       sync.Mutex
   140		streamHTTP *http.Client
   141		limiter    *rateLimiter
   142	}
   143	
   144	// newAPIClient builds a client for key. JSON calls carry a whole-request
   145	// timeout; stream calls cannot (a live run streams for minutes), so they rely
   146	// on the idle deadline in openStream for the body and on streamTransport for
   147	// the headers.
   148	func newAPIClient(key string) *apiClient {
   149		return &apiClient{
   150			key:        key,
   151			baseURL:    apiBaseURL,
   152			jsonHTTP:   &http.Client{Timeout: jsonTimeout},
   153			streamHTTP: &http.Client{Transport: streamTransport()},
   154			limiter:    sharedLimiter,
   155		}
   156	}
   157	
   158	// streamTransport is the default transport with a response-header deadline. The
   159	// idle reader only guards the body after Do returns, so without this a server
   160	// that accepts the connection and never answers would hang a replay forever.
   161	func streamTransport() *http.Transport {
   162		tr := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
   163		tr.ResponseHeaderTimeout = jsonTimeout
   164		return tr
   165	}
   166	
   167	// do sends one request built by build, waiting for the rate limiter first and
   168	// retrying 429 and 5xx responses with Retry-After or exponential backoff.
   169	// Transport failures (DNS, connection reset, timeout) take the same backoff,
   170	// because every request here is an idempotent GET and a sync that gave up on
   171	// one agent over a blip would leave it stale until the next run. A cancelled
   172	// context is never retried. A 2xx response is returned open; any other status
   173	// is returned as *apiError.
   174	func (c *apiClient) do(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client, build func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error)) (*http.Response, error) {
   175		backoff := initialBackoff
   176		for attempt := 0; ; attempt++ {
   177			if err := c.limiter.wait(ctx); err != nil {
   178				return nil, err
   179			}
   180			req, err := build(ctx)
   181			if err != nil {
   182				return nil, err
   183			}
   184			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.key)
   185			resp, err := httpClient.Do(req)
   186			if err != nil {
   187				if ctx.Err() != nil || attempt >= maxRetries {
   188					return nil, err
   189				}
   190				delay := backoff
   191				backoff = min(backoff*2, maxBackoff)
   192				slog.Warn("Cursor API request failed, retrying",
   193					"path", req.URL.Path, "error", err, "delay", delay, "attempt", attempt+1)
   194				c.limiter.holdUntil(c.limiter.now().Add(delay))
   195				continue
   196			}
   197			if resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300 {
   198				return resp, nil
   199			}
   200	
   201			apiErr := readAPIError(resp)
   202			retryable := resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests || resp.StatusCode >= 500
   203			if !retryable || attempt >= maxRetries {
   204				return nil, apiErr
   205			}
   206	
   207			delay := retryAfter(resp.Header.Get("Retry-After"), c.limiter.now())
   208			if delay <= 0 {
   209				delay = backoff
   210				backoff = min(backoff*2, maxBackoff)
   211			}
   212			slog.Warn("Cursor API request throttled or failed, retrying",
   213				"path", req.URL.Path, "status", resp.StatusCode, "delay", delay, "attempt", attempt+1)
   214			c.limiter.holdUntil(c.limiter.now().Add(delay))
   215		}
   216	}

   218	// readAPIError drains and closes resp, decoding the API's error envelope.
   219	func readAPIError(resp *http.Response) *apiError {
   220		defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
   221		apiErr := &apiError{Status: resp.StatusCode}
   222		// The error envelope is small; the cap only guards against a proxy page.
   223		body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 64*1024))
   224		var envelope struct {

   226				Code    string `json:"code"`
   227				Message string `json:"message"`
   228			} `json:"error"`
   229		}

   231			apiErr.Code = envelope.Error.Code
   232			apiErr.Message = envelope.Error.Message
   233		}
   234		return apiErr
   235	}

   239	func retryAfter(header string, now time.Time) time.Duration {
   240		if header == "" {
   241			return 0
   242		}
   243		if secs, err := strconv.Atoi(header); err == nil && secs > 0 {
   244			return time.Duration(secs) * time.Second
   245		}
   246		if t, err := http.ParseTime(header); err == nil {
   247			return t.Sub(now)
   248		}
   249		return 0

// liveSnapshot copies the attached-run set; callers hold w.mu.
func (w *cloudWatcher) liveSnapshot() map[string]bool {
	return maps.Clone(w.live)
}

// attachRunning starts a follower for every unfinished run in this project's
// mirror that has none, up to maxLiveStreams.
func (w *cloudWatcher) attachRunning() {
	for _, snap := range w.mirror.matchingSnapshots(w.origin) {
		for _, run := range snap.runs {
			if run.run.isTerminal() {
				continue
			}
			w.mu.Lock()
			attach := !w.live[run.run.ID] && len(w.live) < maxLiveStreams && w.ctx.Err() == nil
			if attach {
				w.live[run.run.ID] = true
			}
			w.mu.Unlock()
			if !attach {
				continue
			}
			agentID, runID := snap.agent.ID, run.run.ID
			slog.Info("WatchAgent: following live run", "agentId", agentID, "runId", runID)
			w.workers.Go(func() {
				w.followRun(agentID, runID)
				w.mu.Lock()
				delete(w.live, runID)
				w.mu.Unlock()
			})
		}
	}
}

// tightenUserConfigMode strips group and other permission bits from the user
// config, because it can hold credentials such as cursor_api_key. Files created
// by earlier releases are 0644, and os.WriteFile keeps an existing file's mode,
// so creation-time permissions alone would leave upgraded installs readable by
// other local users. Only the user config is touched: a project config is shared
// with the project on purpose, and its permissions belong to the repository.
// Windows has no POSIX mode bits (Chmod there only toggles read-only), so the
// file is left alone.
func tightenUserConfigMode(path string) {
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		return
	}
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	perm := info.Mode().Perm()
	if perm&0o077 == 0 {
		return
	}
	if err := os.Chmod(path, perm&^0o077); err != nil {
		slog.Debug("Could not tighten user config permissions", "path", path, "error", err)
		return
	}
	slog.Debug("Tightened user config permissions", "path", path, "was", perm.String())
}

## Session model

// UserMessage prints a plain message to stderr without any prefix or color
// This respects the silent flag - no output if silent mode is enabled
func UserMessage(format string, args ...interface{}) {
	if !isSilent() {
		message := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, message)
	}
}

// UserWarn prints a warning message to stderr with orange color
// This respects the silent flag - no output if silent mode is enabled
func UserWarn(format string, args ...interface{}) {
	if !isSilent() {
		message := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n%sWarning: %s\n%s", ColorOrange, message, ColorReset)
	}
}

// UserError prints an error message to stderr with bright red color
// This respects the silent flag - no output if silent mode is enabled

// DetectAgent, so already-mirrored histories must still be detected after the

func TestDetectAgentReadsMirrorWithoutKey(t *testing.T) {
	useSettings(t, "")
	f := newFakeAPI(t)
	project := makeProject(t, t.TempDir(), testOrigin)
	if NewProvider().DetectAgent(project, false) {
		t.Error("detected agents with an empty mirror and no key")

		t.Error("mirrored agent not detected without a key")
	}

		t.Errorf("detection without a key made %d API requests", n)
	}
}

// because at one request every 3 seconds a first sync of a busy repository
// spends minutes here, before any session is parsed.
func refreshProject(ctx context.Context, m mirror, projectLocal bool, origin string, progress spi.ProgressCallback) {
	key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
	if key == "" {
		slog.Debug("No Cursor API key; reading the mirror only")
		return
	}
	client := newAPIClient(key)
	agents, err := client.listAgentsFrom(ctx, takeDetectedPage(client), 0)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to list cloud agents; using the mirror only", "error", err)
		return
	}
	var matched []agentRecord
	for _, record := range agents {
		if agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, origin) {
			matched = append(matched, record)
		}
	}
	if len(matched) == 0 {
		return
	}
	if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
		slog.Error("Failed to create mirror", "path", m.root, "error", err)
		return
	}
	for i, record := range matched {
		if err := m.refreshAgent(ctx, client, record, refreshOptions{now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
			slog.Error("Failed to refresh cloud agent", "agentId", record.agent.ID, "error", err)
		}
		if progress != nil {
			progress(i+1, len(matched))
		}
	}
}

// detectedPage hands the first agent-list page DetectAgent fetched to the
// refresh that follows it. sync calls the two back to back, and at one request
// every 3 seconds listing the same page twice is a visible pause. The page is
// taken at most once, only by a client for the same key and server, and only
// while fresh, so a later refresh in a long-lived process lists again.
var detectedPage struct {
	sync.Mutex
	client string
	at     time.Time
	page   *agentPage
}

// detectedPageReuse bounds how old a handed-over page may be.
const detectedPageReuse = 30 * time.Second

func rememberDetectedPage(c *apiClient, page agentPage) {
	detectedPage.Lock()
	defer detectedPage.Unlock()
	detectedPage.client = c.baseURL + "\\x00" + c.key
	detectedPage.at = time.Now()
	detectedPage.page = &page
}

// takeDetectedPage returns the remembered page for c and forgets it, or nil
// when there is none, it is stale, or it came from another key or server.
func takeDetectedPage(c *apiClient) *agentPage {
	detectedPage.Lock()
	defer detectedPage.Unlock()
	page := detectedPage.page
	detectedPage.page = nil
	if page == nil || detectedPage.client != c.baseURL+"\\x00"+c.key || time.Since(detectedPage.at) > detectedPageReuse {
		return nil
	}
	return page
}

func TestClientRetriesThrottledRequests(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		status     int
		retryAfter string
		wantDelay  time.Duration
	}{
		{"429 with Retry-After seconds", http.StatusTooManyRequests, "7", 7 * time.Second},
		{"429 without Retry-After backs off", http.StatusTooManyRequests, "", initialBackoff},
		{"503 retried", http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "", initialBackoff},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			calls := 0
			server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
				calls++
				if calls == 1 {
					if tt.retryAfter != "" {
						w.Header().Set("Retry-After", tt.retryAfter)
					}
					writeAPIError(w, tt.status, "rate_limited", "slow down")
					return
				}
				_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"apiKeyName":"k"}`))
			}))
			defer server.Close()

			clock := &fakeClock{now: time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0)}
			c := newAPIClient("test-key")
			c.baseURL = server.URL
			c.limiter = &rateLimiter{interval: 0, now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

			me, err := c.me(context.Background())
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("me: %v", err)
			}
			if me.KeyLabel != "k" || calls != 2 {
				t.Errorf("got key %q after %d calls, want k after 2", me.KeyLabel, calls)
			}
			if len(clock.slept) != 1 || clock.slept[0] != tt.wantDelay {
				t.Errorf("slept %v, want [%v]", clock.slept, tt.wantDelay)
			}
		})
	}
}

	calls := 0
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		calls++
		if calls == 1 {
			conn, _, err := w.(http.Hijacker).Hijack()
			if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if calls != len(sessions) {
		t.Errorf("progress called %d times for %d sessions", calls, len(sessions))
	}
	return sessions
}

I've made all the changes you asked for on `cloud-agent-provider`. Nothing is committed. Lint shows 0 issues, `go test ./...` and the race runs pass, and the Windows build succeeds. I checked each new test by temporarily undoing its fix and confirming the test then fails.

## What changed

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| #37 `pr_management` | Removed from the tool classifier, so it now renders as `unknown`. The rows in `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md` and `TOOL-AUDIT.md` now say so. |
| #51 `attachRunning` | Each watch poll now reads only `agent.json` and the run records, not every events file. |
| #46 `--silent` | The two "Opened …" / "Could not open …" lines now go through `log.UserMessage` / `log.UserWarn`, which respect `--silent`. |
| #21 `Retry-After` | Capped at 60 seconds, with a comment explaining why. Tests cover a date value, an oversized value and an unparseable value. |
| #70 config comment | Reworded to match the code. All configs are created 0600; only the user config is tightened after the fact. I kept the PR's 0600 rather than loosening it, because a project config can hold `cursor_api_key` too. |
| #28 missing log | A run that can't be decoded during the stream fetch now logs a warning, like the other read path. |
| #6 double listing | `DetectAgent` passes the agent-list page it already fetched to the refresh that follows. The page is used once, only by the same key and server, and only within 30 seconds. |
| #8 progress | The refresh now reports progress per agent, so a first sync shows a counter instead of minutes of silence. |
| #25 | `os.IsNotExist` replaced with `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)` in `mirror.go` and `stream_parser.go`. |

Two changes went slightly beyond what you listed, both in code I was already rewriting:
- **#9:** the mirror directory setup now runs once before the loop instead of once per agent.
- **Detection:** `DetectAgent` was also loading every saved transcript just to check whether any agent existed. It now shares the cheap `agent.json`-only lookup with the watcher.

One test helper behaves differently: `syncProject` used to expect exactly one progress call per session. Progress now runs twice (fetch, then parse), so the helper checks that the parse pass ends at `[n/n]`. The new `TestSyncAfterDetectListsOnce` checks the exact order.

A side effect of #8: the counter shows the agent fetch first and then the parse, both under the "Parsing … sessions [k/n]" label, so it counts up twice. I think that's acceptable because parsing is fast, but it is visible.

## Remaining MIP #1: refresh logging

With #8 done, users now see progress. What's left is that `--log` still records nothing per agent during the refresh.
- **Option A:** add one `slog.Info("Refreshing cloud agent", agentId, i, n)` line per agent. It's one line and helps diagnose a slow sync from a log file.
- **Option B:** leave it as is. The progress counter plus the existing per-agent error logs may be enough.

I recommend A, because a slow sync is the most likely support question for this provider and the log is the only record afterwards.

## Remaining MIP #4: two open questions

**(31) v0 fallback keyed by run position.** If a run is missing from the mirror, the text-only fallback for every later run lands in the wrong exchange.
- **A. Guard:** use the fallback only when the number of runs equals the number of v0 turns; otherwise skip it and log. You'd get a missing exchange rather than a wrong one.
- **B. Key by a real identifier:** match on an id or timestamp in the v0 messages. This needs one look at a live `/v0/.../conversation` response to see whether one exists.
- **C. Document the assumption only.**

I recommend A now, with a test for the missing-run case, and B later if the live response turns out to carry an id. History in the wrong place is worse than a gap.

**(45) Repo matching is case-sensitive.** An origin of `SpecStoryAI/Repo` won't match a Cursor record of `specstoryai/repo`.
- **A. Ignore case:** compare with `strings.EqualFold` in `agentMatchesOrigin` only, which leaves project hashing untouched. The only risk is a self-hosted server with case-sensitive paths, which is negligible.
- **B. Check first:** launch an agent from a mixed-case clone and see what Cursor records.

I recommend A. It's a one-line change plus one row in `TestAgentMatchesOrigin`, and it's safe either way.

## Tests

- **Added:** `TestSyncAfterDetectListsOnce`, which checks that the agent list is requested once, the progress order, and that the handed-over page is used only once. I also added three `Retry-After` rows to the existing table test. Both fail when their fix is undone.
- **Still worth adding:** the missing-run v0 test if you pick A for 31, and the case row if you pick A for 45.
- **Optional cleanup (#58):** fold the URL-normalization cases still tested in `pkg/utils` into the `pkg/spi` test.

## Decision

Items 2, 3 and 5 are done, and most of 1. Once you choose on the #1 log line and the two #4 questions, I'd call this **ready to merge**. Real-agent checks still rest on the PR author's macOS run; nobody has run it with a live key on Linux or Windows.

- Replace the version floor in the changelog on release day.
- Website docs.
- Factory enrollment of `latest-version`.
- Follow-ups #358, #359, and a new issue for a shared tilde-expander (#44).

// buildExchange builds one run's exchange. The stream is the full-fidelity
// source; the v0 conversation (text only) fills in when the stream is missing,
// or when a finished run's capture is partial and the stream has since expired.
func buildExchange(snap *agentSnapshot, index int, run runSnapshot, workspaceRoot string) *schema.Exchange {
	source := snap.dir + "/runs/" + run.run.ID
	useStream := len(run.events) > 0
	if useStream && run.run.isTerminal() && !eventsAreWhole(run.events) && len(v0TurnMessages(snap.conversation, index)) > 0 {
		useStream = false
	}

	var exchange *schema.Exchange
	if useStream {
		exchange = exchangeFromStream(parseRunEvents(run.events, source), run, workspaceRoot)
	}
	if exchange == nil {
		exchange = exchangeFromConversation(snap.conversation, index, run)
	}
	if exchange == nil {
		slog.Debug("Run has no recorded content yet", "agentId", snap.agent.ID, "runId", run.run.ID)
		return nil
	}
	exchange.Metadata = exchangeMetadata(snap.agent, run.run, exchange.Metadata)
	return exchange
}

// exchangeFromStream turns a transcript into messages: the prompt, then agent
// messages in stream order. Thinking and text share one agent message until a
// tool call interrupts; each tool call is its own message.
func exchangeFromStream(t runTranscript, run runSnapshot, workspaceRoot string) *schema.Exchange {
	if t.userText == "" && len(t.segments) == 0 {

// v0TurnMessages returns the v0 messages belonging to run index turn. Ids are
// "turn-N:user" and "turn-N:step:M:assistant"; the agent's very first user
// message has a bare UUID id and belongs to turn 0.
func v0TurnMessages(conv *v0Conversation, turn int) []v0Message {
	if conv == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []v0Message
	for _, msg := range conv.Messages {
		if v0MessageTurn(msg.ID) == turn {
			out = append(out, msg)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// v0MessageTurn parses the turn index from a v0 message id.
func v0MessageTurn(id string) int {
	rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(id, "turn-")
	if !ok {
		return 0
	}
	digits, _, _ := strings.Cut(rest, ":")
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(digits)
	if err != nil {
		return -1
	}
	return n
}

// buildSessionData converts a mirrored agent into SessionData. It returns nil
// when no run yields a user prompt, which means there is nothing to save yet.
func buildSessionData(snap *agentSnapshot, workspaceRoot string) (*schema.SessionData, string) {
	agent := snap.agent
	data := &schema.SessionData{
		SchemaVersion: schema.CurrentSchemaVersion,
		// The API exposes no agent version, so the honest value is "unknown".
		Provider:      schema.ProviderInfo{ID: ProviderID, Name: providerName, Version: "unknown"},
		SessionID:     agent.ID,
		CreatedAt:     agent.CreatedAt,
		UpdatedAt:     agent.UpdatedAt,
		WorkspaceRoot: workspaceRoot,
		Exchanges:     []schema.Exchange{},
	}

	firstPrompt := ""
	for i, run := range snap.runs {
		exchange := buildExchange(snap, i, run, workspaceRoot)
		if exchange == nil {
			continue
		}
		if firstPrompt == "" {
			firstPrompt = firstUserText(exchange)
		}
		data.Exchanges = append(data.Exchanges, *exchange)
	}
	if firstPrompt == "" {
		return nil, ""
	}

func TestResolveAPIKeyEnvironmentWins(t *testing.T) {
	useSettings(t, "from-env")
	SetAPIKey("from-config")
	if key, source := resolveAPIKey(); key != "from-env" || source != apiKeyEnvVar {
		t.Errorf("got %q from %q", key, source)
	}
	t.Setenv(apiKeyEnvVar, "")
	if key, source := resolveAPIKey(); key != "from-config" || source != "cursor_api_key" {
		t.Errorf("got %q from %q", key, source)

	second := data.Exchanges[1]
	if second.Messages[0].ID != "turn-1:user" || len(second.Messages) != 2 {

	}

		}
	}

I've made all three changes with your chosen options and added the two tests. Lint shows 0 issues, `go test ./...` and three race runs pass, and the Windows build succeeds. Nothing is committed. I checked both new tests by undoing each fix; they fail without it and pass with it.

## #1: refresh log

`refreshProject` (`provider.go`) now writes one `slog.Info("Refreshing cloud agent", agentId, index, total)` line per agent before fetching it. A slow sync can now be traced from `--log` as well as from the progress counter.

## #31: v0 fallback guard

- **What it does:** a new `alignedConversation` (`agent_session.go`) builds the v0 conversation into a session only when its turn count equals the number of runs in the mirror. Otherwise it logs a warning and the conversation isn't used for that session.
- **Why:** v0 messages carry only a turn number, not a run id. If a run is missing from the mirror, every later run's text would land in the wrong exchange. With the guard, the partial stream is kept, or the exchange is skipped.
- **How:** `buildSessionData` works this out once and passes it to `buildExchange`, which now takes it as a parameter instead of reading `snap.conversation`.
- **Existing coverage:** the fixture's normal fallback case, `TestV0FallbackForExpiredPartialRun`, still passes, so aligned data isn't affected.

## #45: origin matching ignores case

`agentMatchesOrigin` (`path_utils.go`) now compares with `strings.EqualFold`, with a comment explaining why. Only this provider's matching changes; `git_id` hashing and the shared normalizer are untouched.

// followRun streams a run into its events file until the run ends or the
// watcher stops. Events are flushed and the session queued for delivery after
// each burst (debounced), once more when the run ends, and on stop if an
// update is still undelivered. Only events stamped after the watcher started
// count as activity: attaching replays the run from its start.
func (w *cloudWatcher) followRun(agentID, runID string) {
	events, err := readEventsFile(w.mirror.eventsFile(agentID, runID))
	if err != nil {

// lastEventID returns the id of the last event that carries one.
func lastEventID(events []sseEvent) string {
	for i := len(events) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if events[i].ID != "" {
			return events[i].ID
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// eventsWithID returns the identities of recorded events with the given id.
func eventsWithID(events []sseEvent, id string) map[string]bool {
	set := map[string]bool{}
	if id == "" {
		return set
	}
	for _, ev := range events {
		if ev.ID == id {
			set[eventKey(ev)] = true
		}
	}
	return set
}

// the context, or when the API refuses the listing for good: a rejected key or
// an account on Privacy Mode fails every poll the same way, and polling on
// would leave `run` and `watch` claiming to watch while nothing can ever be
// saved. That error is handed to WatchAgent through fatal.
func (w *cloudWatcher) pollLoop() {
	baseline := true
	for {
		listed, err := w.poll(baseline)
		if err != nil {
			w.fatal <- err
			return
		}
		if listed {
			baseline = false
		}
		if sleepContext(w.ctx, pollInterval) != nil {
			return
		}
	}
}

// poll lists agents and acts on the ones for this project. The baseline poll
// mirrors whatever is new but emits nothing: existing sessions are not news
// because the watcher started. Afterwards an agent seen for the first time or
// whose updatedAt moved is refreshed and emitted. An agent changing during the
// baseline is caught by the next poll, because the baseline records the
// updatedAt it listed, not what the agent became. The first result reports
// whether the listing succeeded: pollLoop keeps the baseline open until it has,
// so a failed first poll cannot turn every pre-existing agent into news. The
// error is set only when the listing was refused permanently (a 4xx other than
// 429); transport, 429 and 5xx failures are retried on the next poll.
//
// "Listed at startup" and "refreshed" are tracked apart. seen records only
// refreshes that succeeded, so an agent whose baseline refresh failed is
// retried on every poll until its mirror is filled; startup remembers the
// updatedAt the baseline listed, so those retries stay silent while nothing
// about the agent has changed, and become news once it has.
func (w *cloudWatcher) poll(baseline bool) (bool, error) {
	agents, err := w.client.listAgents(w.ctx, maxPollPages)
	if err != nil {
		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
			return false, nil
		}
		if permanentAPIError(err) {
			return false, fmt.Errorf("listing cloud agents: %w", err)
		}
		slog.Warn("WatchAgent: listing cloud agents failed; retrying next poll", "error", err)
		return false, nil
	}
	for _, record := range agents {
		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
			return false, nil
		}
		agent := record.agent
		if !agentMatchesOrigin(agent, w.origin) {
			continue
		}
		w.mu.Lock()
		prev, known := w.seen[agent.ID]
		if baseline {
			w.startup[agent.ID] = agent.UpdatedAt
		}
		// Quiet while the agent is exactly as the baseline listed it, even if
		// that baseline refresh failed and this is a retry.
		quiet := baseline || w.startup[agent.ID] == agent.UpdatedAt
		skip := w.liveSnapshot()
		w.mu.Unlock()
		if known && prev == agent.UpdatedAt {
			continue
		}

		if err := w.mirror.ensureRoot(w.projectLocal); err != nil {
			slog.Error("WatchAgent: cannot create mirror", "path", w.mirror.root, "error", err)
			return false, nil
		}
		if err := w.mirror.refreshAgent(w.ctx, w.client, record, refreshOptions{skipStreams: skip, now: time.Now()}); err != nil {
			if w.ctx.Err() == nil {
				slog.Error("WatchAgent: refreshing cloud agent failed; retrying next poll", "agentId", agent.ID, "error", err)
			}
			continue
		}
		w.mu.Lock()
		w.seen[agent.ID] = agent.UpdatedAt
		w.mu.Unlock()
		if quiet {
			slog.Debug("WatchAgent: baseline", "agentId", agent.ID, "updatedAt", agent.UpdatedAt)
		} else {
			slog.Info("WatchAgent: cloud agent updated", "agentId", agent.ID, "updatedAt", agent.UpdatedAt)
			w.enqueue(agent.ID)
		}
	}
	w.attachRunning()
	return true, nil

func TestNormalizedGitURLConsistency(t *testing.T) {
	manager := &ProjectIdentityManager{}

	// Test pairs of URLs that should generate the same normalized form

	for _, pair := range urlPairs {
		t.Run(pair.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			httpsNormalized := manager.normalizeGitURL(pair.https)
			sshNormalized := manager.normalizeGitURL(pair.ssh)

			if httpsNormalized != sshNormalized {
				t.Errorf("HTTPS and SSH URLs should normalize to the same value:\nHTTPS: %s -> %s\nSSH: %s -> %s",

			}

			// Also verify that the hashes would be the same
			httpsHash := manager.createHash(httpsNormalized)
			sshHash := manager.createHash(sshNormalized)

			if httpsHash != sshHash {
				t.Errorf("HTTPS and SSH URLs should generate the same hash:\nHTTPS hash: %s\nSSH hash: %s",
					httpsHash, sshHash)
			}
		})
	}
}

## 53: why the watcher compares local and server times

**The problem it solves.** When `watch` starts and Cursor already has a run in progress, the watcher attaches to that run's live stream. If nothing was saved for that run yet, Cursor replays the stream from the beginning. All of those replayed events happened before you started watching, and the guide says a session that hasn't changed since startup must not be saved or announced.

So in `followRun` (`watcher.go:306`), every event is written to the local copy of Cursor's data, but only events timestamped after the watcher started mark the session as needing delivery. Delivery is what produces the markdown save and the per-save line. The timestamp comes from the event's id, which is Cursor's server time in milliseconds. "After the watcher started" is `w.startedAt = time.Now()`, which is your machine's clock. That's where the two clocks meet.

**What skew does:**

| Your clock vs. Cursor's | Effect | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Ahead by X | New events in the first X seconds look old and aren't delivered | The next live event delivers it. If the run ends inside X, the 60-second poll sees `updatedAt` change and saves it |
| Behind by X | Replayed events from the X seconds before start look new, so the session is saved once on attach | None needed. The save is idempotent, and the agent really was active |

NTP keeps typical skew under a second, so this is a minor ordering issue: no data is lost, and the worst case is one extra save or a save up to 60 seconds late.

**Options:**
- **A. Document it.** Add one sentence at `watcher.go:306` naming the skew and the poll that recovers from it. No code change.
- **B. Compare server time with server time.** Use the agent's `updatedAt` from the startup listing as the cutoff instead of the local clock. That removes skew entirely. Agents first seen after startup have no cutoff, so all their events count, which is correct. The catch is that `updatedAt` may trail a run's latest events, so a run already mid-flight at startup would usually get one extra save on attach. That's the same harmless effect as the clock-behind row, just more often.
- **C. Leave it as is.**

I recommend A. B swaps a rare sub-second edge case for an extra save that would happen more often, and both are harmless; A just keeps the next reader from re-deriving all this.

package cursorcloud

import (

// fastWatcher shortens the watcher's timings so acceptance cases run quickly.
func fastWatcher(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	prevPoll, prevDebounce, prevReconnect := pollInterval, emitDebounce, reconnectDelay
	pollInterval, emitDebounce, reconnectDelay = 40*time.Millisecond, 20*time.Millisecond, 10*time.Millisecond
	t.Cleanup(func() { pollInterval, emitDebounce, reconnectDelay = prevPoll, prevDebounce, prevReconnect })
}

// emissions records delivered sessions.
type emissions struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	sessions []*spi.AgentChatSession
}

func (e *emissions) callback(s *spi.AgentChatSession) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.sessions = append(e.sessions, s)
}

func (e *emissions) all() []*spi.AgentChatSession {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]*spi.AgentChatSession(nil), e.sessions...)
}

// waitFor polls cond until it holds or the deadline passes.
func waitFor(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// startWatcher starts a watcher for a fresh project and returns it with its
// emissions; stop is the caller's.
func startWatcher(t *testing.T) (*cloudWatcher, *emissions) {
	t.Helper()
	project := makeProject(t, t.TempDir(), testOrigin)
	got := &emissions{}
	w := newCloudWatcher(project, projectOrigin(project), newAPIClient("test-key"), false, got.callback)
	w.start(context.Background())
	return w, got
}

// withUpdatedAt returns a copy of an agent object with a new updatedAt.
func withUpdatedAt(t *testing.T, raw json.RawMessage, updatedAt string) json.RawMessage {
	t.Helper()
	var agent map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &agent); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	agent["updatedAt"] = updatedAt
	out, _ := json.Marshal(agent)
	return out
}

}

## 53: activity cutoff now uses Cursor's clock

- **Change:** `followRun` in `watcher.go` no longer compares event times with the local `time.Now()` taken at watch start. It now compares them with the agent's `updatedAt` from the first listing at startup, which is also Cursor's clock, so skew can't affect it. An agent first listed after startup has no cutoff, so all of its events count as new. The now-unused `startedAt` field is gone.
- **New test:** `TestWatcherAttachReplayCutoff` has two cases. When the startup `updatedAt` is after the replayed events, nothing is delivered. When it's before them, the session is delivered. Neither the old code nor the new had a test for this rule. Ignoring the cutoff fails the first case, and the old local-clock comparison would fail the second.

func expandTilde(path string) string {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
		return path
	}

	if err != nil {
		return path
	}

	return filepath.Join(home, path[2:])

// expandHome expands a leading ~ so config and flag values can use it.
func expandHome(path string) string {
	if path != "~" && !strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") && !strings.HasPrefix(path, `~\`) {
		return path
	}
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return path
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, strings.TrimLeft(path[1:], `/\`))

I filed #44 as https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/362. It lists the nine tilde expanders, notes that only Cursor Cloud's handles a bare `~` and Windows `~\`, and proposes one exported `spi.ExpandHome`.

## 46: why the stderr line exists

In this PR, `cursorcloud_exec.go` no longer uses `fmt.Fprintf`. I switched both lines to `log.UserMessage` / `log.UserWarn` earlier, and that change is in what's staged.

I wouldn't remove the lines themselves. For CLI agents, `run` hands the terminal to the agent's own interface. For hosted and IDE providers, `run` opens something outside the terminal (the cloud dashboard, Cursor, VS Code) and then sits watching. Without a line saying "watching, press Ctrl-C to stop", the terminal goes blank and looks hung. That line is the only sign that `run` is working and how to end it.

The real issue was only the output path: `fmt.Fprintf` ignores `--silent`, while `log.UserMessage` respects it.

## The other providers

The same pattern is in two older IDE providers, not just one:

| File | Lines | What they print |
|---|---|---|
| `cursoride/provider.go` | 487–514 | "Session is ready", open-manually hint, "Watching…", "Waiting…" |
| `copilotide/provider.go` | 403–441 | Same set, plus "opened the project" |
| `copilotide/reconstruct.go` | 166 | Warning that the IDE is running |
| `copilotide/reconstruct.go` | 177 | "Quit it, then press Enter" prompt |

I'd convert all of these to `log.UserMessage` / `log.UserWarn` except the `reconstruct.go:177` prompt. That one waits for Enter, so under `--silent` it would block with no text explaining why. It should keep printing directly.

I'd put this in its own small PR rather than #357, since it changes two providers that PR doesn't touch. Want me to make that change on a separate branch, or file it as an issue?

132:func readSSE(r io.Reader, source string, emit func(sseEvent) bool) error {
func readSSE(r io.Reader, source string, emit func(sseEvent) bool) error {
	reader := bufio.NewReader(r)
	var id, event string
	var data strings.Builder
	hasData, skipBlock := false, false
	lineNo := 0

	dispatch := func() bool {
		defer func() {
			id, event = "", ""
			data.Reset()
			hasData, skipBlock = false, false
		}()
		if skipBlock {
			slog.Warn("Skipping oversized SSE block", "source", source, "line", lineNo)
			return true
		}
		if event == "" && !hasData {
			return true
		}
		if event == "" {
			// The SSE default event type; never observed from this API.
			event = "message"
		}
		return emit(sseEvent{ID: id, Event: event, Data: sseData(data.String(), hasData)})
	}

	for {
		line, oversized, err := spi.ReadRecordLine(reader, maxSSELineSize)
		if len(line) > 0 || oversized {
			lineNo++
		}
		if oversized {
			skipBlock = true
		} else if len(line) > 0 || err == nil {
			text := strings.TrimRight(string(line), "\r\n")
			if text == "" {
				if !dispatch() {
					return nil
				}
			} else if !strings.HasPrefix(text, ":") {
				field, value, _ := strings.Cut(text, ":")
				value = strings.TrimPrefix(value, " ")
				switch field {
				case "id":
					id = value
				case "event":
					event = value
				case "data":
					// SSE joins every data line of a block into one payload, so
					// the cap applies to their total, not to each line.
					if data.Len()+1+len(value) > maxSSELineSize {
						skipBlock = true
					} else {
						if hasData {
							data.WriteString("\n")
						}
						data.WriteString(value)
						hasData = true
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if err != nil {
			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
				dispatch()
				return nil
			}
			return err
		}
	}
}

// sseData keeps a data payload as JSON. Every payload observed is a JSON
// object; anything else is preserved as a JSON string so no content is lost.
func sseData(text string, hasData bool) json.RawMessage {
	if !hasData {
		return nil
	}
	if json.Valid([]byte(text)) {
		return json.RawMessage(text)

	case "todo_write":
		return formatTodos(in["todos"])
	case "mcp":
		return formatMCPInput(in)
	case "get_mcp_tools":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"server", "Server"}, {"toolName", "Tool"}})
	case "await":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"blockUntilMs", "Wait (ms)"}})
	case "generate_image":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"description", "Description"}, {"aspectRatio", "Aspect ratio"}, {"filePath", "File"}})
	case "write_canvas":
		var b strings.Builder
		if title := spi.StringValue(in, "title"); title != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Title: %s\n\n", title)
		}
		if contents := spi.StringValue(in, "contents"); contents != "" {
			b.WriteString(spi.CodeFence("jsx", contents))
		}
		return b.String()
	case "read_canvas":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"canvasId", "Canvas"}})
	default:
		return spi.RenderGenericJSON(in)
	}
}

// formatLabeledInput covers the tools whose summary already names the key
// argument; only the secondary arguments are worth a line.
func formatLabeledInput(in map[string]any, name string) string {
	switch name {
	case "file_search":
		return labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"targetDirectory", "Directory"}})
	case "grep_search":
		var b strings.Builder
		b.WriteString(labeledLines(in, [][2]string{{"path", "Path"}, {"glob", "Glob"}}))
		var flags []string
		if v, _ := in["caseInsensitive"].(bool); v {
			flags = append(flags, "case-insensitive")
		}
		if v, _ := in["multiline"].(bool); v {
			flags = append(flags, "multiline")
		}
		if len(flags) > 0 {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Options: %s\n", strings.Join(flags, ", "))
		}
		return b.String()
	default:
		// read_file, delete_file, web_fetch, web_search: the summary carries it.
		return ""
	}
}

// labeledLines renders the given keys, in order, as "Label: value" lines.
// Path-valued labels are shown relative to the VM workspace.
func labeledLines(in map[string]any, keys [][2]string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, kv := range keys {
		value := spi.StringValue(in, kv[0])
		if value == "" {
			continue
		}
		if kv[0] == "path" || kv[0] == "targetDirectory" || kv[0] == "filePath" {
			value = displayPath(value)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s: %s\n", kv[1], spi.InlineCode(value))
	}
	return b.String()

cursorcloud: multi-repository agents are attributed to repos[0] on reindex
## Problem

`ListAllAgentChatSessions` in `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/provider.go` sets `GlobalSessionRef.OriginRepoURL` from `agent.repos[0]`, while project matching (`agentMatchesOrigin`) accepts any entry in `repos`. For an agent that lists several repositories, reindex attributes the session to the first one even if the project that mirrored it matched a later entry, so `list`, `search` and `resume` group it under the wrong project.

Raised by Copilot on #357 (review of 2026-10-14, "previously missed" list).

## Why it was not fixed in #357

Every agent observed against the live API (2026-10-13) has exactly one repository; the Cursor dashboard launches an agent against one repository. The index model carries a single `OriginRepoURL` per session, so a real fix either records which repository matched when the agent was mirrored (which a shared `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` serving several projects makes ambiguous) or extends the index to hold several repositories per session. Both are changes to the session index, not to the provider.

## Suggested fix

Decide at the index level: either allow a `GlobalSessionRef` to carry several origin repositories and let reindex attribute the session to each matching project, or record the matched repository in the mirror's `agent.json` sidecar at refresh time and prefer it on reindex.

func runReindex(force bool) error {
	start := time.Now()

	// Graceful Ctrl+C: stop feeding work, flush what's written, exit cleanly.
	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()

	dbPath, err := sessionindex.DefaultPath()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	store, err := sessionindex.Open(dbPath)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("opening restore index: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = store.Close() }()

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-15 15:58:57Z)**_

I've finished tracing how the session index files these sessions. Here is #359 from the user's side.

## The setup

A Cursor Cloud Agent is launched against one or more GitHub repositories. Cursor records that list on the agent, for example `[frontend, backend]`.

SpecStory decides which of your local projects an agent belongs to by comparing those repositories with each project's git origin.

## What the user does

1. They launch one cloud agent that works on two repos, `frontend` and `backend`. Cursor lists `frontend` first.
2. In their local clone of `backend`, they run `specstory sync`.

## What they see

**`sync` works correctly.** It looks for agents that list `backend` anywhere in their repo list, finds this one, and writes the markdown into `backend/.specstory/history/`. Nothing is wrong there.

**The session browser, `list`, `search` and `resume` can show it in the wrong place.** These read SpecStory's global session index (`~/.specstory/sessions.db`), which groups every session by project. When that index is rebuilt (`specstory reindex`, or the catch-up the session browser runs when it opens), the provider reports only one repository per agent: the first one, `frontend`. So the user may see:
- the `backend` agent session listed under the `frontend` project, or under a project they don't have locally;
- the session missing when they filter `list`/`search` to `backend`;
- `resume` from inside `backend` not offering it.

In short, the markdown is in the right folder, but the index files it under the other repo.

## Who it affects

Only agents launched against more than one repository, and only when the project you work in isn't first in that agent's list. Every agent we've captured has exactly one repository, and the Cursor dashboard launches an agent against one repo. So today this mostly affects agents created through the API, if Cursor even allows several repos there. We haven't seen one.

## Why it wasn't a quick fix

Each session in the index carries a single origin repository. To fix this properly, either:
- **A.** a session can carry several repositories, so it appears under each matching project; or
- **B.** the mirror records which repository matched when the agent was synced, and reindex prefers that.

Both change the index rather than the provider, and B is ambiguous when one shared mirror directory serves several projects.

The one part I haven't confirmed is whether a reindex overwrites the entry `sync` just indexed correctly, or keeps it because nothing changed. Either way, a full rebuild with `specstory reindex --force` attributes the session by the first repository.

https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/359
## Problem

`ListAllAgentChatSessions` in `pkg/providers/cursorcloud/provider.go` sets `GlobalSessionRef.OriginRepoURL` from `agent.repos[0]`, while project matching (`agentMatchesOrigin`) accepts any entry in `repos`. For an agent that lists several repositories, reindex attributes the session to the first one even if the project that mirrored it matched a later entry, so `list`, `search` and `resume` group it under the wrong project.

Raised by Copilot on #357 (review of 2026-10-14, "previously missed" list).

## What the user sees

Suppose an agent was launched against `[frontend, backend]`, and the user syncs from their `backend` clone.

- `sync` works correctly: the markdown lands in `backend/.specstory/history/`.
- After a reindex (`specstory reindex`, or the catch-up the session browser runs when it opens), the session browser, `list`, `search` and `resume` file the session under `frontend`, or under a project the user doesn't have locally.
- Filtering `list`/`search` to `backend` misses the session, and `resume` from inside `backend` doesn't offer it.

This only happens with multi-repository agents where the current project isn't the first repository listed. None have been observed, because the Cursor dashboard launches an agent against a single repository.

## Why it was not fixed in #357

Every agent observed against the live API (2026-10-13) has exactly one repository; the Cursor dashboard launches an agent against one repository. The index model carries a single `OriginRepoURL` per session, so a real fix either records which repository matched when the agent was mirrored (which a shared `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` serving several projects makes ambiguous) or extends the index to hold several repositories per session. Both are changes to the session index, not to the provider.

// printDivider prints a divider line for visual separation
func printDivider() {
	fmt.Println("\n--------")
}

// checkSingleProvider checks a specific provider
func checkSingleProvider(registry *factory.Registry, providerID, customCmd string) error {
	provider, err := registry.Get(providerID)
	if err != nil {
		// Provider not found - show helpful error
		fmt.Printf("❌ Provider '%s' is not a valid provider implementation\n\n", providerID)

		ids := registry.ListIDs()
		if len(ids) > 0 {
			fmt.Println("The registered providers are:")
			for _, id := range ids {
				if p, _ := registry.Get(id); p != nil {
					fmt.Printf("  • %s - %s\n", id, p.Name())
				}
			}
			fmt.Println("\nExample: specstory check " + ids[0])
		}
		return err
	}

	// Set the agent provider for analytics
	analytics.SetAgentProviders([]string{provider.Name()})

	// Run the check
	result := provider.Check(customCmd)

	// Display results with the nice formatting
	if result.Success {
		fmt.Printf("\n✨ %s is installed and ready! ✨\n\n", provider.Name())
		// IDE-backed providers report no version (none is discoverable cheaply);
		// omit the line rather than printing an empty value.
		if result.Version != "" {
			fmt.Printf("  📦 Version: %s\n", result.Version)
		}
		fmt.Printf("  📍 Location: %s\n", result.Location)
		fmt.Printf("  ✅ Status: All systems go!\n\n")

		fmt.Println("🚀 Ready to sync your sessions! 💪")
		normalizedID := strings.ToLower(providerID)
		fmt.Printf("   • specstory run %s\n", normalizedID)
		fmt.Println("   • specstory sync - Save markdown files for existing sessions")
		fmt.Println()

		return nil
	} else {
		fmt.Print(formatCheckFailure(provider.Name(), result, customCmd, false))
		return errors.New("check failed")
	}
}

// formatCheckFailure softens missing optional agents without hiding broken
// installs or an explicitly requested custom command that cannot be found.
// Older providers with no classification retain the failure presentation.
func formatCheckFailure(name string, result spi.CheckResult, customCmd string, summary bool) string {
	if result.ErrorType == spi.CheckErrorNotFound && strings.TrimSpace(customCmd) == "" {
		message := fmt.Sprintf("\nℹ️  %s not found.\n", name)
		if summary {
			return message + "   Optional — skipping.\n"
		}
		if result.ErrorMessage != "" {
			message += "\n" + result.ErrorMessage + "\n"
		}
		return message
	}
	message := fmt.Sprintf("\n❌ %s check failed!\n", name)
	if result.ErrorMessage != "" {
		if summary {
			firstLine := strings.SplitN(result.ErrorMessage, "\n", 2)[0]
			message += "\n  Error: " + strings.TrimSpace(firstLine) + "\n"
		} else {
			message += "\n" + result.ErrorMessage + "\n"
		}
	}
	return message
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-15 16:10:54Z)**_

## Why you got that

That shell has no `CURSOR_API_KEY`, and neither config file has `cursor_api_key`. For this provider, a missing key is reported as "not found". `specstory check` with no argument checks every provider and collapses each "not found" into that one generic line, so the reason is never shown.

The details only appear when you check this provider by itself (`specstory check cursorcloud`):

```
ℹ️  Cursor Cloud Agent not found.

No Cursor API key is configured.
• Create a key at https://cursor.com/dashboard/api
• Then set the CURSOR_API_KEY environment variable, or add it to specstory.toml: …
```

To continue testing, export the key from your keychain:

```zsh
export CURSOR_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -s cursor-api-key -w)"
```

## What a user gets from it: not much

There are two problems.

1. **"Not found" is the wrong idea.** For tools you install, it means "not installed", which is accurate. For a hosted agent there's nothing to install; what's missing is a key. The all-providers summary doesn't say that, or point anywhere that explains it.
2. **The setup text names a file that doesn't exist.** It says to add the key to `specstory.toml`. The real files are `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` and `.specstory/cli/config.toml`. The wrong name appears in:
   - `provider.go` (2 places)
   - `cursorcloud_exec.go`
   - two comments in `path_utils.go`
   - `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md`
   - `changelog.md`
   - `docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md`

## Options for problem 1

- **A. Show the provider's reason in the summary.** Print the first line of its guidance under the header: "No Cursor API key is configured." It's one change in `check.go`. The drawback is that most other tools' first line repeats the header ("DeepSeek TUI not found." then "DeepSeek TUI was not found.").
- **B. Point to the details.** Change "Optional — skipping." to "Optional — skipping. Run `specstory check cursorcloud` for setup." It's one change in `check.go`, works for every provider and never repeats itself. The header still says "not found".
- **C. Let a provider supply its own one-line reason** through a new optional field on `CheckResult`. It reads best ("ℹ️ Cursor Cloud Agent: no API key configured"), but it changes the SPI for one provider.

I recommend B now, because it's simple, shared and honest about where the explanation lives. I'd leave C for when a second hosted provider needs it. Problem 2 is a plain bug, and I'd fix it in this PR either way.

Which option do you want for problem 1, and should I fix the config file name?

func TestCheckFailurePresentation(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tt := range []struct {
		name, errorType, customCmd string
		summary, informational     bool
	}{
		{"optional absent agent", spi.CheckErrorNotFound, "", true, true},
		{"explicit absent agent", spi.CheckErrorNotFound, "", false, true},
		{"missing custom command", spi.CheckErrorNotFound, "/missing/agent", false, false},
		{"permission denied", spi.CheckErrorPermissionDenied, "", true, false},
		{"failed version probe", spi.CheckErrorUnknown, "", true, false},
		{"empty version output", spi.CheckErrorNoOutput, "", true, false},
		{"invalid version output", spi.CheckErrorUnexpectedOutput, "", true, false},
		{"unclassified failure", "", "", true, false},
	} {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			result := spi.CheckResult{ErrorType: tt.errorType, ErrorMessage: "Reason\nRemediation"}
			output := formatCheckFailure("Agent", result, tt.customCmd, tt.summary)
			if strings.Contains(output, "ℹ️") != tt.informational || strings.Contains(output, "❌") == tt.informational {
				t.Fatalf("wrong severity: %s", output)
			}
			if tt.summary {
				if strings.Contains(output, "Remediation") {
					t.Fatalf("summary includes full instructions: %s", output)
				}
				if tt.informational && (strings.Contains(output, "Error:") || !strings.Contains(output, "Optional")) {
					t.Fatalf("missing optional agent reads as an error: %s", output)
				}
			} else if !strings.Contains(output, "Remediation") {
				t.Fatalf("detailed check lost help: %s", output)
			}
		})
	}
}

## How It Works
```
AI Coding Tools              Local First                  Cloud Platform
─────────────────           ─────────────                ─────────────────
                                                          (Login Required)
Cursor IDE         ┐
Copilot IDE        │
Claude Code CLI    │
Cursor CLI         │
Cursor Cloud Agent │
Codex CLI          ├──────►  .specstory/history/  ──────►  cloud.specstory.com
Droid CLI          │          (Auto-Saved Locally)        (Search, Ask & Share)
DeepSeek TUI       │
Antigravity CLI    │
Grok Build         │
Muse Code          │
OpenCode           │
Pi                 │
Qwen Code          ┘
```

## Workflow

1. **Capture** - SpecStory CLI and IDE extensions save every AI interaction locally to `.specstory/history/`
2. **Sync (Optional)** - Sync your local sessions to SpecStory Cloud for safekeeping and team sharing
3. **Search** - Find conversations across all projects locally, or across multiple computers and team members in SpecStory Cloud
4. **Chat (Optional)** - Ask questions across your sessions in SpecStory Cloud to revisit decisions, understand past work, and find solutions
5. **Share** - Export and share specific solutions with your team
6. **Resume** - Resume sessions locally between different agents, and between multiple computers and team members with SpecStory Cloud
7. **Process** - Run [`/lore`](./lore) to mine your history into reusable, evidence-backed agent skills

## Supported Development Tools

SpecStory integrates seamlessly with your favorite AI coding tools, automatically saving all conversations locally to `.specstory/history/` in your project. **Everything is local-first** - your data stays on your machine unless you choose to sync to SpecStory Cloud.
