func formatParameters(input map[string]any) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, key := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(input)) {
		label := parameterLabels[key]
		if label == "" {
			label = key
		}
		// A list of IDs or paths reads better as code spans than as a JSON array.
		if items, ok := stringList(input[key]); ok && len(items) > 0 && !slices.ContainsFunc(items, func(item string) bool {
			return item == "" || strings.ContainsAny(item, "\n`")
		}) {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s: `%s`\n", label, strings.Join(items, "`, `"))
			continue
		}
		value := stringArg(input, key)
		// Every key here is present: preserve explicit null separately from
		// the empty string used by optional-argument lookups.
		if input[key] == nil {
			value = "null"
		}
		if strings.ContainsAny(value, "\n`") {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s:\n%s\n", label, spi.CodeFence("text", value))
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s: `%s`\n", label, value)
		}
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
}

func formatKnownToolBody(tool *ToolInfo) string {
	switch tool.Name {
	case "run_terminal_command", "monitor":
		return formatShellBody(tool.Input)
	case "write":
		return formatWriteBody(tool.Input)
	case "search_replace":
		return formatSearchReplaceBody(tool.Input)
	case "todo_write":
		return formatTodoBody(tool.Input)
	case "spawn_subagent":
		return formatSubagentBody(tool.Input)
		}, ansi.Strip(text))
	}
	return ""
}

// stringArg reads a string argument, encoding non-string values rather than
// dropping them.
func stringArg(args map[string]any, key string) string {
	if args == nil {
		return ""
	}
	value, ok := args[key]
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	switch typed := value.(type) {
	case string:
		return typed
	case nil:
		return ""
	default:
		encoded, err := json.Marshal(typed)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Sprint(typed)
		}
		return string(encoded)
	}
}

// stringList reads a JSON array whose items are all strings. The bool is false
// for any other value, so a caller can fall back to rendering it as JSON.
func stringList(value any) ([]string, bool) {
	switch typed := value.(type) {
	case []string:
		return typed, true
	case []any:
		items := make([]string, 0, len(typed))
		for _, raw := range typed {
			item, ok := raw.(string)
			if !ok {
				return nil, false
			}
			items = append(items, item)
		}
		return items, true
	}
	return nil, false
}

// withoutKeys returns a copy of m without the named keys, leaving m intact.
func withoutKeys(m map[string]any, keys ...string) map[string]any {
	kept := make(map[string]any, len(m))
	for key, value := range m {
		if !slices.Contains(keys, key) {
			kept[key] = value
		}
	}
	return kept
}

// jsonText renders a JSON value as its literal text: strings as-is, everything
// else encoded, including null.
func jsonText(value any) string {
	if text, ok := value.(string); ok {
		return text
	}
	encoded, err := json.Marshal(value)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Sprint(value)
	}
	return string(encoded)
}

// headerText fits text to one line of a collapsed summary, marking a cut.
func headerText(text string, maxRunes int) string {
	line := strings.Join(strings.Fields(text), " ")
	count := 0
	for i := range line {
		if count == maxRunes {
			return strings.TrimRight(line[:i], " ") + "…"
		}

package spi

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// Helpers shared by provider markdown renderers. Each provider decodes its own
// native tool payload into a map[string]any of arguments and then renders those
// arguments; the rendering itself is agent-agnostic, so it lives here rather
// than being re-derived per provider.

// StringValue returns the first of keys present in args, rendered as a plain
// string, or "" when no key is present or the value has an unsupported type.
//
// The type switch is wider than json.Unmarshal can actually produce (which is
// only string, float64, bool, nil, map and slice) so that providers decoding
// with json.Decoder.UseNumber, or building argument maps by hand, get a
// sensible rendering instead of a silently empty one.
func StringValue(args map[string]any, keys ...string) string {
	for _, key := range keys {
		val, ok := args[key]
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		switch v := val.(type) {
		case string:
			return v
		case json.Number:
			return v.String()
		case fmt.Stringer:
			return v.String()
		case []byte:
			return string(v)
		case float64:
			return strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'f', -1, 64)
		case float32:
			return strconv.FormatFloat(float64(v), 'f', -1, 32)
		case int:
			return strconv.Itoa(v)
		case int64:
			return strconv.FormatInt(v, 10)
		case int32:
			return strconv.FormatInt(int64(v), 10)
		case uint:
			return strconv.FormatUint(uint64(v), 10)
		case uint64:
			return strconv.FormatUint(v, 10)
		case bool:
			return strconv.FormatBool(v)
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// NormalizeToolName reduces a tool name to a comparison key by lowercasing it
// and dropping spaces, hyphens and underscores, so that a renderer can match
// one tool whatever spelling the agent emitted ("read_file", "Read File",
}

// RenderGenericJSON is the fallback renderer for a tool whose arguments have no
// bespoke layout: it shows the raw arguments as pretty-printed JSON rather than

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-17 12:26:29Z)**_

I moved Grok's schema formatter into `spi/tool_markdown.go`, and Cursor Cloud's `get_mcp_tools` results now render as text instead of JSON.

Lint with v2.15.0 (CI's version) shows 0 issues. All tests pass, the Windows build succeeds, `./specstory` is rebuilt, and everything is staged.

## What moved into `spi`

- **`FormatInputSchema`:** the parameter list, with required parameters first, types like "array of string" and "string | null", enum values, and nested object fields.
- **Grok's three small helpers it uses:** `StringList`, `WithoutKeys` and `JSONText`, now exported. Grok used them elsewhere too, so Grok calls the `spi` versions and its own copies are gone.
- **Schema-level extras:** Grok's version rendered keys like `additionalProperties` with Grok's label map. In `spi` that's a plain `key: value` line. `additionalProperties` is the only extra key in all of Grok's data, so the output doesn't change.
- **Doubled blank line:** the old formatter printed two blank lines before those extras. I fixed it while moving the code. No Grok test or golden file changed.
- **New `TestFormatInputSchema`:** a table test covering no schema, no properties, ordering with types and enums, arrays and unions, nested objects, and extras.

## What cursorcloud does with it

`formatMCPToolsResult` (`cursorcloud/markdown_tools.go`) now handles three shapes:

| Result                  | Rendered as                                    |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| One tool's definition   | its description, then the parameter list       |
| Large-output pointer    | `Result: Large output has been written to: …`  |
| Anything else           | the JSON block, as before                      |

The `failure-run` and `tool-enumeration` golden files changed in the 8 `get_mcp_tools` results only.

## To look at

The re-sync updated two sessions in `cloud-agent-test/.specstory/history/`:

- `2026-10-16_14-34-03Z-hello-cursor-cloud-agent.md`: several lookups, including `subscribe_timer`, which has five parameters.
- `2026-10-16_14-34-06Z-verification-task-for-a.md`: the Delete and WebFetch lookups.

- **Indented lines in descriptions.** Descriptions are printed as Cursor wrote them. Delete's description has lines indented 4 spaces, which markdown joins into the paragraph above instead of showing as a list.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-17 13:46:48Z)**_

That's right, and I re-checked it against the new sessions. Cursor's API doesn't give a model for an agent or a run, so `Model` stays empty, as `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:83` documents.

Where I looked:

| Source                              | Model info?               |
|-------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `GET /v1/agents/{id}` (`agent.json`) | No                       |
| `GET /v0/agents/{id}`               | No                        |
| Run objects (`runs/*.json`)         | No                        |
| `usage.json`                        | Tokens and cost only      |
| Stream events                       | Only `modelCallId` (UUIDs) |

The only model name anywhere in the mirror showed up by accident, in `tool-enumeration-redo`. That agent called one of Cursor's own agent-management MCP tools, which returned the agent's internal record, including `"originalModelName": "claude-4.5-opus-high-thinking"`. So Cursor tracks the model internally but leaves it out of the public API. We can't rely on it, because it only appears when the agent happens to look itself up.

Two options, neither of which I'd do in this PR:

- **Record the model when we launch the agent.** Both `/v0/models` and `/v1/models` list choices, and launching accepts a model. That only helps for agents SpecStory starts itself. We only read agents, and none of our launches set a model. They ran on the account default, which is what that `originalModelName` shows.
- **Ask Cursor to add `model` to the agent or run object.** This is the real fix, and it would fit into `Model` with no other changes.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-17 13:52:07Z)**_

This is the repo filter doing its job, not a capture bug. The agent you started doesn't belong to `cloud-agent-test`. Here's its record from the API:

```
"repos": [{"url": "origin.cursor.com/git/sean-johnson/tmp-43d1a425e0e39bd7.git", "startingRef": "main"}]
```

It was started on cursor.com/agents without picking a GitHub repo, so Cursor put it in a throwaway scratch repo it hosts itself. That's why the agent said your project was blank, with just one "Initialize project" commit. SpecStory matches cloud agents to a project by git origin (`github.com/specstoryai/cloud-agent-test` here). The watcher saw this agent, found it was on another repo, and skipped it without saying anything. Both runs show FINISHED, so there was data to save.

To check that `run` works, start a new chat on that page with **specstoryai/cloud-agent-test** picked as the repository. It should appear within about 15 seconds (one poll).

The silent skip is a real usability gap, though. `run` opens the agents page, it's easy to forget to pick the repo, and nothing tells you why nothing was saved. Options:

| Option                         | Effort  | Effect                                          |
|--------------------------------|---------|-------------------------------------------------|
| 1. Say so when skipping        | Small   | Explains it the moment it happens               |
| 2. Remind at launch            | Trivial | Heads it off, but is easy to miss               |
| 3. Pre-select the repo in URL  | Unknown | Only if Cursor supports a URL parameter for it  |

1. **Say so when skipping:** during `run`/`watch`, print one line the first time the watcher sees a new agent on another repo. For example: *Skipping "Project content review": it's working on origin.cursor.com/…/tmp-….git, not github.com/specstoryai/cloud-agent-test.* Only agents created after the watch started would get this, so older agents on other repos don't flood the output.
2. **Remind at launch:** extend the "Opened https://cursor.com/agents" line to say *pick specstoryai/cloud-agent-test as the repository*.
3. **Pre-select the repo in the URL:** I haven't checked whether Cursor's page accepts a repo parameter. It would need research.

I recommend 1 and 2 together. 2 is one line of text. 1 is a small watcher change, with a test for "new agent, other repo, notice printed once". Which do you want?

pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:83:- `Model` is empty because the API does not expose it. `Usage` is nil because usage is per run, not per message. Both stay in `RawData`.
pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:84:- When a run's stream was never captured, or a finished run's capture is partial and the stream has expired, the exchange is built from the v0 conversation instead. Messages with ids `turn-N:…` belong to run index N; the first user message has a bare UUID id and belongs to turn 0. The user message takes the run's `createdAt` as its time, and agent messages have none.

pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:101:- A finished run whose events are missing or partial is replayed while it is within 24 h of its `updatedAt`. A `410` leaves the partial capture in place. A whole capture is never fetched again.
pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:102:- `sync` never attaches to an unfinished run, because reading its stream blocks until the run ends. `watch` attaches live, appends events, and rewrites the file atomically after each burst. pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:108:Same-agent resume (`specstory resume` of a cloud session into `cursorcloud`) opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>`, where a follow-up run can be started, and then watches. Resuming a cloud session into a local agent works through the shared `SessionData` flattening, from any directory: with no `OriginCwd` on the index row, resume reads the session by its mirror path (`agent.json`) through `GetAgentChatSessionByPath`.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:3:Research spike, 2026-10-06, in two phases: desk research (docs, forum, Cursor app bundle strings, local databases) followed by a hands-on spike that launched real cloud agents through the Cursor API against a throwaway repo. Covers the CLI (this repo) and the VS Code / Cursor extension (`specstory-monorepo`), which since February 2026 only wraps the CLI (`sync` then `watch`) and does no Cursor reading of its own.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:7:Cursor Cloud Agents (formerly Background Agents) run the agent loop, inference and conversation state in Cursor's cloud. The transcript is stored server-side only, "kept indefinitely", and is never written to the user's machine. SpecStory's two Cursor providers only read local stores: `cursoride` reads `globalStorage/state.vscdb` (`composerData:` / `bubbleId:`) plus `workspaceStorage`, and `cursorcli` reads `~/.cursor/chats/<md5(cwd)>/<id>/store.db`. A cloud agent launched from cursor.com/agents, Slack, GitHub, Linear, the iOS app, the API, Automations, or the `&` prefix in the CLI never touches either store, so SpecStory never sees it. This is a data-location gap, not a parsing bug. The hands-on spike confirmed every part of this: two agents, three runs, and nothing SpecStory reads was written anywhere.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:36:| Full transcript | **No conversation endpoint.** `GET /v1/agents/{id}/runs/{runId}/stream` is SSE with `id:` lines (`<ms>-<seq>`) for `Last-Event-ID` resume. Events: `status`, `assistant` (text deltas), `thinking`, `tool_call` with `args` and `result` (including `stdout` of shell commands), `interaction_update` (step, token and tool lifecycle), `result` (`durationMs`, `git.branches`), `done`. **Retention is 24 hours** (`x-cursor-stream-retention-seconds: 86400`) and a finished run replays in full from the start within that window | `GET /v0/agents/{id}/conversation` returns `{id, messages:[{id, type, text}]}` with `type` `user_message` / `assistant_message`. Text segments only: a run with 25 tool calls yielded 4 messages. Follow-up runs append to the same list. Message ids are stable across calls (`turn-0:step:22:assistant`, `turn-1:user`); the forum claim that they change did not reproduce |
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:37:| Webhooks | "coming" | `statusChange` on `FINISHED` / `ERROR` only, set at launch time, no transcript in payload |
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:38:| Usage | `GET /v1/agents/{id}/usage` returns per-run tokens and `cost.chargedCents` | none |
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:40:Cost observed: the three spike runs were billed at 43, 23 and 12 cents, so a typical short cloud run costs tens of cents. A provider that only reads data costs nothing.

The metadata socket answers `agent/id`, `agent/name`, `agent/source` (`API`), `agent/runtime` (`managed`), `turn/id` (the run id), `workspace/repo-url`, `workspace/branch-name`.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:48:- Repo hooks from `.cursor/hooks.json` do fire: `afterShellExecution` (command and output), `postToolUse` (`tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_output`), `afterAgentResponse` (the full assistant `text`), and `stop` (`generation_id` is the run id). `sessionStart` never fires. Every payload has `transcript_path: null` and `user_email: null`, with `conversation_id` set to the agent id.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:49:- `/tmp` and the working tree persist between runs of the same agent while it is `IDLE`, so a follow-up run sees files from the previous run.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:66:The user supplies a Cursor API key (`CURSOR_API_KEY` or `cursor_api_key` in `config.toml`). On `sync`, the provider lists agents, keeps those whose `repos[].url` matches the current project's origin, and for every run updated since the last sync replays the v1 stream, which within 24 hours of the run contains the complete structured transcript including tool arguments and outputs. Runs older than 24 hours fall back to the v0 conversation endpoint, which gives user and assistant text only. On `watch`, the provider polls the agent list and attaches to the stream of any active run. Markdown lands in `.specstory/history/` as usual and existing cloud sync pushes it.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:68:- Pros: covers every launch surface (web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, mobile, API). Reuses the whole provider → markdown → cloud pipeline. Works for local-only users with no SpecStory Cloud. Project attribution by repo URL is exact. Full fidelity for any run finished within the last day, which a daily `sync` or a running `watch` satisfies.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:90:- Cons: the spike showed this only exists for agents the user has opened in a window, and the search body is a flattened, HTML-escaped text blob with no structure. LevelDB/protobuf parsing is brittle. Misses most launch surfaces. Not a solution on its own.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:103:Why A: it is the only option that works for every launch surface and every user tier while reusing the existing provider, markdown and cloud-sync pipeline, so both deliverables fall out of one piece of work. The user gets history on their local machine in the repo's `.specstory/history/`, and SpecStory Cloud receives it through the sync path already in place. The spike raised A's ceiling: the 24 hour stream replay means a daily `sync` captures the full structured transcript, tool output included, without needing to be online during the run. The text-only v0 fallback only matters for runs older than a day that were never synced. Attribution by repo URL is exact and needs no cwd guessing.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:113:- Transcript source per run: v1 stream replay (primary), v0 conversation (fallback after 24 hours). Treat `tool_call` events keyed by `callId` as the tool record; `assistant` and `thinking` deltas concatenate into the message; `interaction_update` can be ignored for rendering.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:120:Method: a personal API key, a private throwaway repo `specstoryai/cloud-agent-test` connected to Cursor's GitHub app, and three runs launched with `POST /v1/agents` and `POST /v1/agents/{id}/runs`. Each run was streamed live and re-fetched after completion, and the v0 conversation was fetched twice to compare ids. _**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-17 13:53:41Z)**_

You're right. `run` from inside a project should start the agent in that project. Opening the bare agents page, where you then have to pick the repo yourself, doesn't do that.

**The browser can't do it.** I looked for a cursor.com/agents URL that pre-selects a repo. Cursor's staff said in February 2026 that this isn't possible ("Cursor doesn't currently have deeplinks that spin up a brand new agent session (and selects a repo)") and pointed people to the Cloud Agent API instead. The only URL that works opens an existing agent by id.

**The API can.** `POST /v1/agents` takes the repo and the starting branch, which is how I launched the test sessions. The catch is that the API won't create an empty agent: the launch has to include the first prompt. So `run` has to get that first prompt from you.

Options:

| Option                          | First prompt typed in | Lands in this repo |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| A. Ask for it in the terminal   | Terminal              | Always             |
| B. Prompt as an argument        | Command line          | Always             |
| C. Keep the browser flow        | Browser               | Only if you pick it |

- **A (ask in the terminal):** `run cursorcloud` asks for the first prompt, launches the agent against this project's origin and current branch, opens `cursor.com/agents/<id>` so you can follow along and send follow-ups there, and watches as it does now.
  - Pro: it does what you expected, with no setup.
  - Con: the first message is typed in the terminal, not the browser.
- **B (argument):** the same launch, but the prompt is passed on the command line, for example `specstory run cursorcloud -- "Let's do a mastermind game in Forth"`. That's good for scripts, but it's awkward for long prompts, and `run` with no prompt still needs a fallback.
- **C (browser):** keep today's flow and add a reminder to pick the repo, plus a "skipped: other repo" notice. It works, but it isn't what you expected.

I recommend A, with B's argument also accepted when given. Either way, the launch has to handle a few details:

- **Repo URL:** the API needs an `https://github.com/owner/repo` URL, so an SSH origin like yours (`git@github.com:…`) has to be converted.
- **Unpushed branch:** if the current branch isn't on the remote, Cursor can't start from it. My plan is to fall back to the default branch and say so.
- **Cost:** each launch is a paid run. That's true of the browser flow as well, so it's nothing new.

This changes how `run` works for this provider and adds code to `cursorcloud_exec.go` or a new file, so I'll wait for your call on A, B or C before writing anything.

Sources:
- [Create link to new Cursor cloud agent with repo and prompt filled out (Cursor forum)](https://forum.cursor.com/t/create-link-to-new-cursor-cloud-agent-with-repo-and-prompt-filled-out/150650)

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-17 13:56:00Z)**_

The prompt doesn't pick the repo. SpecStory does, by being the one that creates the agent.

There are two ways an agent gets created:

- **In the browser (what happens now):** `run` opens cursor.com/agents and you create the agent there. Cursor's page picks the repo. SpecStory can't tell that page which repo to use, because Cursor has no URL for it. If you don't pick one, Cursor creates a scratch repo, which is what happened.
- **Through the API (option A):** SpecStory creates the agent itself, with a request like this:

  ```json
  POST /v1/agents
  {
    "repos":  [{"url": "https://github.com/specstoryai/cloud-agent-test", "startingRef": "main"}],
    "prompt": {"text": "Howdy Mr. Cursor..."}
  }
  ```

  SpecStory fills in `repos` from the project you ran it in (its git origin and current branch). That's what guarantees the agent lands in this project.

The prompt only comes up because Cursor's API won't create an agent without a first message. Since SpecStory is creating the agent, it needs that message from you first, so A asks for it in the terminal. After that, the browser opens on the new agent, already set to this repo, and you continue there as normal.

So in A, the prompt is just what SpecStory has to send along when it creates the agent. The repo comes from the project directory.

```text
package cursorcloud

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"os/signal"
	"runtime"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/log"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// dashboardURL is where cloud agents are launched and followed.
const dashboardURL = "https://cursor.com/agents"

// ExecAgentAndWatch is `run` for a hosted agent. No local process exists, so
// it opens the cloud agents dashboard (or one agent's page when resuming) with
// the configured opener and then watches until Ctrl-C exactly like WatchAgent.
func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: starting", "projectPath", projectPath, "customCommand", customCommand, "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID, "debugRaw", debugRaw)

	target := dashboardURL
	if resumeSessionID != "" {
		if validAgentID(resumeSessionID) {
			target = dashboardURL + "/" + resumeSessionID
		} else {
			slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: ignoring malformed agent id", "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID)
		}
	}
	if err := openURL(customCommand, target); err != nil {
		// Watching still works when the browser could not be opened; the
		// user can follow the printed URL.
		slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: opening the dashboard failed", "url", target, "error", err)
		log.UserWarn("Could not open %s (%v). Open it in a browser; watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity — press Ctrl-C to stop.", target, err)
	} else {
		log.UserMessage("Opened %s — watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity, press Ctrl-C to stop.\n", target)
	}

	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()
	err := p.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
	if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		err = nil
	}
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: exiting", "error", err)
	return err
}

// openURL runs the opener with url appended. The default is the platform's
// URL handler; a custom command (cursorcloud_cmd or -c) replaces it.
func openURL(customCommand, url string) error {
	args := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
	if len(args) == 0 {
		args = defaultOpener()
	}
	if len(args) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no URL opener for %s", runtime.GOOS)
	}
	cmd := exec.Command(args[0], append(args[1:], url)...)
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: opening dashboard", "command", args[0], "url", url)
	return cmd.Run()
}

// defaultOpener is the platform's own URL handler.
func defaultOpener() []string {
	switch runtime.GOOS {
	case "darwin":
		return []string{"open"}
	case "windows":
		return []string{"rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler"}
	default:
		return []string{"xdg-open"}
	}
}

// WatchAgent polls for cloud agent activity on this project's repository and
// delivers each new or updated session until ctx is cancelled, or until the
// API refuses the agent listing permanently (rejected key, Privacy Mode), which
// is returned as an error so `run` and `watch` report it instead of hanging.
func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("WatchAgent: starting Cursor Cloud Agent polling", "projectPath", projectPath, "debugRaw", debugRaw)
	key, source := resolveAPIKey()
	if key == "" {
		slog.Info("WatchAgent: no API key configured")
		return errors.New("no Cursor API key: set CURSOR_API_KEY or cursor_api_key under [providers] in ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml")
	}
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		slog.Info("WatchAgent: project has no git origin", "projectPath", projectPath)
		return noProjectOriginError(projectPath)
	}

	watcher := newCloudWatcher(projectPath, origin, newAPIClient(key), debugRaw, sessionCallback)
	watcher.start(ctx)
	slog.Info("WatchAgent: polling", "origin", origin, "keySource", source, "mirror", watcher.mirror.root, "interval", pollInterval)

	var err error
	select {
	case <-ctx.Done():
		err = ctx.Err()
		slog.Info("WatchAgent: context cancelled, stopping")
	case err = <-watcher.fatal:
		slog.Error("WatchAgent: the API refused the agent listing; stopping", "error", err)
	}
	watcher.stop()
	slog.Info("WatchAgent: stopped")
	return err
}

package cursorcloud

import (
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

// apiKeyEnvVar is the environment variable Cursor's own tooling reads the API
// key from; it overrides the config file so a one-off key needs no edit.
const apiKeyEnvVar = "CURSOR_API_KEY"

// Settings handed in by the CLI at startup. Each is set once before any
// provider method runs, so no locking is needed.
var (
	configAPIKey        string
	configMirrorDir     string
	userDataDirOverride string
)

// SetAPIKey sets the key from `cursor_api_key` in config.toml. The
// CURSOR_API_KEY environment variable still wins when set.
func SetAPIKey(key string) {
	configAPIKey = strings.TrimSpace(key)
}

// SetMirrorDir sets the mirror location from `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` in
// config.toml (tilde-expanded). Empty keeps the project-local default.
func SetMirrorDir(dir string) {
	configMirrorDir = expandHome(strings.TrimSpace(dir))
}

// SetUserDataDirOverride sets the mirror location from
// `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>`, which wins over the config file.
func SetUserDataDirOverride(dir string) {
	userDataDirOverride = expandHome(strings.TrimSpace(dir))
}

// resolveAPIKey returns the key and where it came from ("" when none).
func resolveAPIKey() (key, source string) {
	if env := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(apiKeyEnvVar)); env != "" {
		return env, apiKeyEnvVar
	}
	if configAPIKey != "" {
		return configAPIKey, "cursor_api_key"
	}
	return "", ""
}

// mirrorFor returns the mirror for a project and whether it lives inside the
// project, which decides whether ensureRoot writes the protective .gitignore.
// The override and config locations are shared by every project and usually
// sit outside it; the default keeps each project's mirror next to its history.
// Locality is decided from the resolved path, not from which setting supplied
// it, because a configured path such as ".specstory/cursorcloud" still writes
// unredacted transcripts into the project and still needs the .gitignore.
func mirrorFor(projectPath string) (mirror, bool) {
	root := userDataDirOverride
	if root == "" {
		root = configMirrorDir
	}
	if root == "" {
		return mirror{root: filepath.Join(projectPath, ".specstory", "cursorcloud")}, true
	}
	root = canonicalMirrorRoot(root)
	return mirror{root: root}, insideProject(root, projectPath)
}

// canonicalMirrorRoot resolves a configured root to an absolute path with
// symlinks evaluated. Session refs carry mirror paths as NativePath, which must
// be absolute so a resume from another directory still finds them, and the
// locality check must see where a symlink really points. The directory may not
// exist yet (ensureRoot creates it), so the nearest existing ancestor is
// resolved and the missing tail re-appended.
func canonicalMirrorRoot(path string) string {
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(path)
	if err != nil {
		return filepath.Clean(path)
	}
	tail := ""
	for dir := abs; ; {
		if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
			return filepath.Join(spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(dir), tail)
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
		if parent == dir {
			return abs
		}
		tail = filepath.Join(filepath.Base(dir), tail)
		dir = parent
	}
}

// insideProject reports whether root, already canonical, lies strictly below
// projectPath. The project root itself does not count: a "*" .gitignore there
// would hide the whole project from git, which is worse than an unprotected
// mirror, so that misconfiguration is left to the user.
func insideProject(root, projectPath string) bool {
	if projectPath == "" {
		return false
	}
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(projectPath), root)
	if err != nil || rel == "." || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
		return false
	}
	return !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
}

// globalMirror is the mirror enumerated by reindex, which has no project: the
// shared location when one is configured, else the current project's mirror.
func globalMirror() mirror {
	if userDataDirOverride != "" || configMirrorDir != "" {
		m, _ := mirrorFor("")
		return m
	}
	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("ListAllAgentChatSessions: cannot resolve working directory", "error", err)
		return mirror{}
	}
	m, _ := mirrorFor(spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean(cwd))
	return m
}

// projectOrigin returns the normalized origin URL of the project's repository,
// or "" when the project has none. Agents are matched to projects by
// repository, because the API records a repository and never a directory.
func projectOrigin(projectPath string) string {
	origin := spi.GitOriginURL(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL(origin)
}

// agentMatchesOrigin reports whether any of the agent's repositories is the
// project's origin. Case is ignored because GitHub and GitLab treat owner and
// repository names case-insensitively, so a clone's origin and the URL Cursor
// records can differ only in case and still name the same repository.
func agentMatchesOrigin(agent apiAgent, origin string) bool {
	if origin == "" {
		return false
	}
	for _, repo := range agent.Repos {
		if strings.EqualFold(spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL(repo.URL), origin) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// workspaceRootFor is the SessionData workspace root: the caller's project,
// else the process working directory as the documented last resort.
func workspaceRootFor(projectPath string) string {
	if projectPath != "" {
		return projectPath
	}
	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		return cwd
	}
	return "."
}

// expandHome expands a leading ~ so config and flag values can use it.
func expandHome(path string) string {
	if path != "~" && !strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") && !strings.HasPrefix(path, `~\`) {
		return path
	}
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return path
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, strings.TrimLeft(path[1:], `/\`))
}

package cursorcloud

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Network constants.
const (
	defaultAPIBaseURL = "https://api.cursor.com"
	jsonTimeout       = 30 * time.Second
	maxRetries        = 4
	maxBackoff        = 60 * time.Second
	// listPageSize is the API's maximum page size for GET /v1/agents.
	listPageSize = 100
)

// initialBackoff is the first retry delay after a 5xx, 429 or transport
// failure, doubling up to maxBackoff. A variable so tests can shorten it.
var initialBackoff = 5 * time.Second

// apiBaseURL is a variable so tests can point the client at an httptest server.
var apiBaseURL = defaultAPIBaseURL

// streamIdleTimeout bounds how long a stream read may see no bytes before the
// connection is treated as dead. The live stream sends a heartbeat event while
// the agent is quiet, so 90 seconds of silence means the connection is gone.
// A variable so tests can shorten it.
var streamIdleTimeout = 90 * time.Second

// errStreamExpired reports a 410 from the run stream endpoint: the stream is
// retained for 24 hours after a run ends and is gone afterwards.
var errStreamExpired = errors.New("run stream expired")

// apiError is a non-success HTTP response from the Cloud Agents API, carrying
// the error envelope the API returns ({"error":{"code","message"}}).
}

// sharedThrottle is the process-wide hold shared by every client.
var sharedThrottle = newThrottle()

// apiClient talks to the Cloud Agents API with one key.
type apiClient struct {
	key        string
	baseURL    string
	jsonHTTP   *http.Client
	streamHTTP *http.Client
	throttle   *throttle
}

// newAPIClient builds a client for key. JSON calls carry a whole-request
// timeout; stream calls cannot (a live run streams for minutes), so they rely
// on the idle deadline in openStream for the body and on streamTransport for
// the headers.
func newAPIClient(key string) *apiClient {
	return &apiClient{
		key:        key,
		baseURL:    apiBaseURL,
		jsonHTTP:   &http.Client{Timeout: jsonTimeout},
		streamHTTP: &http.Client{Transport: streamTransport()},
		throttle:   sharedThrottle,
	}
}

// streamTransport is the default transport with a response-header deadline. The
// idle reader only guards the body after Do returns, so without this a server
// that accepts the connection and never answers would hang a replay forever.
func streamTransport() *http.Transport {
	tr := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
	tr.ResponseHeaderTimeout = jsonTimeout
	return tr
}

// do sends one request built by build, waiting out any hold first and
// retrying 429 and 5xx responses after the server's requested delay or
// exponential backoff.
// Transport failures (DNS, connection reset, timeout) take the same backoff,
// because every request here is an idempotent GET and a sync that gave up on
// one agent over a blip would leave it stale until the next run. A cancelled
// context is never retried. A 2xx response is returned open; any other status
// is returned as *apiError.
func (c *apiClient) do(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client, build func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error)) (*http.Response, error) {
	backoff := initialBackoff
	for attempt := 0; ; attempt++ {
		if err := c.throttle.wait(ctx); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		req, err := build(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.key)
		resp, err := httpClient.Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			if ctx.Err() != nil || attempt >= maxRetries {
				return nil, err
			}
			delay := backoff
			backoff = min(backoff*2, maxBackoff)
			slog.Warn("Cursor API request failed, retrying",
				"path", req.URL.Path, "error", err, "delay", delay, "attempt", attempt+1)
			c.throttle.holdUntil(c.throttle.now().Add(delay))
			continue
		}
		if resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300 {
			return resp, nil
		}

		apiErr := readAPIError(resp)
		retryable := resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests || resp.StatusCode >= 500
		if !retryable || attempt >= maxRetries {
			return nil, apiErr
		}

		delay := retryAfter(resp.Header, c.throttle.now())
		if delay <= 0 {
			delay = backoff
			backoff = min(backoff*2, maxBackoff)
		}
		slog.Warn("Cursor API request throttled or failed, retrying",
			"path", req.URL.Path, "status", resp.StatusCode, "delay", delay, "attempt", attempt+1)
		c.throttle.holdUntil(c.throttle.now().Add(delay))
	}
}

// readAPIError drains and closes resp, decoding the API's error envelope.
func readAPIError(resp *http.Response) *apiError {
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
	apiErr := &apiError{Status: resp.StatusCode}
	// The error envelope is small; the cap only guards against a proxy page.
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 64*1024))
	var envelope struct {
		Error struct {
			Code    string `json:"code"`
			Message string `json:"message"`
		} `json:"error"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &envelope) == nil {
		apiErr.Code = envelope.Error.Code
		apiErr.Message = envelope.Error.Message
	}
	return apiErr
}

// retryAfter returns how long the server asked the client to wait: Retry-After
// (delay-seconds or an HTTP date), else X-RateLimit-Reset, else zero. The
// OpenAPI document promises both headers on a 429 without saying whether the
// reset is seconds from now or a Unix time, so a value too large to be a delay
// is read as a Unix time. The delay is capped at maxBackoff: holdUntil pauses
// every caller in the process, so an outsized value (or a skewed clock) would
// otherwise stall sync and watch for as long as the header says. Retrying
// early costs one more 429 at most.
func retryAfter(h http.Header, now time.Time) time.Duration {
	var delay time.Duration
	if header := h.Get("Retry-After"); header != "" {
		if secs, err := strconv.Atoi(header); err == nil && secs > 0 {
			delay = time.Duration(secs) * time.Second
		} else if t, err := http.ParseTime(header); err == nil {
			delay = t.Sub(now)
		}
	} else if secs, err := strconv.ParseInt(h.Get("X-RateLimit-Reset"), 10, 64); err == nil && secs > 0 {
		if secs > unixTimeThreshold {
			delay = time.Unix(secs, 0).Sub(now)
		} else {
			delay = time.Duration(secs) * time.Second
		}
	}
	return min(delay, maxBackoff)
}

// unixTimeThreshold separates a reset given as seconds from now from one given
// as a Unix time: no server asks for a delay of a billion seconds.
const unixTimeThreshold = 1_000_000_000

// FindGitRoot walks up from dir to the nearest ancestor containing a .git entry and
// returns it. The .git entry may be a directory (normal clone) or a file (git
// worktree or submodule); both satisfy the search. Returns false if no .git is
// found before the filesystem root.
func FindGitRoot(dir string) (string, bool) {
	if abs, err := filepath.Abs(dir); err == nil {
		dir = abs
	}
	dir = filepath.Clean(dir)
	for {
		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); err == nil {
			return dir, true
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
		if parent == dir {
			return "", false
		}
		dir = parent
	}
}

// readOriginURL returns the origin remote URL from a git config file, or "" if the
// file is unreadable or has no origin remote.
func readOriginURL(gitConfigPath string) string {
	gitConfig, err := os.ReadFile(gitConfigPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	matches := originRemoteURLRegex.FindSubmatch(gitConfig)
	if len(matches) < 2 {
		return ""
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(matches[1]))
}

// gitConfigPath returns the path to the git config file that holds a root's
// remotes, handling both a normal .git directory and a .git file (worktrees and
// submodules, whose private gitdir points at a commondir that holds the shared
// config). Returns "" when it cannot be resolved.
func gitConfigPath(gitRoot string) string {
	gitPath := filepath.Join(gitRoot, ".git")
	info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	if info.IsDir() {
		return filepath.Join(gitPath, "config")
	}

	// A .git file reads "gitdir: <path>" and points at the worktree's private git
	// dir; the shared config lives in the common dir, not that private dir.
	data, err := os.ReadFile(gitPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
	if !strings.HasPrefix(content, "gitdir:") {
		return ""
	}
	gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(content, "gitdir:"))
	if gitDir == "" {
		return ""
	}
	if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
		gitDir = filepath.Join(gitRoot, gitDir)
	}
	commonDir := gitDir
	if cd, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(gitDir, "commondir")); err == nil {
		c := strings.TrimSpace(string(cd))
		if !filepath.IsAbs(c) {
			c = filepath.Join(gitDir, c)
		}
		commonDir = filepath.Clean(c)
	}
	return filepath.Join(commonDir, "config")
}

// buildSessionData converts a mirrored agent into SessionData. It returns nil
// when no run yields a user prompt, which means there is nothing to save yet.
func buildSessionData(snap *agentSnapshot, workspaceRoot string) (*schema.SessionData, string) {
	agent := snap.agent
	data := &schema.SessionData{
		SchemaVersion: schema.CurrentSchemaVersion,
		// The API exposes no agent version, so the honest value is "unknown".
		Provider:      schema.ProviderInfo{ID: ProviderID, Name: providerName, Version: "unknown"},
		SessionID:     agent.ID,
		CreatedAt:     agent.CreatedAt,
		UpdatedAt:     agent.UpdatedAt,
		WorkspaceRoot: workspaceRoot,
		Exchanges:     []schema.Exchange{},
	}

	conv := alignedConversation(snap)
	firstPrompt := ""
	textOnly := 0
	for i, run := range snap.runs {
		exchange := buildExchange(snap, conv, i, run, workspaceRoot)
		if exchange == nil {
			continue
		}
		if firstPrompt == "" {
			firstPrompt = firstUserText(exchange)
		}
		if exchange.Metadata["source"] == v0Source {
			textOnly++
		}
		data.Exchanges = append(data.Exchanges, *exchange)
	}
	if firstPrompt == "" {
		return nil, ""
	}
	if note := textOnlyNote(textOnly, len(data.Exchanges)); note != "" {
		data.Notes = []string{note}
	}
	data.Slug = spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(firstPrompt)
	return data, firstPrompt
}

// buildExchange builds one run's exchange. The stream is the full-fidelity
// source; the v0 conversation conv (text only, nil when unusable) fills in when
// the stream is missing, or when a finished run's capture is partial and the
// stream has since expired.
				return part.Text
			}
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// sessionName prefers the agent's own name (Cursor sets one, derived from the
// prompt when the launcher gave none) over the shared generator.
func sessionName(agent apiAgent, firstPrompt string) string {
	if name := strings.TrimSpace(agent.Name); name != "" {
		return name
	}
	return spi.GenerateReadableName(firstPrompt)
}

This provides the same support for saving to local markdown files and to the SpecStory Cloud as for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/docs/api/claude-code), [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli), [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), Factory's [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli), [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/product), Google's [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/), [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI), [VS Code Copilot](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/copilot), [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/), [Pi](https://pi.dev), [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code), [Grok Build](https://x.ai/cli) and [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/).
specstory-cli/changelog.md:8:- Cloud agent conversations are never written to your machine, so SpecStory reads them from the Cursor API with your Cursor API key (`CURSOR_API_KEY`, or `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]` in `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`) and matches agents to your project by its git `origin`. The Cursor API serves full transcripts, including tool calls and their output, for only 24 hours after a run finishes; after that it returns only the conversation text. `specstory run cursorcloud` opens cursor.com/agents and saves sessions as your agents work.

specstory-cli/README.md:47:Cursor Cloud Agents run in Cursor's backend, and their conversations are never written to your machine. The `cursorcloud` provider reads them from the [Cloud Agents API](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints) with your Cursor API key (create one at https://cursor.com/dashboard/api, then set `CURSOR_API_KEY` or `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]`). Agents are matched to the current project by repository: an agent belongs to the project when one of its repositories is the project's git `origin`. The provider keeps a local mirror of what it has read in `.specstory/cursorcloud/` (it writes its own `.gitignore` there, because the mirror holds unredacted transcripts); `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` moves it. A finished run's full transcript, including tool calls and output, is available from the API for 24 hours; after that only its text remains, so sync at least daily or keep `specstory watch` running. `specstory run cursorcloud` opens https://cursor.com/agents in your browser and then watches until interrupted with `ctrl-c`. Resuming another agent's session into a cloud agent is not supported, because that would launch a new paid run; cloud sessions can be resumed into local agents.

specstory-cli/docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:7:Cursor Cloud Agents (formerly Background Agents) run the agent loop, inference and conversation state in Cursor's cloud. The transcript is stored server-side only, "kept indefinitely", and is never written to the user's machine. SpecStory's two Cursor providers only read local stores: `cursoride` reads `globalStorage/state.vscdb` (`composerData:` / `bubbleId:`) plus `workspaceStorage`, and `cursorcli` reads `~/.cursor/chats/<md5(cwd)>/<id>/store.db`. A cloud agent launched from cursor.com/agents, Slack, GitHub, Linear, the iOS app, the API, Automations, or the `&` prefix in the CLI never touches either store, so SpecStory never sees it. This is a data-location gap, not a parsing bug. The hands-on spike confirmed every part of this: two agents, three runs, and nothing SpecStory reads was written anywhere.

// writeGitConfig creates dir/.git/config naming origin, returning dir.
func writeGitConfig(t *testing.T, dir, origin string) string {
	t.Helper()
	gitDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".git")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(gitDir, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	config := "[core]\n\tbare = false\n"
	if origin != "" {
		config += "[remote \"origin\"]\n\turl = " + origin + "\n\tfetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*\n"
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(gitDir, "config"), []byte(config), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return dir
}

func TestGitOriginURL(t *testing.T) {
	const origin = "git@github.com:specstoryai/cloud-agent-test.git"

	t.Run("repository root", func(t *testing.T) {
		root := writeGitConfig(t, t.TempDir(), origin)
		if got := GitOriginURL(root); got != origin {
			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want %q", got, origin)
		}
	})

	t.Run("subdirectory walks up to the root", func(t *testing.T) {
		root := writeGitConfig(t, t.TempDir(), origin)
		sub := filepath.Join(root, "a", "b")
		if err := os.MkdirAll(sub, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if got := GitOriginURL(sub); got != origin {
			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want %q", got, origin)
		}
	})

	t.Run("worktree .git file follows commondir", func(t *testing.T) {
		main := writeGitConfig(t, filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "main"), origin)
		private := filepath.Join(main, ".git", "worktrees", "wt")
		if err := os.MkdirAll(private, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(private, "commondir"), []byte("../..\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		worktree := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "wt")
		if err := os.MkdirAll(worktree, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(worktree, ".git"), []byte("gitdir: "+private+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if got := GitOriginURL(worktree); got != origin {
			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want %q", got, origin)
		}
	})

	t.Run("no origin remote", func(t *testing.T) {
		root := writeGitConfig(t, t.TempDir(), "")
		if got := GitOriginURL(root); got != "" {
			t.Errorf("GitOriginURL = %q, want empty", got)
		}
	})
}

// dir, or "" when HEAD is detached, unreadable, or dir is not in a repository.
func GitHeadBranch(dir string) string {
	root, ok := FindGitRoot(dir)
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	// HEAD is per worktree, so it lives in the private dir, not the common one.
	private, _ := gitDirs(root)
	if private == "" {
		return ""
	}
	head, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(private, "HEAD"))
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	branch, _ := strings.CutPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(string(head)), "ref: refs/heads/")
	if branch == strings.TrimSpace(string(head)) {
		// A detached HEAD holds a commit id, not a ref.
		return ""
	}
	return branch
}

// gitConfigPath returns the path to the git config file that holds a root's
// remotes, or "" when it cannot be resolved. The config is shared by every
// worktree, so it lives in the common dir.
func gitConfigPath(gitRoot string) string {
	_, common := gitDirs(gitRoot)
	if common == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return filepath.Join(common, "config")
}

// gitDirs returns a root's private git dir, which holds per-worktree state such
// as HEAD, and its common dir, which holds the shared config. They are the same
// .git directory in a normal clone; a .git file (worktrees and submodules)
// points at a private gitdir whose commondir names the shared one. Both are ""
// when they cannot be resolved.
func gitDirs(gitRoot string) (private, common string) {
	gitPath := filepath.Join(gitRoot, ".git")
	info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", ""
	}
	if info.IsDir() {
		return gitPath, gitPath
	}

	// A .git file reads "gitdir: <path>" and points at the private git dir.
	data, err := os.ReadFile(gitPath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", ""
	}
	content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
	if !strings.HasPrefix(content, "gitdir:") {
		return "", ""
	}
	gitDir := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(content, "gitdir:"))
	if gitDir == "" {
		return "", ""
	}
	if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
		gitDir = filepath.Join(gitRoot, gitDir)
	}
	commonDir := gitDir
	if cd, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(gitDir, "commondir")); err == nil {
		c := strings.TrimSpace(string(cd))
		if !filepath.IsAbs(c) {
			c = filepath.Join(gitDir, c)
		}
		commonDir = filepath.Clean(c)
	}
	return gitDir, commonDir
}
'''

// launchAgent creates a cloud agent, which starts its first (paid) run at once.
func (c *apiClient) launchAgent(ctx context.Context, launch launchRequest) (apiAgent, error) {
	body, err := json.Marshal(launch)
	if err != nil {
		return apiAgent{}, err
	}
	resp, err := c.do(ctx, c.jsonHTTP, func(ctx context.Context) (*http.Request, error) {
		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, c.baseURL+"/v1/agents", bytes.NewReader(body))
		if err == nil {
			req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		}
		return req, err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return apiAgent{}, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
	raw, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		return apiAgent{}, fmt.Errorf("read launch response: %w", err)
	}
	// The created agent may come wrapped as {"agent": {...}, ...} or bare.
	var wrapped struct {
		Agent json.RawMessage `json:"agent"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(raw, &wrapped) == nil && len(wrapped.Agent) > 0 {
		raw = wrapped.Agent
	}
	var agent apiAgent
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &agent); err != nil {
		return apiAgent{}, fmt.Errorf("decode launch response: %w", err)
	}
	if !validAgentID(agent.ID) {
		return apiAgent{}, fmt.Errorf("launch response has no valid agent id (%q)", agent.ID)
	}
	return agent, nil
}

'''

func writeAPIError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, code, message string) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{"error": map[string]string{"code": code, "message": message}})
}

// useSettings isolates the provider's package settings and key for one test.
func useSettings(t *testing.T, envKey string) {
	t.Helper()
	t.Setenv(apiKeyEnvVar, envKey)
	prevKey, prevMirror, prevOverride := configAPIKey, configMirrorDir, userDataDirOverride
	configAPIKey, configMirrorDir, userDataDirOverride = "", "", ""
	t.Cleanup(func() { configAPIKey, configMirrorDir, userDataDirOverride = prevKey, prevMirror, prevOverride })
}

// fakeClock drives a throttle deterministically: sleeping advances time.
type fakeClock struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	now   time.Time
	slept []time.Duration
}

func (c *fakeClock) Now() time.Time {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return c.now
}

func (c *fakeClock) Sleep(_ context.Context, d time.Duration) error {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	c.slept = append(c.slept, d)
	c.now = c.now.Add(d)
	return nil
}

// TestThrottleHoldsOnlyAfterPushback: requests are not paced in advance, and a
// hold set by one caller's 429 delays the next request from any caller.
func TestThrottleHoldsOnlyAfterPushback(t *testing.T) {
	clock := &fakeClock{now: time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0)}
	throttle := &throttle{now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

	for range 3 {
		if err := throttle.wait(context.Background()); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if len(clock.slept) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("unthrottled requests slept %v", clock.slept)
	}

	throttle.holdUntil(clock.Now().Add(20 * time.Second))
	for range 2 {
		if err := throttle.wait(context.Background()); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if len(clock.slept) != 1 || clock.slept[0] != 20*time.Second {
		t.Errorf("after holdUntil slept %v, want [20s] and then no further wait", clock.slept)
	}
}

func TestClientRetriesThrottledRequests(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		status    int
		headers   map[string]string
		wantDelay time.Duration
	}{
		{"429 with Retry-After seconds", http.StatusTooManyRequests, map[string]string{"Retry-After": "7"}, 7 * time.Second},
		{"429 without Retry-After backs off", http.StatusTooManyRequests, nil, initialBackoff},
		{"429 with Retry-After date", http.StatusTooManyRequests, map[string]string{"Retry-After": time.Unix(1_800_000_010, 0).UTC().Format(http.TimeFormat)}, 10 * time.Second},
		// holdUntil pauses every caller, so an outsized value must not stall the process.
		{"429 with outsized Retry-After is capped", http.StatusTooManyRequests, map[string]string{"Retry-After": "3600"}, maxBackoff},
		{"429 with unparseable Retry-After backs off", http.StatusTooManyRequests, map[string]string{"Retry-After": "soon"}, initialBackoff},
		{"429 with reset in seconds", http.StatusTooManyRequests, map[string]string{"X-RateLimit-Reset": "12"}, 12 * time.Second},
		{"429 with reset as a Unix time", http.StatusTooManyRequests, map[string]string{"X-RateLimit-Reset": "1800000015"}, 15 * time.Second},
		{"Retry-After wins over reset", http.StatusTooManyRequests, map[string]string{"Retry-After": "4", "X-RateLimit-Reset": "30"}, 4 * time.Second},
		{"503 retried", http.StatusServiceUnavailable, nil, initialBackoff},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			calls := 0
			server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
				calls++
				if calls == 1 {
					for k, v := range tt.headers {
						w.Header().Set(k, v)
					}
					writeAPIError(w, tt.status, "rate_limited", "slow down")
					return
				}
				_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"apiKeyName":"k"}`))
			}))
			defer server.Close()

			clock := &fakeClock{now: time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0)}
			c := newAPIClient("test-key")
			c.baseURL = server.URL
			c.throttle = &throttle{now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

			me, err := c.me(context.Background())
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("me: %v", err)
			}
			if me.KeyLabel != "k" || calls != 2 {
				t.Errorf("got key %q after %d calls, want k after 2", me.KeyLabel, calls)
			}
			if len(clock.slept) != 1 || clock.slept[0] != tt.wantDelay {
				t.Errorf("slept %v, want [%v]", clock.slept, tt.wantDelay)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestClientRetriesTransportErrors closes the socket without a response on the
// first attempt, which the client sees as a transport error rather than a status.
func TestClientRetriesTransportErrors(t *testing.T) {
	calls := 0
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		calls++
		if calls == 1 {
			conn, _, err := w.(http.Hijacker).Hijack()
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("hijack: %v", err)
				return
			}
			_ = conn.Close()
			return
		}
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"apiKeyName":"k"}`))
	}))
	defer server.Close()

	clock := &fakeClock{now: time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0)}
	c := newAPIClient("test-key")
	c.baseURL = server.URL
	c.throttle = &throttle{now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

	me, err := c.me(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("me: %v", err)
	}
	if me.KeyLabel != "k" || calls != 2 {
		t.Errorf("got key %q after %d calls, want k after 2", me.KeyLabel, calls)
	}
	if len(clock.slept) != 1 || clock.slept[0] != initialBackoff {
		t.Errorf("slept %v, want [%v]", clock.slept, initialBackoff)
	}
}

// TestClientDoesNotRetryCancelledContext checks that a transport error caused by
// the caller giving up is returned at once instead of being backed off.
func TestClientDoesNotRetryCancelledContext(t *testing.T) {
	calls := 0
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		calls++
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"apiKeyName":"k"}`))
	}))
	defer server.Close()

	clock := &fakeClock{now: time.Unix(1_800_000_000, 0)}
	c := newAPIClient("test-key")
	c.baseURL = server.URL
	c.throttle = &throttle{now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	_, err := c.me(ctx)
	if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want context.Canceled", err)
	}
	if calls != 0 || len(clock.slept) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("calls = %d, slept %v; want no request and no backoff", calls, clock.slept)
	}
}

func TestClientGivesUpAfterMaxRetries(t *testing.T) {
	calls := 0
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		calls++
		writeAPIError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "rate_limited", "slow down")

	c.baseURL = server.URL
	c.throttle = &throttle{now: clock.Now, sleep: clock.Sleep}

	_, err := c.me(context.Background())
	var ae *apiError
	if !errors.As(err, &ae) || ae.Status != http.StatusTooManyRequests {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want a 429 apiError", err)
	}
	if calls != maxRetries+1 {
		t.Errorf("calls = %d, want %d", calls, maxRetries+1)
	}
}

// dashboardURL/<id>.
const dashboardURL = "https://cursor.com/agents"

// launchName names every agent `run` starts. Cursor would otherwise name the
// agent after launchPromptText, which says nothing about the session, so the
// session title comes from the user's first real prompt instead (sessionName).
const launchName = "SpecStory session"

// launchPromptText opens every agent `run` starts. The API cannot create an
// agent without a prompt, and this one keeps the paid first run short: no
// tools, just a greeting, so the user takes over in the browser.
const launchPromptText = "Session started by SpecStory. Don't read files or run any tools yet. Briefly greet the user and ask what they'd like to work on."

// ExecAgentAndWatch is `run` for a hosted agent. No local process exists, so it
// starts a cloud agent on this project's repository (or, when resuming, uses
// that agent), opens the agent's page with the configured opener, and then
// watches until Ctrl-C exactly like WatchAgent.
func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: starting", "projectPath", projectPath, "customCommand", customCommand, "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID, "debugRaw", debugRaw)

	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()

	agentID := resumeSessionID
	if agentID == "" {
		agent, err := launchSession(ctx, projectPath)
		if err != nil {
			slog.Error("ExecAgentAndWatch: launch failed", "error", err)
			return fmt.Errorf("could not start a Cursor Cloud Agent: %w", err)
		}
		agentID = agent.ID
	} else if !validAgentID(agentID) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%q is not a Cursor Cloud Agent id", agentID)
	}

	target := dashboardURL + "/" + agentID
	if err := openURL(customCommand, target); err != nil {
		// Watching still works when the browser could not be opened; the
		// user can follow the printed URL.
		slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: opening the agent page failed", "url", target, "error", err)
		log.UserWarn("Could not open %s (%v). Open it in a browser; watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity — press Ctrl-C to stop.", target, err)
	} else {
		log.UserMessage("Opened %s — watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity, press Ctrl-C to stop.\\n", target)
	}

	err := p.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
	if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		err = nil
	}
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: exiting", "error", err)
	return err
}

// launchSession starts a cloud agent on the project's repository and current
// branch. Cursor's agents page cannot be told which repository to use, so an
// agent started there lands wherever the user picks, or in a scratch
// repository when they pick none; launching through the API is the only way
// to guarantee the agent works on, and is saved to, this project.
func launchSession(ctx context.Context, projectPath string) (apiAgent, error) {
	key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
	if key == "" {
		return apiAgent{}, errNoAPIKey
	}
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		return apiAgent{}, noProjectOriginError(projectPath)
	}
	// The API takes an HTTPS URL, while the origin may be SSH; the normalized
	// host/owner/repo form is the same for both.
	repoURL := "https://" + origin
	branch := spi.GitHeadBranch(projectPath)
	client := newAPIClient(key)

	slog.Info("launchSession: launching", "repo", repoURL, "branch", branch)
	agent, err := client.launchAgent(ctx, newLaunchRequest(repoURL, branch))
	if branch != "" && isUnknownBranch(err) {
		log.UserWarn("Branch %s is not on %s, so the agent starts from the default branch. Push the branch to start from it.", branch, origin)
		branch = ""
		agent, err = client.launchAgent(ctx, newLaunchRequest(repoURL, branch))
	}
	if err != nil {
		return apiAgent{}, err
	}
	analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCursorCloudAgentLaunched, analytics.Properties{"has_branch": branch != ""})
	slog.Info("launchSession: launched", "agentID", agent.ID, "branch", branch)
	return agent, nil
}

// newLaunchRequest is the launch body for repoURL; an empty branch starts the
// agent from the repository's default branch.
func newLaunchRequest(repoURL, branch string) launchRequest {
	return launchRequest{
		Name:   launchName,
		Prompt: launchPrompt{Text: launchPromptText},
		Repos:  []launchRepo{{URL: repoURL, StartingRef: branch}},
	}
}

// isUnknownBranch reports the launch refusal for a branch the remote does not
// have (an unpushed local branch). Cursor validates the branch before creating
// the agent, so nothing was started or billed, and the launch can be retried
// from the default branch. The API has no dedicated code for this, so the
// validation message is matched.
func isUnknownBranch(err error) bool {
	var apiErr *apiError
	if !errors.As(err, &apiErr) || apiErr.Status != http.StatusBadRequest {
		return false
	}
	return apiErr.Code == "validation_error" && strings.HasPrefix(apiErr.Message, "Branch ") && strings.Contains(apiErr.Message, "does not exist")
}

package cursorcloud

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

var updateGolden = flag.Bool("update", false, "rewrite golden session-data files")

// testWorkspace is the project root used for golden output. It is POSIX
// shaped on every OS because path hints are computed by shape.
const testWorkspace = "/project"

// snapshotFromFixture mirrors a fixture into a temp dir and reads it back,
// exercising the same read path the provider uses.
func snapshotFromFixture(t *testing.T, name string) *agentSnapshot {
	t.Helper()
	fx := loadFixture(t, name)
	m := mirror{root: t.TempDir()}
	writeFixtureMirror(t, m, fx)
	snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(m.agentDir(fx.agent.agent.ID))
	if err != nil || snap == nil {
		t.Fatalf("load snapshot: %v", err)
	}
	return snap
}

func marshalSession(t *testing.T, data *schema.SessionData) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	out, err := json.MarshalIndent(data, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return append(out, '\n')
}

func TestBuildSessionDataGolden(t *testing.T) {
	for _, name := range []string{"fixture-run", "tool-enumeration", "failure-run"} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			snap := snapshotFromFixture(t, name)
			data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)
			if data == nil {
				t.Fatal("no session built")
			}
			if !data.Validate() {
				t.Error("session data failed schema validation")
			}
			got := marshalSession(t, data)

			// A second build of the same snapshot must change no bytes.
			again, _ := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)
			if !bytes.Equal(got, marshalSession(t, again)) {
				t.Error("a second build produced different output")
			}

			golden := filepath.Join("testdata", name, "session-data.golden.json")
			if *updateGolden {
				if err := os.WriteFile(golden, got, 0o644); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
			want, err := os.ReadFile(golden)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read golden (run with -update to create): %v", err)
			}
			if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
				t.Errorf("session data differs from %s; run with -update after checking the change\n%s", golden, firstDifference(got, want))
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBuildSessionDataStructure(t *testing.T) {
	snap := snapshotFromFixture(t, "failure-run")
	data, firstPrompt := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)

	if len(data.Exchanges) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d exchanges, want one per run", len(data.Exchanges))
	}
	if data.Exchanges[0].ExchangeID != "run-ec41805a-07c4-4c80-874f-f077b9877582" {
		t.Errorf("first exchange is %s, want the earlier run first", data.Exchanges[0].ExchangeID)
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(firstPrompt, "Verification task for a transcript parser") {
		t.Errorf("first prompt = %q", firstPrompt)
	}
	if data.Slug != "verification-task-for-a" {
		t.Errorf("slug = %q", data.Slug)
	}
	if data.Provider.Version != "unknown" || data.Provider.ID != ProviderID {
		t.Errorf("provider = %+v", data.Provider)
	}

	first := data.Exchanges[0]
	if first.Messages[0].Role != schema.RoleUser || first.Messages[0].Timestamp != "2026-10-13T16:30:30.790Z" {
		t.Errorf("first message = %+v, want the user prompt stamped from its event id", first.Messages[0])
	}
	// The run opens with thinking then text, sharing one agent message.
	if parts := first.Messages[1].Content; len(parts) != 2 || parts[0].Type != schema.ContentTypeThinking || parts[1].Type != schema.ContentTypeText {
		t.Errorf("second message parts = %+v, want thinking then text", parts)
	}
	if first.Metadata["branch"] != "cursor/specstory-failure-capture-1e05" || first.Metadata["agentUrl"] == nil {
		t.Errorf("metadata = %+v", first.Metadata)
	}
	// The result event duplicates the final text; it must appear once.
	final := "Completed all six verification steps"
	count := 0
	for _, msg := range first.Messages {
		for _, part := range msg.Content {
			count += strings.Count(part.Text, final)
		}
	}
	if count != 1 {
		t.Errorf("final text rendered %d times, want once", count)
	}
}

func TestV0FallbackForExpiredPartialRun(t *testing.T) {
	snap := snapshotFromFixture(t, "failure-run")
	// Truncate the second run's capture as if the watcher stopped mid-run and
	// the stream expired before a sync could replay it.
	snap.runs[1].events = snap.runs[1].events[:40]
	// And drop the first run's capture entirely.
	snap.runs[0].events = nil

	data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)
	for i, ex := range data.Exchanges {
		if ex.Metadata["source"] != v0Source {
			t.Errorf("exchange %d source = %v, want v0-conversation", i, ex.Metadata["source"])
		}
	}
	first := data.Exchanges[0]
	// Turn 0 starts with the agent's first user message, whose id is a bare UUID.
	if first.Messages[0].ID != "cde498a2-37da-4b54-b81f-82bc82341d4b" || first.Messages[0].Role != schema.RoleUser {
		t.Errorf("turn 0 first message = %+v", first.Messages[0])
	}
	if len(first.Messages) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("turn 0 has %d messages, want 3", len(first.Messages))
	}
	second := data.Exchanges[1]
	if second.Messages[0].ID != "turn-1:user" || len(second.Messages) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("turn 1 messages = %+v", second.Messages)
	}
	// The missing tool calls are explained once, for the whole session.
	if want := []string{textOnlyNote(2, 2)}; !slices.Equal(data.Notes, want) {
		t.Errorf("notes = %q, want %q", data.Notes, want)
	}
	for _, msg := range append(first.Messages, second.Messages...) {
		if msg.Tool != nil {
			t.Error("the v0 fallback is text only")
		}
	}
}

// so a run missing from the mirror would hand turn 0's text to what is really
// run 1. The partial stream must be kept instead.
func TestV0FallbackSkippedWhenARunIsMissing(t *testing.T) {
	snap := snapshotFromFixture(t, "failure-run")
	snap.runs = snap.runs[1:]
	snap.runs[0].events = snap.runs[0].events[:40]

	data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, testWorkspace)

	}
	ex := data.Exchanges[0]
	if ex.Metadata["source"] == v0Source {
		t.Error("v0 text used although its turns no longer line up with the runs")
	}

			t.Error("turn 0's first prompt was attributed to run 1")
		}
	}
}

// replaceUserPrompt rewrites the run's prompt event to text.
func replaceUserPrompt(t *testing.T, events []sseEvent, text string) {
	t.Helper()
	for i, ev := range events {
		if ev.Event != "interaction_update" || !bytes.Contains(ev.Data, []byte(`"user-message-appended"`)) {
			continue
		}

		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		events[i].Data = data
		return
	}
	t.Fatal("no user-message-appended event in the run")
}

- An agent directory without `agent.json` is not an agent yet. Readers skip it.

## Resume

Same-agent resume (`specstory resume` of a cloud session into `cursorcloud`) opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>`, where a follow-up run can be started, and then watches. Resuming another agent's session into `cursorcloud` is unsupported: the only way to create a cloud agent conversation is to launch a new paid run, so `ReconstructSession` returns `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`. Resuming a cloud session into a local agent works through the shared `SessionData` flattening, from any directory: with no `OriginCwd` on the index row, resume reads the session by its mirror path (`agent.json`) through `GetAgentChatSessionByPath`.
```

The API cannot create an agent without a prompt, so the agent is named `SpecStory session` and opens with a fixed no-tools greeting; both are skipped when choosing the session title and slug, and an agent with only the greeting yields no session yet. A launch is never resent after a 5xx or a transport failure, because the first attempt may already have started a paid run. `run` then opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>` and watches.

// convertSnapshot builds the session, its RawData and, when asked, the
// native debug export, all from one snapshot.
func convertSnapshot(snap *agentSnapshot, projectPath string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
	data, _ := buildSessionData(snap, workspaceRootFor(projectPath))
	if data == nil {
		slog.Debug("Skipping cloud agent with no recorded prompt yet", "agentId", snap.agent.ID)
		return nil
	}
	raw, err := buildRawData(snap)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("Failed to build raw data", "sessionId", snap.agent.ID, "error", err)
		return nil
	}
	if debugRaw {
		if err := writeDebugOutput(snap); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to write debug output", "sessionId", snap.agent.ID, "path", spi.GetDebugDir(snap.agent.ID), "error", err)
		}
	}
	return &spi.AgentChatSession{
		SessionID:   snap.agent.ID,
		CreatedAt:   snap.agent.CreatedAt,
		Slug:        data.Slug,
		SessionData: data,
		RawData:     raw,
	}
}

// ListAgentChatSessions lists this project's mirrored agents without any
// network access.
func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	result := []spi.SessionMetadata{}
	if origin == "" {
		return result, nil
	}
	m, _ := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	for _, snap := range m.matchingSnapshots(origin) {
		data, firstPrompt := buildSessionData(snap, workspaceRootFor(projectPath))
		if data == nil {
			continue
		}
		result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
			SessionID: snap.agent.ID,
			CreatedAt: snap.agent.CreatedAt,
			Slug:      data.Slug,
			Name:      sessionName(snap.agent, firstPrompt),
		})
	}
	return result, nil
}

`specstory run cursorcloud` now starts the agent in the project you run it from, and I tested it against `cloud-agent-test`. It no longer opens the bare agents page. Lint (v2.15.0) is clean, all tests pass, the Windows build and `./specstory` both build, and the changes are staged.

## The live test

I ran the new binary in `cloud-agent-test` with `echo` standing in for the browser opener. It created agent `bc-603c1993-…` on `github.com/specstoryai/cloud-agent-test`, opened its page, and started watching. The greeting run took about 8 seconds and cost one short paid run. The agent did what the prompt asks: no tools, one line of hello.

## What `run` does now

- **Launches through the API:** it creates the agent with this project's repo (your SSH origin converted to `https://`) and your checked-out branch.
  - The agent is named "SpecStory session" and opens with your greeting prompt.
  - Then `run` opens `cursor.com/agents/<id>` and watches.
- **Unpushed branch:** Cursor refuses an unknown branch before creating anything (I checked: a 400, nothing billed). `run` then retries once from the default branch and tells you to push if you want the agent on yours.
- **No duplicate launches:** a launch is only retried after a 429, where Cursor refused it outright. After a 5xx or a dropped connection the first attempt may already have started a paid agent, so it isn't sent again. GETs retry as before.
- **Title and slug:** both come from your first real prompt. An agent that has only the greeting isn't saved yet, so you never get a file named after the greeting.
- **Resume:** works as before and opens that agent's page.

## One thing to clean up

Your own `specstory run cursorcloud` from 09:48 (pid 46545) is still running on the old binary. It saw my test agent and wrote `2026-10-17_14-04-28Z-session-started-by-specstory.md` with the old naming. The new binary skips that agent: a sync processed 8 of the 9 agents in the mirror. To clean up:

1. Ctrl-C that run.
2. Delete that `.md`.
3. Run `specstory run cursorcloud` again to see the new flow.

When the browser opens, the agent will already be greeting you, so just type your real first message there.

## Changes

- `cursorcloud_exec.go`: the launch, the branch fallback and the greeting prompt.
- `api_client.go`: the create-agent call, and GET-only retries for 5xx and transport errors.
- `agent_session.go`: the title and slug skip the greeting.
- `spi/git_origin.go`: a new `GitHeadBranch`, which reads `HEAD` from the right place in worktrees too.
- Tests:
  - launch retries and response decoding;
  - greeting only versus greeting then your prompt;
  - `GitHeadBranch` on a branch, a detached HEAD, a worktree, and outside a repository.
- Docs: a "Run" section in `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md`, plus updated wording in both READMEs, the changelog, the config template and the check/sync help text.
