# Specstory CLI Changelog

## v2.16.0 2026-10-16

### 📢 Announcements

- The SpecStory CLI now supports [Cursor Cloud Agents](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent) (i.e. `cursorcloud`), Cursor's hosted agents launched from `https://cursor.com/agents`, Slack, GitHub, Linear, the Cursor apps, or the Cloud Agents API, for sessions read from Cloud Agents API version `1.0.0`. This provides the same support for saving to local markdown files and to the SpecStory Cloud as for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/docs/api/claude-code), [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli), [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), Factory's [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli), [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/product), Google's [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/), [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI), [VS Code Copilot](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/copilot), [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/), [Pi](https://pi.dev), [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code), [Grok Build](https://x.ai/cli) and [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/).
- Cursor Cloud agent sessions are never written to your local machine by Cursor, so SpecStory reads them from the Cursor API with your Cursor API key (provide via the `CURSOR_API_KEY` ENV var, or `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]` in `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`) and matches agents to your project by its git `origin`. 
- The Cursor API serves full session transcripts, including tool calls and their output, for only 24 hours after a run finishes; after that it returns only the conversation text. SpecStory keeps a local copy of each Cursor Cloud Agent transcript in `.specstory/cursorcloud/` in your project (or in the directory set by `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` in `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`), so a session synced within those 24 hours keeps its tool calls permanently. Run `specstory sync` at least every 24 hours, or keep `specstory watch` running, to capture the details of each run in time. Don't delete the `.specstory/cursorcloud/` directory in your project or a run older than 24 hours can only be rebuilt from the conversation text alone without its tool calls. The directory holds unredacted transcripts, so SpecStory adds a `.gitignore` file to that directory to keep it out of git.
- You can resume a Cursor Cloud Agent session into another agent. Resuming another agent's session into a Cursor Cloud Agent is not supported, because creating a cloud agent conversation launches a new paid run.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 14:13:22Z)**_

I read your changelog edit, and it says it well. One small thing: the `cursor_api_key` bullet has a trailing space after "`origin`.".

## When the downgrade actually happens

On one machine it basically doesn't. The mirror keeps the full stream permanently, so a sync keeps rendering the tool calls. It happens when the full markdown exists but the mirror doesn't:

- **Another machine:** `.specstory/history/` is often committed, but the mirror is gitignored. A teammate, or your second machine, syncs a session older than 24 hours and rewrites the committed full file with the text-only one. This is the realistic case, and it's the same problem the cloud's size rule solves.
- **Lost mirror:** someone deletes `.specstory/cursorcloud/` or changes `cursorcloud_mirror_dir`. That's what happened to us.

SpecStory Cloud is already covered by its size rule. Only the local write is exposed.

## Options

| Option                             | Mess  | Risk                                    |
|------------------------------------|-------|-----------------------------------------|
| 1. Never shrink, all providers     | Small | Freezes legitimate shrinks              |
| 2. Never shrink when text-only     | Small | Edge case when both copies are partial  |
| 3. Leave as is                     | None  | Downgrades on a second machine          |

1. **Never shrink, all providers.** The rule from cloud sync, applied to every local write. I'd avoid it. Plenty of legitimate updates make a file smaller: the `get_mcp_tools` change we just made, redaction, any formatter cleanup. That rule would have kept those old files forever.
2. **Never shrink when this render is text-only** (recommended). The provider marks a session as missing tool calls. It already knows this, since that's what drives the header note. The local writer then keeps the existing file when the new render is smaller, and the sync output says something like "kept (fuller copy on disk)". Every other write is unchanged, so formatter changes still roll out.
   - **Code:** about 10 lines at the write in `pkg/session/session.go`, one field on `spi.AgentChatSession` (not on the cloud schema), one line in cursorcloud, and a table test.
   - **Edge case:** machine A has runs 1–3 in full, and machine B has runs 1–3 text-only plus a new run 4 in full. Neither copy is complete. Whichever is larger wins, the same compromise the cloud makes. Fixing that properly would mean merging markdown, and that's the mess to avoid.
3. **Leave it.** The changelog already tells people to keep the mirror. But the second-machine case isn't something they can avoid by following that advice.

I recommend option 2. Want me to go ahead?

// loadResumeSource reads the source session for a cross-agent resume. A session with
// no recorded cwd but a known native path is read by path when its provider can, since
// a by-id lookup would be scoped to the current directory's project; everything else
// is looked up by id under its original cwd, falling back to the current one.
func loadResumeSource(plan *resumePlan, cwd string) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	if plan.fromCwd == "" && plan.fromNativePath != "" {
		if reader, ok := plan.from.(spi.PathSessionReader); ok {
			return reader.GetAgentChatSessionByPath(plan.fromNativePath, "", false)
		}
	}
	fromCwd := plan.fromCwd
	if fromCwd == "" {
		fromCwd = cwd
	}
	return plan.from.GetAgentChatSession(fromCwd, plan.sessionID, false)
}

// prepareCloudResumeTarget resumes a session that lives only in SpecStory Cloud: fetch its
// SessionData, refuse a schema newer than this CLI understands, then reconstruct into the target
// agent's native store (always — there is no local file to resume in place). Returns the fresh
// native session ID, just like the cross-agent path.
func prepareCloudResumeTarget(plan *resumePlan, cwd string, out io.Writer) (string, error) {
	track := func(outcome string) {
		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventResumeReconstructed, analytics.Properties{
			"from_agent": plan.fromID,
			"to_agent":   plan.toID,
			"outcome":    outcome,
			"source":     "cloud",
		})
	}

	fprintf(out, "\nFetching %s session %s from SpecStory Cloud...\n", plan.from.Name(), shortID(plan.sessionID))
	raw, err := cloud.FetchSessionData(plan.projectID, plan.sessionID)
	if err != nil {
		track("error")
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to fetch session from cloud: %w", err)
	}

	var data schema.SessionData
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &data); err != nil {
		track("error")
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to parse cloud session data: %w", err)
	}

	// Refuse a blob produced by a newer CLI schema than this build understands — reconstructing it
	// could silently drop or mangle fields this version doesn't know about.
	if schemaVersionNewer(data.SchemaVersion, schema.CurrentSchemaVersion) {
		track("schema_too_new")
		return "", utils.ValidationError{Message: "Resuming this session requires an updated SpecStory CLI."}
	}

	note := fmt.Sprintf("Resumed from a %s session on another machine via SpecStory.", plan.from.Name())
	rec, err := materializeReconstructed(plan, cwd, &data, note)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported) {
			track("unsupported")
			return "", utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
				"%s can't be a resume target for cloud sessions — resuming from the cloud requires reconstructing a local native session, which it doesn't support. Choose a different target agent", plan.to.Name())}
		}
		slog.Warn("resume: cloud reconstruction failed", "from", plan.fromID, "to", plan.toID, "error", err)
		track("error")
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to reconstruct cloud session for %s: %w", plan.to.Name(), err)
	}
	track("success")
	fprintf(out, "Reconstructed cloud %s session into %s as %s.\n", plan.from.Name(), plan.to.Name(), shortID(rec.SessionID))
	printIDERestartNote(plan, out)
	return rec.SessionID, nil
}

// printIDERestartNote tells the user how to surface a session reconstructed into an

// Cursor only picks up imported sessions from its SQLite database on startup, and VS
// Code holds its chat session index in memory and flushes it over ours on shutdown.
func printIDERestartNote(plan *resumePlan, out io.Writer) {
	if plan.toID == "cursoride" {
		fprintf(out, "\nNote: only Cursor 3 is supported. Restart Cursor to see the imported session in the Agent sidebar.\n")
	}
	// An ID-prefix check so every Copilot IDE variant — stock VS Code, Insiders,
	// VSCodium, and any added later — gets the note without this layer importing
	// a concrete provider package. Reconstruction normally holds its write until
	// the app is quit, so this only matters for the scripted path that warned
	// and proceeded with the app still running.
	if strings.HasPrefix(plan.toID, "copilotide") {
		// The provider name is "<app> Copilot IDE"; trimming the suffix names the
		// actual app (VS Code, VSCodium, ...) so Insiders/VSCodium users aren't
		// told about the wrong application. If the naming convention ever
		// changes, the full provider name prints — awkward but still correct.
		app := strings.TrimSuffix(plan.to.Name(), " Copilot IDE")
		fprintf(out, "\nNote: if %s was running during the import, fully quit and reopen it to see the session.\n", app)
	}
}

// schemaVersionNewer reports whether SessionData version v is newer than this CLI's supported
// version (dotted numeric, e.g. "1.0" vs "1.1"). Unparseable components compare as 0, so a
// malformed version is treated as not-newer and allowed through rather than blocking resume.
func schemaVersionNewer(v, current string) bool {
	return compareSchemaVersion(v, current) > 0
}

func compareSchemaVersion(a, b string) int {
	as, bs := strings.Split(a, "."), strings.Split(b, ".")
	n := len(as)
	if len(bs) > n {
		n = len(bs)
	}
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		av, bv := 0, 0
		if i < len(as) {
			av, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(as[i]))
		}
		if i < len(bs) {
			bv, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(bs[i]))
		}
		if av != bv {
			if av > bv {
				return 1
			}
			return -1
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// shortID abbreviates a session ID for display.
func shortID(id string) string {
	if len(id) <= 13 {
		return id
	}
	return id[:5] + "..." + id[len(id)-5:]
}

// an interactive command — on a local disk the very first check passes, so it never waits.

Right, that's by design today. `cursorcloud` reports `SupportsReconstruction() == false`, so the picker leaves it out. The reason in the code is that "creating a cloud agent conversation launches a new paid run". But `run` now launches a paid run every time, so that reason doesn't hold up anymore.

## Why it isn't just "turn it on"

Cross-agent resume is built for local agents:

1. The target's `ReconstructSession` turns the session into native file bytes, with no side effects.
2. Resume writes that file into the agent's store.
3. Resume calls `ExecAgentAndWatch` with the new session ID.

A cloud agent has no native file. The only way to give it the old conversation is to launch a new agent whose first prompt carries the flattened transcript.

## How it could fit without bending the SPI

- **`ReconstructSession`:** flattens the transcript with the same `spi.FlattenSessionData` every provider uses, and builds one prompt from it:
  - the migration note;
  - the transcript;
  - an instruction like the `run` greeting: "this is prior context, don't act on it, ask what's next".
  
  It returns that prompt as the file content, under a placeholder ID (`pending-<uuid>`).
- **`NativeSessionPath`:** points at a `pending/` folder in the mirror, so resume writes the prompt there like any other native file.
- **`ExecAgentAndWatch` with a `pending-…` ID:** reads that file, launches the agent through the same code `run` uses (repo and branch), deletes the file, opens the agent page, and watches.
- **Title and slug:** skip the transcript prompt, the same way the greeting is skipped.

The resume code in `pkg/cmd` doesn't change at all.

## Tradeoffs

- **Cost grows with the session.** The whole transcript becomes input tokens on a paid run. A short session costs cents. A long one could reach dollars, and every resume pays it again. The picker could label the choice, for example "Cursor Cloud Agent (new paid run)".
- **Unknown prompt size limit.** Cursor doesn't document a maximum prompt size. A long session might be refused, or might fill a large part of the model's context. I'd find out with one large-prompt launch, which is paid if it succeeds. If there is a limit, the options are to truncate (keeping the most recent turns) or to refuse with a clear message.
- **Duplicated history.** The new cloud session's markdown repeats the old transcript as its first message. Local targets already behave this way, since the reconstructed turns are in their native file.
- **Docs:** the changelog bullet and README say this isn't supported, so both would change.

My recommendation is to build it, with a picker label that says a paid run starts, plus a limit check first. It's a moderate change, mostly in `reconstruct.go` and `cursorcloud_exec.go`, and it reuses the launch code. Want me to probe the prompt limit first, then build it? Or leave it unsupported for this release?

Separately, I noticed a stale doc line from the last change. `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md` line 12 still says transport failures are always retried, but now only GETs are. I'll fix that with whatever comes next.

"""Probe the Cursor Cloud launch prompt size: probe.py <chars>
Launches one agent on the throwaway repo with a prompt of exactly <chars>
characters; if accepted, cancels its run at once and deletes the agent.
The API key is read from the keychain and never printed."""
import base64
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

KEY = subprocess.run(["security", "find-generic-password", "-s", "cursor-api-key", "-w"],
                     capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
AUTH = "Basic " + base64.b64encode((KEY + ":").encode()).decode()


def call(method, path, body=None, timeout=300):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://api.cursor.com" + path, method=method, data=data,
                                 headers={"Authorization": AUTH, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
            return r.status, r.read().decode(errors="replace")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.read().decode(errors="replace")


n = int(sys.argv[1])
head = "Size probe by SpecStory. Do not read files or run tools. Reply with the single word ok.\n\n"
filler = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. "
text = (head + filler * (n // len(filler) + 1))[:n]

start = time.time()
status, body = call("POST", "/v1/agents", {
    "name": f"specstory-size-probe-{n}",
    "prompt": {"text": text},
    "repos": [{"url": "https://github.com/specstoryai/cloud-agent-test"}],
})
print(f"chars={n} bytes={len(json.dumps(text))} status={status} secs={time.time() - start:.1f}")
if status not in (200, 201):
    print("body:", body[:1500])
    sys.exit(0)

resp = json.loads(body)
agent_id, run_id = resp["agent"]["id"], resp["run"]["id"]
cs, cb = call("POST", f"/v1/agents/{agent_id}/runs/{run_id}/cancel", {})
print("accepted:", agent_id, run_id, "| cancel:", cs, cb[:200])
time.sleep(3)
rs, rb = call("GET", f"/v1/agents/{agent_id}/runs/{run_id}")
print("run status:", rs, json.loads(rb).get("status") if rs == 200 else rb[:200])
ds, db = call("DELETE", f"/v1/agents/{agent_id}")
print("delete:", ds, db[:200])

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 14:34:20Z)**_

Good to hear that resuming from a Cursor Cloud Agent into another agent works.

The probe found no size limit when an agent is created. All five sizes were accepted, and every probe agent was cancelled and deleted straight away:

| Prompt chars | ≈ tokens | Status | Time  |
|--------------|----------|--------|-------|
| 1,000        | 250      | 201    | 2.1s  |
| 10,000       | 2.5k     | 201    | 2.1s  |
| 100,000      | 25k      | 201    | 2.3s  |
| 1,000,000    | 250k     | 201    | 4.9s  |
| 10,000,000   | 2.5M     | 201    | 17.0s |

The OpenAPI spec agrees: it sets no `maxLength` on `prompt.text`, while it does cap images, subagent prompts and other fields. So there was no rejection message to learn from.

That doesn't mean there's no limit. 10M characters is roughly 2.5M tokens, far beyond any model's context window. The real limit shows up once the run starts. Either the run fails with an error, or Cursor quietly summarizes or truncates the prompt. Because I cancelled each run immediately, I didn't see which.

To set a real limit for resume, I'd let one oversized run go to the end and see what happens:

1. **Launch 1M characters (about 250k tokens) and let it run.** If it fails with a context error, that error is our message, and it should cost little since the model never really starts. If it succeeds, Cursor is compacting the prompt. That's useful to know, but it could cost a few dollars on the default model (Opus, high thinking).
2. **Then, if it failed, narrow it down** with a few runs between 100k and 1M characters. Each run that succeeds costs real money, roughly $0.50 to $2 at those sizes.

That's well above the "tens of cents" you've approved for test runs before, so I'm checking first. Should I let the 1M run go to completion? The other choice is to skip the measurement and set a fixed limit in SpecStory instead, for example around 400k characters (about 100k tokens), and explain it to the user when a session goes over.

---

_**User (2026-10-18 14:36:53Z)**_

Let's just let the limit at 1M chars of session data. Larger than that in the resumed session and tell the user it's too large to resume in a Cursor Cloud Agent, the limit is 1M chars in the session.

Also... many providers have a "native" resume for resuming a session from the same provider so we actually just launch the SAME session rather than create a copy... you need to investigate supporting that for Cursor Cloud Agent if possible, if not, we create the copy just as if it was a resume from another agent.

	return m.enterTargetPicker(sess), nil
}

// enterTargetPicker pins sess as the chosen session and opens the target-selection step, with
// the highlight on the last-resumed agent (else the session's own agent). Shared by the
// picker's selection flow (beginResume) and the --session pinned entry, so the two can't drift.
func (m sessionTUI) enterTargetPicker(sess *sessionindex.Session) sessionTUI {
	m.chosen = sess
	m.mode = modeTarget
	m.targets = m.eligibleTargets(sess)
	m.targetCursor = m.defaultTargetIndex()
	return m
}

// eligibleTargets narrows the installed agents to the valid resume targets for
// sess. Any agent that can reconstruct sessions into its native store
// qualifies; the session's own agent additionally qualifies for local sessions,
// which resume natively in place with no reconstruction. A cloud session has no
// local native file, so even its own agent must reconstruct to qualify. This
// keeps a provider without a serializer (Antigravity) out of the list except
// for its own local sessions, where picking it would otherwise dead-end after
// selection.
func (m sessionTUI) eligibleTargets(sess *sessionindex.Session) []agentChoice {
	var out []agentChoice
	for _, a := range m.installed {
		sameAgentLocal := sess != nil && !sess.IsCloud && a.id == sess.Agent
		if sameAgentLocal || a.provider.SupportsReconstruction() {
			out = append(out, a)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (m sessionTUI) defaultTargetIndex() int {
	// Prefer the last-resumed agent, else the chosen session's own agent (same-agent resume).
	// An explicit preset (`resume <agent>`) never reaches here — beginResume skips the
	// target-selection step entirely in that case.
	want := m.lastAgent
	if want == "" && m.chosen != nil {
		want = m.chosen.Agent
	}
	for i, a := range m.targets {
		if a.id == want {
			return i
		}
	}

func prepareResumeTarget(plan *resumePlan, cwd string, out io.Writer) (string, error) {

package cursorcloud

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// maxResumePromptChars caps the transcript a resume hands a new cloud agent.
// The API accepted launch prompts of up to 10M characters when probed, so the
// cap is SpecStory's own: about 1M characters (~250k tokens) is already past
// what a model's context holds, so a larger transcript would start a paid run
// that fails or loses most of the session.
const maxResumePromptChars = 1_000_000

// resumePromptHead opens the prompt a resumed session's new agent starts with.
// It keeps the first paid run short: the transcript is context, not a task.
const resumePromptHead = "Session resumed by SpecStory. The conversation so far is below, as context only. Don't act on it, read files, or run any tools yet. Briefly confirm you have the context and ask what the user would like to do next."

// pendingPrefix marks the session ID ReconstructSession mints. Cursor assigns
// an agent's id when the agent is launched, so the reconstructed "native
// session" is a launch request that ExecAgentAndWatch carries out.
const pendingPrefix = "pending-"

// pendingResume is the native file of a reconstructed session.
type pendingResume struct {
	// SourceAgentID is set when the session came from a cloud agent, which is
	// reopened in place while it still exists rather than copied.
	SourceAgentID string `json:"sourceAgentId,omitempty"`
	Name          string `json:"name"`
	Prompt        string `json:"prompt"`
}

// ReconstructSession turns a session into a pending launch: a new cloud agent
// whose first prompt is the flattened transcript. A cloud agent's conversation
// lives in Cursor's backend, so seeding a new agent with the transcript is the
// only way to carry a session into one.
func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
	turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, opts)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	pending := pendingResume{Name: spi.ResumedSessionTitle(data.Slug), Prompt: resumePrompt(turns)}
	if data.Provider.ID == ProviderID && validAgentID(data.SessionID) {
		pending.SourceAgentID = data.SessionID
	} else if err := checkResumeSize(pending.Prompt); err != nil {
		// A session from a cloud agent may still reopen in place, which needs no
		// transcript, so its size is checked only if it has to be copied.
		return nil, err
	}
	content, err := json.Marshal(pending)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("encode pending resume: %w", err)
	}
	id := pendingPrefix + uuid.NewString()
	return &spi.ReconstructedSession{SessionID: id, Filename: id + ".json", Content: content}, nil
}

// NativeSessionPath places a pending launch in the project's mirror, whose
// .gitignore keeps the unredacted transcript out of git until `resume` reads
// and removes it.
func (p *Provider) NativeSessionPath(projectPath string, filename string) (string, error) {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(filename, pendingPrefix) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not a pending Cursor Cloud Agent resume", filename)
	}
	m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return m.pendingFile(filename), nil
}

// SupportsReconstruction reports true: any session can seed a new cloud agent.
func (p *Provider) SupportsReconstruction() bool {
	return true
}

// ResumeTargetNote warns that resuming another agent's session here starts a
// new paid cloud run. A cloud agent's own session reopens the same agent,
// which starts nothing until the user sends a follow-up.
func (p *Provider) ResumeTargetNote(sourceAgent string) string {
	if sourceAgent == ProviderID {
		return ""
	}
	return "starts a new paid cloud run"
}

// resumePrompt renders the flattened turns as one prompt.
func resumePrompt(turns []spi.Turn) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(resumePromptHead)
	for _, turn := range turns {
		role := "User"
		if turn.Role == schema.RoleAgent {
			role = "Agent"
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n\n## %s\n\n%s", role, turn.Text)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// checkResumeSize refuses a transcript too large for a new agent's prompt.
func checkResumeSize(prompt string) error {
	if n := len([]rune(prompt)); n > maxResumePromptChars {
		return fmt.Errorf("this session is too large to resume in a Cursor Cloud Agent: it has %d characters, and the limit is %d characters", n, maxResumePromptChars)
	}
	return nil
}

// pendingFile is where a pending launch is stored in the mirror.
func (m mirror) pendingFile(filename string) string {
	return filepath.Join(m.root, "pending", filepath.Base(filename))
}

}

// ensureRoot creates the mirror root and, for a mirror inside the project,
// the .gitignore that keeps raw transcripts out of commits.
func (m mirror) ensureRoot(projectLocal bool) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(m.root, 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !projectLocal {
		return nil
	}
	path := filepath.Join(m.root, ".gitignore")
	if existing, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil && gitignoreExcludesAll(existing) {
		return nil
	}
	return writeFileAtomic(path, []byte(mirrorGitignore))
}

// gitignoreExcludesAll reports whether a .gitignore carries the bare "*" rule

// let git track raw transcripts, so ensureRoot rewrites it rather than trusting

// dashboardURL is where cloud agents are followed; an agent's page is
// dashboardURL/<id>.
const dashboardURL = "https://cursor.com/agents"

// launchName names every agent `run` starts. Cursor would otherwise name the
// agent after launchPromptText, which says nothing about the session, so the
// session title comes from the user's first real prompt instead (sessionName).
const launchName = "SpecStory session"

// launchPromptText opens every agent `run` starts. The API cannot create an
// agent without a prompt, and this one keeps the paid first run short: no
// tools, just a greeting, so the user takes over in the browser.
const launchPromptText = "Session started by SpecStory. Don't read files or run any tools yet. Briefly greet the user and ask what they'd like to work on."

// ExecAgentAndWatch is `run` for a hosted agent. No local process exists, so it
// starts a cloud agent on this project's repository (or, when resuming, uses
// that agent), opens the agent's page with the configured opener, and then
// watches until Ctrl-C exactly like WatchAgent.
func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: starting", "projectPath", projectPath, "customCommand", customCommand, "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID, "debugRaw", debugRaw)

	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()

	agentID := resumeSessionID
	if agentID == "" {
		agent, err := launchSession(ctx, projectPath)
		if err != nil {
			slog.Error("ExecAgentAndWatch: launch failed", "error", err)
			return fmt.Errorf("could not start a Cursor Cloud Agent: %w", err)
		}
		agentID = agent.ID
	} else if !validAgentID(agentID) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%q is not a Cursor Cloud Agent id", agentID)
	}

	target := dashboardURL + "/" + agentID
	if err := openURL(customCommand, target); err != nil {
		// Watching still works when the browser could not be opened; the
		// user can follow the printed URL.
		slog.Warn("ExecAgentAndWatch: opening the agent page failed", "url", target, "error", err)
		log.UserWarn("Could not open %s (%v). Open it in a browser; watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity — press Ctrl-C to stop.", target, err)
	} else {
		log.UserMessage("Opened %s — watching for Cursor Cloud Agent activity, press Ctrl-C to stop.\n", target)
	}

	err := p.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
	if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		err = nil
	}
	slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: exiting", "error", err)

// resumeTarget returns the agent to open. `run` (no session) starts a new
// agent. A cloud agent's own session reopens that agent, so the conversation
// continues where it was rather than in a copy. Anything else, or an agent
// that can no longer be reopened here, starts a new agent seeded with the
// session's transcript.
func resumeTarget(ctx context.Context, projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
	key, _ := resolveAPIKey()
	if key == "" {
		return "", errNoAPIKey
	}
	client := newAPIClient(key)

	var agent apiAgent
	var err error
	switch {
	case sessionID == "":
		agent, err = launchSession(ctx, client, projectPath, launchName, launchPromptText)
	case strings.HasPrefix(sessionID, pendingPrefix):
		return resumePending(ctx, client, projectPath, sessionID)
	case validAgentID(sessionID):
		return resumeAgent(ctx, client, projectPath, sessionID)
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not a Cursor Cloud Agent id", sessionID)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("could not start a Cursor Cloud Agent: %w", err)
	}
	return agent.ID, nil
}

// resumePending carries out a launch ReconstructSession prepared: it reopens
// the source cloud agent when there is one to reopen, and otherwise launches a
// new agent with the transcript.
func resumePending(ctx context.Context, client *apiClient, projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
	m, _ := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	path := m.pendingFile(sessionID + ".json")
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("read the prepared resume: %w", err)
	}
	// The file holds an unredacted transcript and has served its purpose once
	// read; a failed launch is retried by resuming again.
	if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil {
		slog.Warn("resumePending: could not remove the prepared resume", "path", path, "error", err)
	}
	var pending pendingResume
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &pending); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("decode the prepared resume: %w", err)
	}
	if pending.SourceAgentID != "" {
		reopened, err := reopenAgent(ctx, client, projectPath, pending.SourceAgentID)
		if err != nil || reopened {
			return pending.SourceAgentID, err
		}
	}
	return launchCopy(ctx, client, projectPath, pending.Name, pending.Prompt)
}

// resumeAgent reopens a cloud agent's own session. When the agent cannot be
// reopened here, the session is copied into a new agent from the mirror,
// which keeps the transcript after Cursor has deleted the agent.
func resumeAgent(ctx context.Context, client *apiClient, projectPath, agentID string) (string, error) {
	reopened, err := reopenAgent(ctx, client, projectPath, agentID)
	if err != nil || reopened {
		return agentID, err
	}
	m, _ := mirrorFor(projectPath)
	snap, err := loadAgentSnapshot(m.agentDir(agentID))
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	var data *schema.SessionData
	if snap != nil {
		data, _ = buildSessionData(snap, workspaceRootFor(projectPath))
	}
	if data == nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("Cursor Cloud Agent %s can't be reopened here, and SpecStory has no copy of its session to start a new agent from", agentID)
	}
	turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, spi.ReconstructOptions{MigrationNote: "Resumed from an earlier Cursor Cloud Agent session via SpecStory."})
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return launchCopy(ctx, client, projectPath, spi.ResumedSessionTitle(data.Slug), resumePrompt(turns))
}

// reopenAgent reports whether agentID can be reopened for this project. An
// agent Cursor no longer has, or one on another repository (whose activity
// this project's watch would never pick up), cannot. An archived agent is
// unarchived first, because resuming it is a request to use it again.
func reopenAgent(ctx context.Context, client *apiClient, projectPath, agentID string) (bool, error) {
	record, err := client.getAgent(ctx, agentID)
	if isNotFound(err) {
		slog.Info("reopenAgent: agent no longer exists", "agentID", agentID)
		return false, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if !agentMatchesOrigin(record.agent, projectOrigin(projectPath)) {
		slog.Info("reopenAgent: agent is on another repository", "agentID", agentID, "repos", record.agent.Repos)
		return false, nil
	}
	if record.agent.Status == "ARCHIVED" {
		if err := client.unarchiveAgent(ctx, agentID); err != nil {
			return false, fmt.Errorf("could not unarchive Cursor Cloud Agent %s: %w", agentID, err)
		}
		log.UserMessage("Unarchived Cursor Cloud Agent %s to resume it.\\n", agentID)
	}
	slog.Info("reopenAgent: reopening", "agentID", agentID)
	return true, nil
}

// launchCopy starts a new agent seeded with a transcript, refusing one too
// large for a prompt before anything is billed.
func launchCopy(ctx context.Context, client *apiClient, projectPath, name, prompt string) (string, error) {
	if err := checkResumeSize(prompt); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	log.UserMessage("Starting a new Cursor Cloud Agent with the session so far. This is a new paid cloud run.\\n")
	agent, err := launchSession(ctx, client, projectPath, name, prompt)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("could not start a Cursor Cloud Agent: %w", err)
	}
	return agent.ID, nil
}

// launchSession starts a cloud agent on the project's repository and current
// branch. Cursor's agents page cannot be told which repository to use, so an
// agent started there lands wherever the user picks, or in a scratch
// repository when they pick none; launching through the API is the only way
// to guarantee the agent works on, and is saved to, this project.
func launchSession(ctx context.Context, client *apiClient, projectPath, name, prompt string) (apiAgent, error) {
	origin := projectOrigin(projectPath)
	if origin == "" {
		return apiAgent{}, noProjectOriginError(projectPath)
	}
	// The API takes an HTTPS URL, while the origin may be SSH; the normalized
	// host/owner/repo form is the same for both.
	repoURL := "https://" + origin
	branch := spi.GitHeadBranch(projectPath)

	slog.Info("launchSession: launching", "repo", repoURL, "branch", branch, "promptChars", len(prompt))
	agent, err := client.launchAgent(ctx, newLaunchRequest(repoURL, branch, name, prompt))
	if branch != "" && isUnknownBranch(err) {
		log.UserWarn("Branch %s is not on %s, so the agent starts from the default branch. Push the branch to start from it.", branch, origin)
		branch = ""
		agent, err = client.launchAgent(ctx, newLaunchRequest(repoURL, branch, name, prompt))
	}
	if err != nil {
		return apiAgent{}, err
	}
	slog.Info("launchSession: launched", "agentID", agent.ID, "branch", branch)
	return agent, nil
}

const testOrigin = "git@github.com:specstoryai/cloud-agent-test.git"

// makeProject creates a git checkout at dir whose origin is origin.
func makeProject(t *testing.T, dir, origin string) string {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, ".git"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	config := "[remote \"origin\"]\n\turl = " + origin + "\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "config"), []byte(config), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return dir
}

	useSettings(t, "test-key")

		t.Errorf("unknown id got %v, %v; want nil, nil", s, err)
	}
}

			}

func sessionWithText(providerID, sessionID, text string) *schema.SessionData {
	return &schema.SessionData{
		SchemaVersion: schema.CurrentSchemaVersion,
		Provider:      schema.ProviderInfo{ID: providerID, Name: providerID, Version: "1"},
		SessionID:     sessionID,
		Slug:          "forth-mastermind",
		Exchanges: []schema.Exchange{{Messages: []schema.Message{
			{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: text}}},
			{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "Sure."}}},
		}}},
	}
}

// TestReconstructSession: any session becomes a pending launch. A cloud agent's
// own session remembers its agent so resume can reopen it, and skips the size
// cap until it actually has to be copied.
func TestReconstructSession(t *testing.T) {
	const cloudAgent = "bc-11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"
	huge := strings.Repeat("x", maxResumePromptChars)
	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		data       *schema.SessionData
		wantSource string
		wantErr    string
	}{
		{name: "another agent's session", data: sessionWithText("claude", "c-1", "Let's write Forth")},
		{name: "a cloud agent's session", data: sessionWithText(ProviderID, cloudAgent, "Let's write Forth"), wantSource: cloudAgent},
		{name: "another agent's session over the cap", data: sessionWithText("claude", "c-1", huge), wantErr: "too large to resume"},
		{name: "a cloud agent's session over the cap", data: sessionWithText(ProviderID, cloudAgent, huge), wantSource: cloudAgent},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			useSettings(t, "")
			p := NewProvider()
			rec, err := p.ReconstructSession(tt.data, spi.ReconstructOptions{MigrationNote: "Resumed via SpecStory."})
			if tt.wantErr != "" {
				if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tt.wantErr) {
					t.Fatalf("err = %v, want %q", err, tt.wantErr)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !strings.HasPrefix(rec.SessionID, pendingPrefix) || rec.Filename != rec.SessionID+".json" {
				t.Errorf("session %q file %q, want a pending id and its .json", rec.SessionID, rec.Filename)
			}
			var pending pendingResume
			if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Content, &pending); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if pending.SourceAgentID != tt.wantSource || pending.Name != "forth-mastermind" {
				t.Errorf("pending = source %q name %q, want source %q", pending.SourceAgentID, pending.Name, tt.wantSource)
			}
			if !strings.HasPrefix(pending.Prompt, resumePromptHead) || !strings.Contains(pending.Prompt, "## User\\n\\n") {
				t.Errorf("prompt does not open with the resume head and the transcript: %.200q", pending.Prompt)
			}

			// The transcript waits in the mirror, behind its .gitignore.
			project := makeProject(t, t.TempDir(), testOrigin)
			path, err := p.NativeSessionPath(project, rec.Filename)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			m, _ := mirrorFor(project)
			if path != m.pendingFile(rec.Filename) {
				t.Errorf("path = %s, want the mirror's pending dir", path)
			}
			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(m.root, ".gitignore")); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("mirror .gitignore missing: %v", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestResumeTarget: a cloud agent's own session reopens the same agent while it
// exists on this project's repository; otherwise the session is copied into a
// new agent, unless the transcript is over the cap.
func TestResumeTarget(t *testing.T) {
	fx := loadFixture(t, "fixture-run")
	agentID := fx.agent.agent.ID
	withAgent := func(change func(map[string]any)) json.RawMessage {
		var agent map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(fx.agent.raw, &agent); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		change(agent)
		raw, _ := json.Marshal(agent)
		return raw
	}
	pending := func(source, prompt string) pendingResume {
		return pendingResume{SourceAgentID: source, Name: "forth-mastermind", Prompt: prompt}
	}
	small := resumePromptHead + "\\n\\n## User\\n\\nhello"

	tests := []struct {
		name         string
		agent        json.RawMessage // served by the API; nil serves none
		mirrored     bool            // the agent's session is in the mirror
		pending      *pendingResume  // resume through a pending launch, else by agent id
		wantID       string
		wantLaunch   bool
		wantUnarchiv bool
		wantErr      string
	}{
		{name: "pending: source agent reopens", agent: fx.agent.raw, pending: ptr(pending(agentID, small)), wantID: agentID},
		{name: "pending: source agent gone, copied", pending: ptr(pending(agentID, small)), wantID: launchedAgentID, wantLaunch: true},
		{name: "pending: another agent's session, copied", agent: fx.agent.raw, pending: ptr(pending("", small)), wantID: launchedAgentID, wantLaunch: true},
		{name: "pending: copy over the cap refused", pending: ptr(pending(agentID, strings.Repeat("x", maxResumePromptChars+1))), wantErr: "too large to resume"},
		{name: "agent id: reopens", agent: fx.agent.raw, wantID: agentID},
		{name: "agent id: archived agent unarchived", agent: withAgent(func(a map[string]any) { a["status"] = "ARCHIVED" }), wantID: agentID, wantUnarchiv: true},
		{name: "agent id: on another repository, copied from the mirror", agent: withAgent(func(a map[string]any) {
			a["repos"] = []map[string]string{{"url": "https://github.com/specstoryai/another"}}
		}), mirrored: true, wantID: launchedAgentID, wantLaunch: true},
		{name: "agent id: gone and not mirrored", wantErr: "no copy of its session"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			useSettings(t, "test-key")
			f := newFakeAPI(t)
			if tt.agent != nil {
				f.setAgent(tt.agent)
			}
			project := makeProject(t, t.TempDir(), testOrigin)
			m, projectLocal := mirrorFor(project)
			if err := m.ensureRoot(projectLocal); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if tt.mirrored {
				writeFixtureMirror(t, m, fx)
			}
			sessionID := agentID
			if tt.pending != nil {
				sessionID = pendingPrefix + "test"
				raw, _ := json.Marshal(tt.pending)
				if err := writeFileAtomic(m.pendingFile(sessionID+".json"), raw); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}

			got, err := resumeTarget(context.Background(), project, sessionID)
			if tt.wantErr != "" {
				if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tt.wantErr) {
					t.Fatalf("err = %v, want %q", err, tt.wantErr)
				}
			} else if err != nil || got != tt.wantID {
				t.Fatalf("resumeTarget = %q, %v; want %q", got, err, tt.wantID)
			}
			if launched := len(f.launches) > 0; launched != tt.wantLaunch {
				t.Errorf("launched = %v, want %v", launched, tt.wantLaunch)
			}
			if tt.wantLaunch && !strings.HasPrefix(f.launches[0].Prompt.Text, resumePromptHead) {
				t.Errorf("copy prompt does not carry the transcript: %.100q", f.launches[0].Prompt.Text)
			}
			if unarchived := f.count("/v1/agents/"+agentID+"/unarchive") > 0; unarchived != tt.wantUnarchiv {
				t.Errorf("unarchived = %v, want %v", unarchived, tt.wantUnarchiv)
			}
			if tt.pending != nil {
				if _, err := os.Stat(m.pendingFile(sessionID + ".json")); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
					t.Error("the pending transcript was left in the mirror")
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

The OpenAPI document promises `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `-Remaining` and `-Reset` headers on `429`; no rate-limit headers appear on successful responses. The client therefore sends requests one at a time without pacing, and retries `429` responses after `Retry-After` (else `X-RateLimit-Reset`, else exponential backoff), holding every caller in the process meanwhile. A GET also retries `5xx` responses and transport failures (DNS, connection reset, timeout) with the same backoff. A launch (`POST`) retries only `429`, because after a `5xx` or a dropped connection the agent may already exist, and resending would start a second paid run. A cancelled context is never retried.
pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:13:- Accounts on Privacy Mode (Legacy) get `400 validation_error` "Cloud agent is not supported in Privacy Mode (Legacy)" from every agent call.
pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:108:`specstory run cursorcloud` launches a new agent with `POST /v1/agents` instead of opening the bare agents page, because that page cannot be told which repository to use: an agent started there without one lands in a scratch repository (`origin.cursor.com/git/<user>/tmp-….git`) that never matches the project. The launch sets `repos[0].url` to `https://` plus the normalized origin and `startingRef` to the checked-out branch. The API validates the branch before creating anything (`400 validation_error`, "Branch '…' does not exist in repository …"), so an unpushed branch is retried once without `startingRef`, starting from the default branch. The API cannot create an agent without a prompt, so the agent is named `SpecStory session` and opens with a fixed no-tools greeting; both are skipped when choosing the session title and slug, and an agent with only the greeting yields no session yet. A launch is never resent after a 5xx or a transport failure, because the first attempt may already have started a paid run. `run` then opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>` and watches.
pkg/providers/cursorcloud/CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md:112:Same-agent resume (`specstory resume` of a cloud session into `cursorcloud`) opens `https://cursor.com/agents/<id>`, where a follow-up run can be started, and then watches. Resuming another agent's session into `cursorcloud` is unsupported: the only way to create a cloud agent conversation is to launch a new paid run, so `ReconstructSession` returns `spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported`. Resuming a cloud session into a local agent works through the shared `SessionData` flattening, from any directory: with no `OriginCwd` on the index row, resume reads the session by its mirror path (`agent.json`) through `GetAgentChatSessionByPath`.
pkg/providers/cursorcloud/reconstruct.go:18:// what a model's context holds, so a larger transcript would start a paid run
pkg/providers/cursorcloud/reconstruct.go:23:// It keeps the first paid run short: the transcript is context, not a task.
changelog.md:10:- You can resume a Cursor Cloud Agent session into another agent. Resuming another agent's session into a Cursor Cloud Agent is not supported, because creating a cloud agent conversation launches a new paid run.
README.md:47:Cursor Cloud Agents run in Cursor's backend, and their conversations are never written to your machine. The `cursorcloud` provider reads them from the [Cloud Agents API](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints) with your Cursor API key (create one at https://cursor.com/dashboard/api, then set `CURSOR_API_KEY` or `cursor_api_key` under `[providers]`). Agents are matched to the current project by repository: an agent belongs to the project when one of its repositories is the project's git `origin`. The provider keeps a local mirror of what it has read in `.specstory/cursorcloud/` (it writes its own `.gitignore` there, because the mirror holds unredacted transcripts); `cursorcloud_mirror_dir` or `--user-data-dir cursorcloud:<path>` moves it. A finished run's full transcript, including tool calls and output, is available from the API for 24 hours; after that only its text remains, so sync at least daily or keep `specstory watch` running. `specstory run cursorcloud` starts a cloud agent on the project's repository and current branch (the default branch when the current one is not pushed), opens its page in your browser, and then watches until interrupted with `ctrl-c`. The agent opens with a short greeting, which is a paid run like any other, and you continue the conversation in the browser. Resuming another agent's session into a cloud agent is not supported, because that would launch a new paid run; cloud sessions can be resumed into local agents.
docs/CURSOR-CLOUD-AGENTS.md:25:An account on "Privacy Mode (Legacy)" cannot use cloud agents at all. Every v0 and v1 agents call returns `400 validation_error: "Cloud agent is not supported in Privacy Mode (Legacy)"`. Customers reporting missing cloud agent histories are therefore on standard Privacy Mode, whose conversations are stored server-side.

Any session can now be resumed into a Cursor Cloud Agent. I tested it live with your "Do you know Forth?" Claude Code session:

## Prompt size probe

Cursor accepted every size I tried (1k, 10k, 100k, 1M and 10M characters, all `201`), and its API spec sets no maximum. So the limit is ours, as you decided: a session over 1,000,000 characters is refused before anything is launched, with the message *"this session is too large to resume in a Cursor Cloud Agent: it has N characters, and the limit is 1000000 characters"*. Each probe agent was cancelled and deleted immediately. It's recorded in the format doc.

## Same-agent resume

Resuming a Cursor Cloud session into Cursor Cloud continues the same agent whenever it can:

- **The agent still exists on this repo:** it's reopened. That works for a local session and for one from SpecStory Cloud, whose reconstruction remembers the source agent.
- **The agent is archived:** it's unarchived first, and you're told.
- **Cursor deleted it, or it's on another repo:** it falls back to a copy, as if resuming from another agent. A local session is copied from the mirror.

## What else changed

- **Resuming from another agent:** the transcript is flattened with the same helper every provider uses, waits briefly in the mirror's `pending/` folder (behind its `.gitignore`), then launches through the same code as `run`. The pending file is deleted once it's read.
- **Paid-run note:**
  - the picker shows "Cursor Cloud Agent (starts a new paid cloud run)" for other agents' sessions;
  - the CLI prints "This is a new paid cloud run." before launching.
  - The note comes from a small optional `spi.ResumeTargetNoter` interface. It isn't shown when reopening the same agent, since that starts nothing.
- **Titles:** the transcript prompt is skipped when choosing the title and slug, like the `run` greeting.
- **Docs:** the changelog, the README, the "Resume" section of `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md` and the research doc now describe resuming into Cursor Cloud and the 1M limit. The retry line in the format doc is fixed too.
- **Tests:** a table test for reconstruct (sources, the cap, and the pending file location), and one for the resume decision. The resume test covers reopening, archived, deleted, another repo, not in the mirror, and over the cap.

## One gap I didn't fix

The resumed agent is named "Resumed session". Every provider that reconstructs titles the session from `SessionData.Slug`, and Claude Code doesn't fill that field. So this happens with Claude Code sources in Codex, Droid, Cursor and the rest too. It's a small fix in the Claude Code provider, but it touches every target, so I'd do it separately if you want it.

Commit message:

```
Cursor Cloud Agent provider: resume any session into a cloud agent, reopening the same agent when possible; 1M character limit
```

// Used by both sync mode (GetAgentChatSession/GetAgentChatSessions) and watch mode.
func convertToAgentChatSession(session *GeminiSession, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
	// Generate structured session data
	sessionData, err := GenerateAgentSession(session, workspaceRoot)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("convertToAgentChatSession: failed to generate session data",
			"sessionId", session.ID,
			"error", err)
		return nil
	}

	// Extract slug from first user message
	var slug string
	for _, msg := range session.Messages {
		if msg.Type == "user" {
			slug = spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(msgContent(msg))
			break
		}
	}
	if slug == "" {
		slug = "gemini-session"
	}

```text
- Use `schema.CurrentSchemaVersion` and the shared `schema.ContentTypeText` / `schema.ContentTypeThinking` constants when constructing `SessionData`, rather than repeating their string values. Native record fields and code-fence language labels follow their own formats.
- `spi.CodeFence` for every fenced block, sized past any backtick run in the content. Never write a literal triple backtick, and never backslash-escape backticks.
- `spi.ReadRecordLine` with `spi.MaxRecordLineSize` for every JSONL session file. It is the only correct way to cap a record: a cap applied after `bufio.Reader.ReadString` returns has already allocated the oversized record it exists to prevent. A capped `bufio.Scanner` is still right for sidecar and index files, where losing the remainder of the file is acceptable.
- `spi.CapRunes` for truncation. Never slice a string by bytes.
- Compare a sentinel error with `errors.Is` and match an error type with `errors.As`. Never `err == io.EOF` or `err.(*exec.ExitError)`: a wrapped error fails both, and wrapping gets added later by someone who has no reason to look for a bare comparison.
- `spi.LanguageFromPath`, `spi.RenderGenericJSON`, `spi.TodoSymbol`, `spi.FormatDiffBlock`, `spi.StringValue`, `spi.NormalizeToolName` for tool rendering.
- `spi.LookPathForCheck` for binary lookup, `spi.ClassifyCheckError` for lookup/storage errors, and `spi.ClassifyCheckExecutionError` for probe failures after the binary was found. Populate `CheckResult.ErrorType` with the same `spi.CheckError*` value sent to analytics; leave it empty on success. Empty `--version` output on a successful run is a success reported as `"unknown"`, not a failure (`spi.CheckErrorNoOutput` is a legacy shape).
- `analytics.CheckAttempt` populated once per `Check`, with the event emitted by `analytics.TrackCheckSuccess` or `analytics.TrackCheckFailure`. No inline `analytics.TrackEvent` calls in a provider.
- `spi.SplitCommandLine` for custom commands; `spi.EnsureResumeArgs` when the agent resumes via a subcommand, or `spi.EnsureResumeFlagArgs` when it uses a flag.
- `spi.AgentExitError` to report a non-zero agent exit. Never call `os.Exit` inside a provider; it skips the final session save (the reason is in `pkg/spi/exit.go`).
- `spi.GetDebugDir` for debug output paths. See [Native debug output](#native-debug-output) for the provider's export responsibilities; the CLI writes `session-data.json` itself.
- `spi.NormalizePath` and `spi.ExtractShellPathHints` for path hints; `spi.CanonicalizePathOrClean` for local path comparison; `spi.FileURIToPath` for any `file://` URI.
- `spi.GitOriginURL`, `spi.NormalizeGitRemoteURL` and `spi.FindGitRoot` when a session is matched to a project by repository rather than by directory. They are the normalization the CLI hashes into `git_id`, so a provider that normalized URLs its own way would attribute sessions to a different project than the rest of the CLI.
- `spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage`, `spi.GenerateReadableName`, and `spi.ReadableTitleFromSessionData` for slugs, names, and titles. If the agent records its own title or summary for a session, prefer it for `Name` and fall back to the shared generator.
- `spi.PrepareTurns`, `spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot`, `spi.ReconstructRole`, `spi.RFC3339Millis`, `spi.ResumedSessionTitle` in `ReconstructSession`.
- `spi.NewFSWatcher` to create every fsnotify watcher, in production code and tests alike. Never call `fsnotify.NewWatcher` or `fsnotify.NewBufferedWatcher` directly; see [The watcher](#the-watcher) for why.
- `spi.WatchWindowDays`, `spi.WatchWindowCutoff`, `spi.DateDirWithinWatchWindow` when watched paths can grow without limit and the store layout supports a rolling date window. A fixed set of directory watches does not need a rolling window merely because the number of session files grows.
- `spi.DeliverSession` for synchronous callback delivery with panic recovery. If using `spi.DispatchSession` for asynchronous delivery, track and join every callback before shutdown.
- SQLite stores: open every read handle as `file:<path>?mode=ro&` plus `spi.BusyTimeoutPragma`. The `file:` scheme is required; the driver ignores `mode=` on a bare path and opens read-write-create. Call `spi.EnsureWALMode` once at watcher startup, never on a read path.

Providers must never import `pkg/utils`, `pkg/session`, or `pkg/cloud` (the import graph cycles through the registry), nor `pkg/telemetry` (layering).

### Honest data over convenient data

- `CheckResult.Version` is the version string the probe printed. It is empty when no version probe is possible (an IDE store, a hosted agent), and the CLI then omits the version line; it is the literal `"unknown"` when the binary ran but printed nothing. Never any other label.
- `ProviderInfo.Version` is the agent's version when the native data records it, otherwise the literal `"unknown"`. The model name is not a substitute; it belongs on each agent message's `Model` field, and it is the real model, never a placeholder such as an automatic-mode label.
- `SessionData.WorkspaceRoot` is never empty: the workspace the agent stated, then the caller's project path, then the process working directory as a documented last resort. These fallbacks support path normalization and rendering; they are not evidence that the session belongs to the caller's project.
- `GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd` records the session's originating working directory. Leave it empty when the origin cannot be determined; do not fill it from a rendering fallback. Global enumeration still returns the session, and the CLI assigns the `"unknown"` project ID. The literal `"unknown"` belongs in neither `OriginCwd` nor `WorkspaceRoot`. A session that records a repository but no directory leaves `OriginCwd` empty and sets `OriginRepoURL`; reindex attributes it to the project with that origin by the same `git_id` normalization. A provider whose sessions carry no cwd must implement `spi.PathSessionReader`, because reindex and resume read such sessions by path.
- Never infer project membership from the paths that tools touched; one read of `~/.gitconfig` would attach the session to every project under the home directory. Session-to-project matching uses containment of stated paths, never a rendering fallback or a guessed common ancestor.
- `GetAgentChatSession` returns `nil, nil` for not found. Errors are for real failures.

## Self-review checklist

- [ ] Package named for the product, lowercased and unspaced
- [ ] Necessary files only, similar to the recommended files list, no file sprawl
- [ ] `var _ spi.Provider` assertion present
- [ ] Every SPI method implemented, including `ListAllAgentChatSessions` and the three reconstruction methods
- [ ] Tests cover behavioral contracts and capability consistency, including agreement between `SupportsReconstruction` and the reconstruction methods; trivial constant-return methods do not need standalone tests
- [ ] Provider registered in `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`
- [ ] Config wired: `<id>_cmd` in template, struct, switch, doc comment, and test rows, with both wiring tests passing
- [ ] Brand-specific TUI color added
- [ ] Both READMEs updated
- [ ] Draft changelog.md entry added
- [ ] `<AGENT>-FORMAT.md`, in the provider package, written from the current release with the write lifecycle and baseline version, no legacy notes
- [ ] `tools.txt` from the agent itself, prefixes stripped, declaration preferred over self-report
- [ ] Bespoke renderers and classifier cases use names from `tools.txt` and are backed by observed tool records
- [ ] Tool audit identifies the tested environment and distinguishes declared, enabled, and exercised tools
- [ ] Unexercised tools have documented reasons, and observed failed calls have verified error rendering
- [ ] Tool inventory sweep test exists
- [ ] Markdown code blocks use `spi.CodeFence` instead of hard-coded triple backticks, so backticks in the content cannot prematurely close the block
- [ ] Text truncation uses `spi.CapRunes` instead of byte slicing such as `text[:limit]`, which can split a multibyte Unicode character and produce invalid UTF-8
- [ ] No local copies or equivalents of the helpers available in `pkg/spi`
- [ ] Provider `Check` reports exactly one outcome through `analytics.TrackCheckSuccess` or `analytics.TrackCheckFailure` using `analytics.CheckAttempt`, rather than calling `analytics.TrackEvent` directly, so event names and properties stay consistent across providers
- [ ] No `os.Exit` calls
- [ ] The change signal is fsnotify for a file-based store or a bounded poll for a remote store, supplemented by bounded periodic reconciliation
- [ ] File-based stores: every fsnotify watcher, including those in tests, is created with `spi.NewFSWatcher`, so calling `Add`/`Remove` from the event loop cannot deadlock on Windows
- [ ] Watcher does not keep accumulating open files or filesystem watches as session history grows: use a fixed set of directory watches or prune older watches (with `spi.WatchWindow*` for date-organized stores) to avoid exhausting operating-system resources during long-running watches
  - [ ] Watcher leaves existing, unchanged sessions alone at startup
  - [ ] Session activity during watcher initialization is eventually emitted
  - [ ] Late-arriving directories are adopted even when their files have old modification times
  - [ ] Initial discovery of pre-existing directories does not count as new activity
  - [ ] Watcher shutdown drains pending updates without emitting sessions merely because it stops
  - [ ] Watcher startup and shutdown acceptance cases each have a test
  - [ ] Watcher context created per start
- [ ] Session callbacks have panic recovery
- [ ] Goroutines are tracked with `wg.Go` only
- [ ] JSONL session files use `spi.ReadRecordLine` with `spi.MaxRecordLineSize` to cap memory allocation while reading each record and allow reading to continue after an oversized record
  - [ ] Oversized and malformed session records skipped with a Warn, not failing to read the entire session file
- [ ] Native ordering and branch selection preserved and tested where applicable
- [ ] Tool results identified and paired using native semantics

```text
## v2.15.1 2026-09-24

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Your answers to Codex CLI's `request_user_input` questions are now included in saved markdown. Previously the question and options were saved, but the selected option and any note were dropped, leaving an empty result. Each question is now shown with its options and your answer underneath, and questions you cancelled are marked as unanswered. Thanks to [daviddwlee84](https://github.com/daviddwlee84) for the detailed report and reproduction in [issue 333](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/issues/333).
- For Codex tools that SpecStory doesn't have a dedicated format for, the tool's arguments are now also shown as JSON. Previously they were lost whenever the tool also returned output.
- On Windows, `specstory run` and `specstory watch` no longer stop saving sessions partway through. Occasionally, when the agent created new session files while SpecStory was starting to watch a new directory, the file watcher could hang: no error was shown, and nothing more was saved to markdown or SpecStory Cloud until SpecStory was restarted. This could affect every supported agent.

## v2.15.0 2026-09-23
10:- You can resume a Cursor Cloud Agent session into another agent, and resume any agent's session into a Cursor Cloud Agent. Resuming a Cursor Cloud Agent session into Cursor Cloud reopens the same agent. Resuming any other session starts a new cloud agent, which is a new paid run, seeded with the session so far. Sessions over 1,000,000 characters are too large to resume into a Cursor Cloud Agent.
25:- OpenCode is a cross-provider `specstory resume` target: you can resume any agent's session into OpenCode, and resume an OpenCode session into another agent. OpenCode's free Zen models decline to continue a conversation that was not produced through Zen, so a resumed session needs another configured model to continue. Thanks to [marton78](https://github.com/marton78) for the original OpenCode provider contribution in [PR 156](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/156).
42:- Session names derived from a long first prompt are now shortened to 100 characters instead of 100 bytes. Prompts written without spaces, such as Chinese, no longer end in `��` replacement characters in `specstory list`, `specstory resume`, and SpecStory Cloud session titles.
49:- Grok is a cross-provider `specstory resume` target: you can resume any agent's session into Grok, and resume a Grok session into another agent.
68:- Selecting a session to resume now overrides conflicting resume flags in custom commands for Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Droid, Gemini, Antigravity, and DeepSeek TUI. Previously a configured session ID could take precedence over the session you selected.
69:- Cursor CLI live saving now picks up changes to existing sessions resumed outside SpecStory, rather than ignoring sessions that were already present when watching started. Reading a newly created session before its first message has been written no longer causes a crash.
72:- Sessions transferred into DeepSeek TUI with `specstory resume` are now discoverable by project. Previously their generated file layout could hide the workspace information from session discovery, leaving them out of subsequent listings and syncs.
78:- The SpecStory CLI now supports [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) (i.e., `qwen`) for sessions created from Qwen Code version `0.23.4` or higher. Sessions from earlier versions may work, but are not officially supported. This provides the same support for saving to local markdown files and to the SpecStory Cloud as for [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/docs/api/claude-code), [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli), [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/), Factory's [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli), [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/product), [Visual Studio Code Copilot](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/copilot), Google's [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/), [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI), [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/) and [Pi](https://pi.dev). Qwen Code sessions can also be resumed in other agents with `specstory resume`, and other agents' sessions can be resumed in Qwen Code. Thanks to [JinYang88](https://github.com/JinYang88) for the alternative Qwen Code provider in [PR 267](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/267), which informed clearer shell command transcripts that show the working directory and more consistent use of the shared session schema.
```

	return agent, nil

// Waiting for a new agent's first run. Cursor's agent page renders blank, and
// stays blank until reloaded, when it is opened while the run is still
// CREATING; the run leaves that state a few seconds after the launch. Variables
// so tests can shorten them.
var (
	runStartTimeout = 30 * time.Second
	runStartPoll    = time.Second
)

// waitForRunStart returns once the agent's first run has left CREATING, or
// after runStartTimeout. Opening the page late beats opening a blank one, and
// a failure here never stops the launch: the page is opened regardless.
func waitForRunStart(ctx context.Context, client *apiClient, agentID string) {
	log.UserMessage("Waiting for the Cursor Cloud Agent to start...\\n")
	deadline := time.Now().Add(runStartTimeout)
	for {
		runs, err := client.listRuns(ctx, agentID)
		if err != nil {
			slog.Warn("waitForRunStart: could not read the agent's runs; opening its page anyway", "agentID", agentID, "error", err)
			return
		}
		// A new agent has exactly one run.
		if len(runs) > 0 && runs[0].run.Status != "CREATING" {
			slog.Info("waitForRunStart: run started", "agentID", agentID, "status", runs[0].run.Status)
			return
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			slog.Warn("waitForRunStart: run still being created; opening its page anyway", "agentID", agentID, "timeout", runStartTimeout)
			return
		}
		if err := sleepContext(ctx, runStartPoll); err != nil {
			return
		}
	}
}'''

s=s.replace('\t"syscall"\n','\t"syscall"\n\t"time"\n',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

You're right to call that out. I had only confirmed the resume through the API: the run finished and the reply came back. I never loaded the page, so "works" was overstated.

Your refresh shows the agent itself was fine, with the right name, repo, prompt and reply. What was broken was opening the page too early. SpecStory opened the tab as soon as Cursor accepted the launch, while the run was still `CREATING`. The page apparently renders blank in that state and doesn't update until you reload.

## The fix

- **Wait before opening:** after launching an agent, SpecStory now prints "Waiting for the Cursor Cloud Agent to start...". It checks the run once a second, opens the page once the run has left `CREATING`, and watches. That covers both `run` and a resume that starts a copy.
- **Bounded:** after 30 seconds it opens the page anyway. A failed status check never blocks the launch.
- **No wait when reopening:** an existing agent is already past `CREATING`.
- **Test:** a new table test covers a run that has started, one that has finished, and one stuck in `CREATING` (it keeps checking until the timeout).
- **Docs:** the "Run" section of `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md` now describes the wait and why.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:06:02Z)**_

## What it does today

`spi.ResumedSessionTitle(slug)` returns the source session's slug, or "Resumed session" when the slug is empty. A slug is a filename fragment: the first four words of the first prompt, lowercased and hyphenated. So your Codex session became "tell-me-all-about" and the Claude one "hello-mr-claude-do".

## The proposed change

Pass the session itself, `ResumedSessionTitle(data *schema.SessionData)`, and pick the title in this order:

1. **`spi.ReadableTitleFromSessionData(data)`:** the first user prompt, whitespace-normalized and cut at a word boundary within 100 characters, for example "Tell me all about this repo…". This helper already exists. It's what titles a session in SpecStory Cloud today, and it matches how `list` and the resume picker name sessions locally. So the resumed copy would look like the original in every place SpecStory shows it.
2. **The slug**, when there's no user text.
3. **"Resumed session"**, as now.

## What it touches

- **Code:** the `spi` function and its test, plus the call sites in seven targets:
  - Cursor CLI, Cursor IDE (two sites), VS Code Copilot, Droid, DeepSeek TUI and OpenCode;
  - Cursor Cloud (two sites).
  
  Each call site goes from `data.Slug` to `data`. Grok stays as it is: it writes "Resumed session" in a step that never sees the session data, and it re-summarizes the session itself anyway.
- **Tests:** one `cursorcloud` test asserts the slug-based name, and `cursoride/database_test.go` probably does the same. Both need updating.
- **Changelog:** one bug-fix line.
- **Length:** Cursor's limit for agent names is far above 100 characters, so nothing gets rejected.

## A problem this turned up

For a Cursor Cloud session that SpecStory started (with `run`, or as a resume copy), the first user message is SpecStory's own opening prompt. `ReadableTitleFromSessionData` would title it "Session started by SpecStory. Don't read files or run any tools yet…".

That's not only a risk for this change. It's happening today: `session.go` uses the same helper for the SpecStory Cloud title, so every Cursor Cloud session started by `run` would show that greeting as its cloud title. I fixed the local title and slug in the provider, but not this shared path.

Options for fixing it:

| Option                        | Effect                                  |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| A. Flag the opening exchange  | Generic; every title helper can skip it |
| B. Drop it from SessionData   | Simple, but loses a real exchange       |
| C. Special-case the text      | Leaks provider knowledge into `spi`     |

- **A:** `cursorcloud` marks its opening exchange in the exchange metadata, for example `"specstoryPrompt": true`, and `firstUserMessageText` skips marked exchanges. That fixes the cloud title, the new resume title and any future use, and the exchange stays in the markdown.
- **B:** the greeting and the agent's reply would disappear from the saved session.
- **C:** `spi` would hard-code `cursorcloud`'s prompt text.

## Recommendation

Do the title change and option A together. They share the same helper, and A also fixes the cloud titles of sessions started by `run`. Want me to go ahead?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:07:59Z)**_

I'd use the exchange's `Metadata` map. It's already in the shared schema, it's free-form (`additionalProperties: true` in `session-data-v1.json`), and `cursorcloud` already writes `runId`, `status`, `branch` and `source` there.

**1. Name the flag once, in `pkg/spi/schema`,** so the provider that sets it and the helpers that read it share one constant:

```go
// MetadataOpenedBySpecStory marks an exchange whose prompt SpecStory sent to
// open a session (a greeting, or a transcript carried into a new agent), not
// one the user wrote. Titles skip it; the exchange is still rendered.
const MetadataOpenedBySpecStory = "openedBySpecStory"
```

**2. `cursorcloud` sets it** in `buildSessionData`, at the spot that already recognizes the greeting and resume prompts. Cursor's API has no field marking where a prompt came from, so recognizing it by text stays. The difference is that it's recognized once, and the result travels with the session data:

```go
if isSpecStoryPrompt(text) {
    exchange.Metadata[schema.MetadataOpenedBySpecStory] = true
}
```

**3. `spi.firstUserMessageText` skips flagged exchanges.** That fixes both `ReadableTitleFromSessionData` (the SpecStory Cloud title) and the new resume title.

Why this shape:

- **It survives the trip to SpecStory Cloud.** The `SessionData` blob is uploaded as-is, so a session resumed on another machine is titled correctly too.
- **Nothing is hidden.** The greeting and the agent's reply still appear in the markdown. Only title choice ignores them.
- **`spi` stays generic.** It knows "SpecStory opened this exchange", not anything about Cursor. Any provider whose agent SpecStory starts could set the same flag.
- **The provider's own title logic can use it too.** `cursorcloud`'s slug and name choice could check the flag instead of repeating the text match, so the text is matched in one place.

Two related choices are yours:

- **Flattening:** should `spi.FlattenSessionData` also skip flagged exchanges? When a Cursor Cloud session started by `run` is resumed into another agent, the greeting and "Hello! What would you like to work on?" are carried along as context. They're harmless but noise. My lean is to skip them, but it's a judgement call.
- **Sessions already in SpecStory Cloud:** they keep the greeting title until they're synced again. The flag changes `SessionData`, not the markdown, so whether a re-sync happens depends on the cloud's "only write when larger" rule. A session that gets a new run will re-sync anyway. For test sessions like ours I wouldn't worry about it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:08:27Z)**_

It would work, and it's simpler than the flag. I'd still pick the flag.

## Why it works

- **Titles fix themselves.** The schema lets an exchange contain only agent messages. If the opening prompt becomes thinking on an agent message, the exchange has no user message. `firstUserMessageText`, the SpecStory Cloud title, the resume title and `cursorcloud`'s own slug logic all move on to your real first prompt, with no flag and no `spi` change.
- **Markdown hides it.** Thinking renders as a collapsed "Thought Process" block, so the greeting and the resume transcript stop taking up the top of the file.
- **Prompt counts get more accurate.** `watch` and the stats count user messages, and you didn't write that prompt.

## Why I'd still use the flag

- **It records something that didn't happen.** The guide's "Honest data over convenient data" rule exists for exactly this. Thinking means the model's own reasoning. This text was a prompt SpecStory sent, as the user, and it was billed as input. Anything that reads `SessionData` later (cloud resume, search, a future feature) would take it as the agent's reasoning.
- **It blurs real thinking.** That run has its own thinking ("The user wants me to greet them…"). Both would sit in one agent message, and nothing would tell them apart.
- **The resume case gets odd.** A copied session's opening prompt is the whole earlier conversation, up to 1M characters. As thinking, your earlier session would appear as one huge thought by the new agent.
- **It's the same amount of detection.** Cursor's API still doesn't mark where a prompt came from, so `cursorcloud` recognizes it by text either way. The only difference is what it does next: set a flag, or rewrite the message.

## A middle ground

Keep it as thinking, but start the text with an explicit attribution, for example "SpecStory opened this session with:", followed by the prompt. Readers of the markdown wouldn't be misled. Anything reading `SessionData` still would, and real thinking is still mixed in.

My recommendation is the flag. It's one schema constant, one line in `cursorcloud`, and one check in `spi`. It fixes every title, and the session data stays accurate. Choose the thinking approach if collapsing the opening prompt in the markdown matters more to you than the data being accurate. You could also combine them: flag the exchange, and have the markdown renderer collapse flagged exchanges.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:08:58Z)**_

No. Whatever SpecStory sends, Cursor records it as the user's message.

The launch API (`POST /v1/agents`) gives only one place for our text: `prompt.text`, described as "Task instruction for the agent". The run stream then records it as `user-message-appended`. That's where `cursorcloud` reads the user turn, and Cursor's page shows it as your message bubble. The spec has no system-prompt or instructions field. The fields that look close don't fit:

| Field             | Why it doesn't help                                         |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `customSubagents` | Their system prompts reach the model only when it delegates |
| `envVars`         | Beta, 4,096 bytes per value, and only shell commands see it |
| `mode`            | Only switches between `agent` and `plan`                    |

A prompt can shape only the agent's reply. We could ask it to restate the context as thinking, but that adds to the run, not replaces anything. The user message is still there, so the title would still come from it, and we'd still need the flag.

So what Cursor sends back has to be fixed on our side, and the flag is still how I'd do it.

I did find something useful in the spec: `agentId`. The launch request accepts a client-chosen id in `bc-<uuid>` form, and "Re-POSTing the same `agentId` returns `409 agent_id_conflict` instead of creating a duplicate." That would make launches safe to retry:

- **Retries:** right now a launch is never resent after a 5xx or a dropped connection, because it might create a second paid agent. With our own `agentId`, a retry either creates the agent or gets a 409 meaning it already exists. Retrying after a blip becomes safe.
- **Resume:** `ReconstructSession` could pick the real agent id up front, instead of the `pending-<uuid>` placeholder.

The catch is that `agentId` "cannot be combined with `envVars`", and we don't use those. It's a separate change from the title work, so I'd only do it if you want it.
