_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:12:12Z)**_

The flag and the title change are both in and staged. Lint (v2.15.0) is clean, all tests pass, both builds succeed, and no golden files changed.

## Title change

- **New title rule:** `spi.ResumedSessionTitle` now takes the session data. It uses the first prompt you wrote, tidied up and cut at a word boundary within 100 characters. That's the same title `list` and SpecStory Cloud show. It falls back to the slug, then to "Resumed session". Your Codex session would now come back as "Tell me all about…" instead of "tell-me-all-about".
- **Every target agent that shows titles uses it:** Cursor CLI, Cursor IDE, VS Code Copilot, Droid, DeepSeek TUI, OpenCode and Cursor Cloud.
- **Grok** still writes "Resumed session", because it writes that summary before the session data is available. There's a comment saying why.

## The flag

- **The constant:** `schema.MetadataOpenedBySpecStory` (`"openedBySpecStory": true`), stored in the exchange's existing free-form metadata.
- **Where it's set:** `cursorcloud` sets it on the `run` greeting and on a resume copy's transcript exchange, in the one place it already recognized them.
- **Where it's read:** `spi`'s first-prompt lookup skips flagged exchanges. That fixes three titles at once:
  - SpecStory Cloud no longer titles a session started by `run` with "Session started by SpecStory. Don't read files…";
  - a resumed session's title skips the greeting;
  - `cursorcloud`'s own title and slug do too.
- **Nothing hidden:** the exchange still appears in the markdown.

## Tests

- **New table test for `ResumedSessionTitle`:**
  - no session;
  - a first prompt, with whitespace tidied;
  - a flagged opening exchange skipped;
  - only a flagged exchange, falling back to the slug;
  - no prompt text, falling back to the slug;
  - a blank slug.
- **`cursorcloud` greeting test:** now checks that the greeting exchange is flagged, that your own exchange isn't, and that the SpecStory Cloud title is your prompt.
- **Updated expectations:** four provider tests that expected the slug title now expect the first prompt, written out as literals.

## Docs

- **Changelog:** the bug-fix bullet now covers the whole change. Resumed sessions are titled with the original first prompt; before, they got the slug, or "Resumed session" for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Pi.
- **`NEW-PROVIDER-GUIDE.md`:** the slug rule now explains that the slug is only the fallback. A new rule says a provider must flag any exchange SpecStory opened.
- **`CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md`:** documents the flag.

As agreed, I didn't change flattening: when a Cursor Cloud session started by `run` is resumed into another agent, the greeting is still carried along as context.

```
Title resumed sessions with the original first prompt; flag exchanges SpecStory opened so titles skip them
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:14:35Z)**_

As written, it doesn't. I worded it as a rule for every provider, but only one kind of provider ever has an exchange SpecStory opened.

- **Local agents:** SpecStory starts the agent's own program, and the user types the first prompt. SpecStory never sends a prompt of its own, so there's nothing to flag.
- **Resume into a local agent:** the reconstructed file holds the original conversation's turns. When that file is read back, its first user message is the original prompt, so titles are already right. The migration note is an agent turn, not a user one.
- **Cursor Cloud:** there's no local program, so SpecStory has to create the agent through the API, and the API won't create one without a prompt. That greeting (or a resume transcript) is the only case.

For almost every provider author, the guide line describes a situation they'll never be in.

Options:

1. **Drop it from the guide.** The flag stays documented where it's used: the constant's comment in `schema`, and `CURSOR-CLOUD-FORMAT.md`. The tradeoff is that the next hosted-agent provider wouldn't learn about it from the guide.
2. **Make it conditional and move it to "Run and exec".** That section already covers how `run` starts each kind of agent. One sentence would do: "A provider whose `run` or `resume` has to start the agent with a prompt SpecStory writes (a hosted agent with no local process, for example) flags that exchange with `schema.MetadataOpenedBySpecStory`, so titles skip it."

I recommend option 2. It only speaks to providers in that situation, and it sits where an author working on `run` will read it. Either way, I'd also drop the matching line from the "Honest data" list. Which do you want?

```text
### Run and exec

- Honor the custom command from `-c` and `<id>_cmd`; parse it with `spi.SplitCommandLine`.
- When a resume id is requested it wins over any id pinned in the configured command. Use `spi.EnsureResumeFlagArgs` for flag-style resume (`--resume <id>`), passing the agent's supported flag names. It replaces pinned ids, fills bare or empty flags, and preserves the caller's slice.
- Stop the watcher and join in-flight saves before returning the agent's exit status.
- For an IDE provider, `run` opens the project directory with the IDE's own CLI, canonicalizing the path first, prints install guidance if that CLI is missing, waits for the IDE to create the workspace, and then watches until Ctrl-C. No silent fallback to opening the app on its home screen.
- For a hosted agent, `run` opens the agent's web surface with the configured `<id>_cmd` (default: the operating system's URL opener), prints one line saying so, and then behaves as `watch` until Ctrl-C. Say so in the README row and in the config template comment for `<id>_cmd`.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:48:05Z)**_

## What went wrong

Slack rejected the message. The release run log shows the webhook replied `invalid_attachments`.

- **The cause:** a Slack `section` block holds at most 3,000 characters, and the workflow puts the entire changelog into one block. The v2.16.0 text is 3,140 characters. v2.15.1 was 1,122 and v2.15.0 was 2,644, which is why those worked. The Cursor Cloud Agent announcement bullets pushed this release over.
- **Why the run was still green:** the Slack step (`release.yml:110`) calls `curl` without `--fail`. Slack answered with an error, `curl` exited 0, and the step passed.

The release itself is fine: goreleaser, the GitHub release notes and the Homebrew job all succeeded. Only the Slack post is missing.

## Fix options

| Option                       | Content in Slack     | Effort |
|------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| 1. Split into several blocks | Full changelog       | Small  |
| 2. Truncate with a link      | ~2,900 chars + link  | Small  |

1. **Split into several blocks** (recommended). Break the changelog into `section` blocks at line boundaries, each under 3,000 characters. Slack allows 50 blocks per message, so nothing is cut. It's a few lines of `jq` in the same step.
2. **Truncate with a link.** Cut the text near 2,900 characters and end with "… full notes:" plus a link to the GitHub release. It's simpler, but the post loses the end of the changelog.

Either way, I'd also make the failure visible: use `curl --fail-with-body`, and set `continue-on-error: true` on that step. The step would then show as failed with Slack's error, without failing the job. That matters because `update-homebrew-tap` depends on this job, and a Slack hiccup shouldn't block the Homebrew update.

## For v2.16.0 now

Re-running the release job would re-run goreleaser against an existing release, so I wouldn't do that. Two options:

- I give you the message text to paste into #specstory-clients.
- I also add a `workflow_dispatch` trigger to a small notify-only job, which could re-send any version's notes later.

Want me to go with option 1, the visible failure, and the notify-only job? Or just option 1, with you posting v2.16.0 by hand?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:48:46Z)**_

Confirmed. The extra entry is a leftover **draft** from v2.15.0, and GitHub always lists drafts at the top.

| Release id  | State     | Created          | Notes                               |
|-------------|-----------|------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `394679127` | Published | 2026-09-23 13:04 | The real v2.15.0, our changelog     |
| `394679198` | Draft     | 2026-09-23 13:17 | goreleaser's default commit list    |

It came from the duplicate release run that day. Two runs of `release.yml` started for the `specstory-cli/v2.15.0` tag in the same second. One published the real release. The other's goreleaser step failed partway, after it had created a second release as a draft and uploaded the 11 assets. That run's Homebrew job was skipped, and nothing cleaned up the draft.

It's harmless: a draft is only visible to repo maintainers, and the real v2.15.0 and v2.16.0 are correct. It just sorts first in the list.

To fix it:

1. **Delete the draft** (`DELETE /repos/specstoryai/getspecstory/releases/394679198`). That removes only the draft and its duplicate assets. The `v2.15.0` tag and the published release stay. I'd delete it by id rather than with `gh release delete v2.15.0`, which could hit the wrong one since both share the tag.
2. **Prevent it in `release.yml`:** add `concurrency: { group: release-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: false }`. A second run for the same tag would then wait for the first, then fail cleanly when it finds the release already exists, instead of racing to create one.

Deleting a release on GitHub can't be undone, so I'll wait for a yes. Want me to delete draft `394679198`? And should I add the concurrency guard alongside the Slack fix?

```bash
              def sections($max):

                | reduce .[] as $line ([""];
                    if (.[-1] | length) > 0 and (.[-1] | length) + 1 + ($line | length) > $max
                    then . + [$line]
                    else .[-1] = (if .[-1] == "" then $line else .[-1] + "\\n" + $line end)

                    color: "#e35a2c",
                    blocks: (
                      [ { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": $title } } ]
                      + [ $text | sections(2900)[] | { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": . } } ]
                    )
                  }
                ]
              }' > payload.json'''
assert s.count(old)==1
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-18 15:53:31Z)**_

The URL lives in Slack's app configuration, not the regular Slack app. Which page depends on how the bot was set up, so try these in order.

**1. A Slack app (most likely)**

1. Go to https://api.slack.com/apps and sign in to the SpecStory workspace if asked.
2. Under "Your Apps", open the app behind **SpecStory Release Bot**. It may have a slightly different name.
3. In the left sidebar under **Features**, click **Incoming Webhooks**.
4. Scroll to **Webhook URLs for Your Workspace** and find the row whose channel is **#specstory-clients**.
5. Click **Copy** on that row. The URL looks like `https://hooks.slack.com/services/T…/B…/…`.

If the app isn't listed under "Your Apps", you aren't one of its collaborators. Whoever created it can add you from the app's **Collaborators** page, or copy the URL for you.

**2. A legacy "Incoming WebHooks" integration**

The workflow sets its own bot name and icon, which older custom integrations allow, so it might be one of those:

1. Go to `https://<your-workspace>.slack.com/apps/manage/custom-integrations`.
2. Click **Incoming WebHooks**.
3. Find the configuration posting to **#specstory-clients**, click the pencil (edit) icon, and copy the **Webhook URL**.

**If you can't find it either way:** in Slack, open #specstory-clients, click the channel name, then the **Integrations** tab. It lists the apps that post there, including the Release Bot, and shows who added it. That person can get you the URL.

Once it's copied, run the `curl` command from my last message.

     - Other endpoints: `/runs/{runId}/cancel`, `/unarchive`, `DELETE /v1/agents/{id}`.
     - There is no prompt maxLength, and no system-prompt field.
     - `agentId` is a client-supplied id: re-POSTing it returns 409. It cannot be combined with `envVars`. (Noted only, not implemented.)
   - **Agent page:** the cursor.com agent page renders blank while the run is CREATING, so SpecStory waits until the run leaves CREATING.
   - **Retries:** POST retries only 429; GET also retries 5xx and transport errors (avoids duplicate paid agents).
   - **Resume as a pending launch:** `ReconstructSession` returns `pending-<uuid>` with JSON content (`sourceAgentId`, `name`, `prompt`) stored in the mirror's `pending/`. `ExecAgentAndWatch` reads and deletes it, then reopens the same agent (if it exists on the project's repo; archived agents are unarchived) or launches a copy.
   - **Size limit:** `maxResumePromptChars = 1_000_000`.
   - **Opening-exchange flag:** `schema.MetadataOpenedBySpecStory = "openedBySpecStory"` in `Exchange.Metadata`. `spi.firstUserMessageText` skips flagged exchanges, which fixes the cloud title (`ReadableTitleFromSessionData`) and resume titles.
   - **Resume titles:** `spi.ResumedSessionTitle(data *schema.SessionData)` returns the readable first prompt, else the slug, else "Resumed session".
   - **Picker note:** the optional `spi.ResumeTargetNoter` interface (`ResumeTargetNote(sourceAgent string) string`) shows "(starts a new paid cloud run)".
   - **Slack:** a section block's text is limited to 3000 chars, and the error is `invalid_attachments`. `curl` without `--fail` hides the error.
   - **Lint:** golangci-lint v2.15.0 via `go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.15.0 run`.
